sentences.zh: 陳德榮芮复傳蔣林閻堯熙王時翔藍鼎元葉新施昭庭陳慶門週人龍童華黃世發李渭謝仲坃李大本牛運震張甄陶邵大業周克開汪輝祖劉大紳吳煥彩紀大奎邵希曾}}=陳德榮=陳德榮，字廷彥，直隸安州人。

translations.literal: Chen Derong, Rui Fuchuan biography, Jiang Lin, Yan Yaoxi, Wang Shixiang, Lan Dingyuan, Ye Xin, Shi Zhaoting, Chen Qingmen, Zhou Renlong, Tong Hua, Huang Shifa, Li Wei, Xie Zhongxun, Li Daben, Niu Yunzhen, Zhang Zhentao, Shao Daye, Zhou Kekai, Wang Huizu, Liu Dashen, Wu Huancai, Ji Dakui, Shao Xiceng. Chen Derong. Chen Derong, courtesy name Tingyan, was a native of Anzhou in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Derong, Rui Fuchuan, Jiang Lin, Yan Yaoxi, Wang Shixiang, Lan Dingyuan, Ye Xin, Shi Zhaoting, Chen Qingmen, Zhou Renlong, Tong Hua, Huang Shifa, Li Wei, Xie Zhongxun, Li Daben, Niu Yunzhen, Zhang Zhentao, Shao Daye, Zhou Kekai, Wang Huizu, Liu Dashen, Wu Huancai, Ji Dakui, and Shao Xiceng. Chen Derong, courtesy name Tingyan, was from Anzhou in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十一年進士，授湖北枝江知縣。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year of Kangxi he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Zhijiang in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifty-first year of the Kangxi reign (1712) and was appointed magistrate of Zhijiang in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 修百里洲堤，除轉餉雜派。

translations.literal: He repaired the dike on Bailizhou and abolished miscellaneous levies for transport rations.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired the dike at Bailizhou and abolished the miscellaneous surcharges levied for transport rations.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年，遷貴州黔西知州，父憂歸。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongzheng he was transferred to be prefect of Qianxi in Guizhou, then returned home upon his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Yongzheng reign (1725) he was transferred to serve as prefect of Qianxi in Guizhou, but returned home when his father died.

sentences.zh: 服闋，署威寧府。

translations.literal: When his mourning period ended, he served as acting prefect of Weining Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period ended, he served as acting prefect of Weining.

sentences.zh: 未幾，威寧改州，補大定知府。

translations.literal: Before long Weining was changed to a subprefecture, and he was appointed prefect of Dading.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Weining was reduced from a prefecture to a subprefecture, and he was appointed prefect of Dading.

sentences.zh: 烏蒙土司叛，東川、鎮雄附之，德榮赴威寧防守。

translations.literal: The native-official chieftain of Wumeng rebelled; Dongchuan and Zhenxiong joined him, and Derong went to Weining to organize the defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the native chieftain of Wumeng rebelled and Dongchuan and Zhenxiong sided with him, Derong went to Weining to organize the defense.

sentences.zh: 城陴頹圮，倉猝聚米桶，實土石，比次甃​​築，墉堞屹然。

translations.literal: The city walls were crumbling; in haste he gathered rice buckets, filled them with earth and stone, and built them up in succession with brick facing, so that the battlements stood firm.
translations.idiomatic: The walls were crumbling; in haste he had rice buckets filled with earth and stone and built up in courses with brick facing, until the battlements stood firm again.

sentences.zh: 賊焚牛衛鎮，去城三十里，德榮日夜備戰，賊不敢逼。

translations.literal: The bandits burned Niugwei Town, thirty li from the city; Derong made ready for battle day and night, and the bandits did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels burned Niugwei Town, thirty li from the city; Derong prepared for battle day and night, and the rebels did not dare approach.

sentences.zh: 總兵哈元生援至，賊敗走。

translations.literal: Regional commander Ha Yuansheng arrived with reinforcements, and the bandits were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Ha Yuansheng arrived with reinforcements, and the rebels were defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 尋以母憂去官。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he left office on account of his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，授江西廣饒九南道。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed intendant of the Guangrao-Jiunan circuit in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, he was appointed intendant of the Guangrao–Jiunan circuit in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 九江、大孤兩關錮弊盡革之。

translations.literal: He thoroughly abolished all corrupt practices at the Jiujiang and Dagu passes.
translations.idiomatic: He thoroughly rooted out corrupt practices at the Jiujiang and Dagu passes.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，經略張廣泗疏薦，擢貴州按察使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, Grand Coordinator Zhang Guangsi memorialized recommending him, and he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qianlong reign (1736), Grand Coordinator Zhang Guangsi recommended him in a memorial, and he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 時群苗交煽，軍事方殷，古州姑盧硃洪文諸叛案，德​​榮治鞫，詳慎重輕，咸稱其情，眾心始安。

translations.literal: At that time the Miao were inciting one another in rebellion and military affairs were pressing; in the cases of rebellion at Guzhou, Gulu, Zhu, Hongwen, and others, Derong conducted investigations and trials with careful attention to severity and leniency; all praised his fairness, and public sentiment began to settle.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Miao were stirring one another to rebellion and military affairs were urgent; in the rebellion cases at Guzhou, Gulu, Zhu, Hongwen, and elsewhere, Derong conducted trials with careful attention to severity and leniency. All praised his fairness, and public sentiment began to calm.

sentences.zh: 及苗疆漸定，駐師與屯將吏多以刻急見能。

translations.literal: As the Miao frontier gradually stabilized, the stationed troops and colonizing officers and officials mostly sought to display ability through harsh severity.
translations.idiomatic: As the Miao frontier gradually settled, the garrison troops and colonizing officers mostly sought to prove their worth through harsh severity.

sentences.zh: 二年，貴陽大火，德榮謁經略曰：「天意如此，當竭誠修省，苗亦人類，曷可盡殺？

translations.literal: In the second year a great fire broke out in Guiyang; Derong called on the grand coordinator and said: "Heaven's will is thus—we should devote ourselves in sincerity to self-examination. The Miao are also human—how can we slaughter them all?"
translations.idiomatic: In the second year a great fire broke out in Guiyang. Derong called on the grand coordinator and said, "When Heaven shows its will in this way, we should devote ourselves sincerely to self-examination. The Miao are human beings too—how can we slaughter them all?"

sentences.zh: 」廣泗感動，戒將吏如德榮言。

translations.literal: Guangsi was moved, and warned the officers and officials as Derong had said.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi was moved and warned his officers and officials to heed Derong's words.

sentences.zh: 四年，署布政使，疏言：「黔地山多水足，可以疏土成田。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, acting as financial commissioner, he memorialized stating: "Guizhou has many mountains and abundant water, by which poor soil may be turned into fields."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, while serving as acting financial commissioner, he memorialized: "Guizhou has many mountains and ample water; poor soil can be turned into farmland."

sentences.zh: 小民難於工本，不能變瘠為腴。

translations.literal: The common people find it hard to bear the cost of labor and cannot turn barren land into fertile.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary people cannot afford the cost of labor and cannot turn barren land into fertile fields.

sentences.zh: 山荒尤多，流民思墾，輒見撓阻。

translations.literal: Waste mountains are especially numerous; wandering people wish to open land but are always obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: Waste mountains are especially numerous; displaced people who wish to reclaim land are constantly obstructed.

sentences.zh: 桑條肥沃，亦不知蠶繅之法。

translations.literal: The mulberry branches are fertile, yet they do not know methods of sericulture and reeling.
translations.idiomatic: Mulberry grows abundantly, yet the people do not know how to raise silkworms or reel silk.

sentences.zh: 自非牧民者經營而勸率之，利不可得而興也。

translations.literal: Unless those who shepherd the people undertake to plan and lead them, benefits cannot be raised up.
translations.idiomatic: Unless those who govern the people plan and lead them, these benefits cannot be realized.

sentences.zh: 今就鄰省僱募種棉、織布、飼蠶、紡績之人，擇地試種，設局教習，轉相仿效，可以有成。

translations.literal: Now hire from neighboring provinces people skilled in planting cotton, weaving cloth, raising silkworms, and spinning, choose land to try planting, establish bureaus to teach and practice, and with mutual imitation it can succeed.
translations.idiomatic: We should hire from neighboring provinces people skilled in planting cotton, weaving cloth, raising silkworms, and spinning; choose land for trial planting; establish bureaus for instruction; and through mutual imitation success can be achieved.

sentences.zh: 應責各道因地制宜，隨時設教。

translations.literal: Each circuit should be charged to suit local conditions and establish instruction as circumstances permit.
translations.idiomatic: Each circuit should be charged to adapt to local conditions and provide instruction as circumstances allow.

sentences.zh: 一年必有規模，三年漸期成效。

translations.literal: In one year there must be a pattern; in three years results may gradually be expected.
translations.idiomatic: Within one year there should be a framework in place; within three years results may gradually be expected.

sentences.zh: 」詔允行。

translations.literal: The edict approved implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 乃給工本，築壩堰，引山泉，治水田，導以蓄洩之法。

translations.literal: He then supplied working capital, built dams and sluices, led in mountain springs, managed paddy fields, and guided them in methods of storage and release.
translations.idiomatic: He then supplied working capital, built dams and sluices, channeled mountain springs, developed paddy fields, and taught the people methods of storage and drainage.

sentences.zh: 官署自育蠶，於省城大興寺繅絲織作，使民知其利。

translations.literal: In the official residence they raised silkworms themselves; at Daxing Temple in the provincial capital they reeled silk and wove, so the people would know the profit.
translations.idiomatic: The yamen itself raised silkworms; at Daxing Temple in the provincial capital they reeled silk and wove cloth, so the people would see the profit in it.

sentences.zh: 六年，疏陳課民樹杉，得六萬株。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he memorialized reporting instruction to the people to plant fir, obtaining sixty thousand trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he reported that the people had been instructed to plant fir trees, yielding sixty thousand saplings.

sentences.zh: 七年，貴築、貴陽、開州、威寧、餘慶、施秉諸州、縣報墾田至三萬六千畝。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Guizhu, Guiyang, Kaizhou, Weining, Yuqing, Shibing, and other prefectures and counties reported reclaimed fields reaching thirty-six thousand mu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the prefectures and counties of Guizhu, Guiyang, Kaizhou, Weining, Yuqing, Shibing, and elsewhere reported thirty-six thousand mu of newly reclaimed land.

sentences.zh: 開野蠶山場百餘所，比戶機杼相聞。

translations.literal: They opened more than a hundred mountain fields for wild silkworms; in every household the sound of looms was heard.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred wild-silkworm mountain sites were opened, and the sound of looms was heard in every household.

sentences.zh: 德榮據以入告，數被溫旨嘉獎。

translations.literal: Derong reported these matters upward and several times received warm edicts of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Derong reported these achievements to the throne and several times received warm edicts of commendation.

sentences.zh: 又大修城郭、壇廟、學舍。

translations.literal: He also extensively repaired city walls, altars and temples, and school buildings.
translations.idiomatic: He also undertook major repairs of city walls, altars, temples, and school buildings.

sentences.zh: 廣置棲流所，收行旅之病者。

translations.literal: He broadly established shelters for vagrants to take in sick travelers on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He established many shelters for vagrants to take in sick travelers on the road.

sentences.zh: 益囚糧。

translations.literal: He increased grain rations for prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: He increased the grain rations for prisoners.

sentences.zh: 冬寒，卹老疾嫠孤之無衣者。

translations.literal: In winter's cold he gave relief to the old and sick, widows and orphans who lacked clothing.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter cold he provided clothing for the aged and infirm, widows, and orphans who had none.

sentences.zh: 親課諸生，勗以為己之學。

translations.literal: He personally examined the students and exhorted them with learning for one's own sake.
translations.idiomatic: He personally examined the students and exhorted them to study for their own sake.

sentences.zh: 設義學二十四於苗疆，風氣丕變。

translations.literal: He established twenty-four charity schools in the Miao frontier, and custom greatly changed.
translations.idiomatic: He established twenty-four charity schools in the Miao frontier, and local customs were greatly transformed.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遷安徽布政使，賑鳳、潁水災，流移獲安。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to be financial commissioner of Anhui, relieving famine from floods in Fengyang and Yingzhou; the displaced obtained peace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was transferred to financial commissioner of Anhui, where he relieved flood victims in Fengyang and Yingzhou; the displaced found security.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 德榮在貴州興蠶桑，為百世之利。

translations.literal: Derong's promotion of sericulture in Guizhou was a benefit for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Derong's promotion of sericulture in Guizhou was a benefit for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 時遵義知府陳玉畐，山東歷城人，到郡見多檞樹，土人取為薪炭。

translations.literal: At that time Chen Yubi, prefect of Zunyi, a native of Licheng in Shandong, on reaching the prefecture saw many oak trees that the local people used for fuel and charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chen Yubi, prefect of Zunyi and a native of Licheng in Shandong, on arriving at his post saw many oak trees that the locals used only for fuel and charcoal.

sentences.zh: 玉畐曰：「此青萊樹也，吾得以富吾民矣。

translations.literal: Yubi said: "These are qinglai trees—I can enrich my people with them."
translations.idiomatic: Yubi said, "These are qinglai trees—I can use them to enrich my people."

sentences.zh: 」乃購歷城山蠶種，兼以蠶師來，試育五年，而蠶大熟，獲繭八百萬，自是遵綢之名大著。

translations.literal: He then purchased mountain silkworm eggs from Licheng and brought silk masters as well; after five years of trial raising the silkworms matured fully, obtaining eight million cocoons; from then the fame of Zunchou silk became great.
translations.idiomatic: He then purchased mountain silkworm eggs from Licheng and brought silk masters with them; after five years of trial cultivation the silkworms matured fully and eight million cocoons were obtained, and from then on the fame of Zunyi silk spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 正安州吏目徐階平，亦自浙江購繭種，仿玉畐行之正安，亦大食其利。

translations.literal: Xu Jieping, petty official of Zheng'an Subprefecture, also purchased cocoon eggs from Zhejiang and imitated Yubi's method in Zheng'an, likewise greatly profiting.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jieping, a petty official of Zheng'an Subprefecture, also purchased cocoon eggs from Zhejiang and followed Yubi's method in Zheng'an, likewise reaping great profit.

sentences.zh: 遵義鄭珍著樗繭譜，以傳玉畐遺法。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhen of Zunyi wrote the Chumu Can Spectrum to transmit Yubi's surviving method.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhen of Zunyi wrote the Chumu Canpu to preserve Yubi's methods for posterity.

sentences.zh: =芮复傳=芮复傳，字衣亭，順天寶坻人，原籍江蘇溧陽。

translations.literal: Rui Fuchuan. Rui Fuchuan, courtesy name Yiting, was a native of Baodi in Shuntian, with original household registration in Liyang, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Rui Fuchuan, courtesy name Yiting, was a native of Baodi in Shuntian; his original household registration was in Liyang, Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十八年進士，授浙江錢塘知縣。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year of Kangxi he passed the jinshi and was appointed magistrate of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the forty-eighth year of the Kangxi reign (1709) and was appointed magistrate of Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 悉除諸無名錢，曰：「官足給饔飧而已。

translations.literal: He abolished all nameless fees entirely, saying: "For an official, enough to supply one's meals is sufficient."
translations.idiomatic: He abolished all unauthorized levies, saying, "An official needs only enough to supply his meals."

sentences.zh: 」有金三者，交通上官署，為奸利，立逮杖斃之，一時大快。

translations.literal: There was one Jin San who colluded with the higher yamen and profited by malice; he immediately had him arrested and beaten to death with the stick, to universal delight.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Jin San who colluded with the higher yamen for illicit profit; Fuchuan had him arrested at once and beaten to death with the stick, to universal delight.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，大旱，复傳勘實上狀，上官欲寢之，固爭曰：「律有捏災、匿災並當劾，某今日請受捏災罪。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year there was a great drought; Fuchuan investigated truthfully and submitted a report upward; his superior wished to suppress it; he firmly protested: "The law provides that fabricating disaster and concealing disaster are both subject to impeachment; today I ask to receive the crime of fabricating disaster."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year a severe drought struck; Fuchuan investigated and reported the facts, but his superior wished to suppress the report. He protested firmly: "The law punishes both fabricating disasters and concealing them; today I ask to be charged with fabricating a disaster."

sentences.zh: 」時同城仁和民千人，跣走圍署，曰：「錢塘為民父母，仁和獨不父母我耶？

translations.literal: At that time a thousand people from neighboring Renhe county, barefoot, ran and surrounded the yamen, saying: "Qiantang is parent to the people—does Renhe alone not parent us?"
translations.idiomatic: At that time a thousand people from neighboring Renhe County, barefoot, ran to surround the yamen, crying, "Qiantang is parent to its people—does Renhe alone refuse to parent us?"

sentences.zh: 」上官感動，竟以災聞。

translations.literal: The superior was moved and in the end reported the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The superior was moved and in the end reported the disaster to the court.

sentences.zh: 開倉行賑，复傳設粥廠二十有七。

translations.literal: They opened the granaries and carried out relief; Fuchuan established twenty-seven gruel kitchens.
translations.idiomatic: The granaries were opened for relief, and Fuchuan established twenty-seven gruel kitchens.

sentences.zh: 微行覘視，治胥吏之侵擾者，帑不費而賑溥。

translations.literal: Making unannounced rounds to observe, he punished yamen runners who harassed; the treasury was not wasted yet relief was broad.
translations.idiomatic: Making unannounced inspections, he punished yamen clerks who harassed the people; the treasury was not wasted, yet relief reached many.

sentences.zh: 駐防營卒馳躪民田，便宜懲治，輒縛而鞭之。

translations.literal: Garrison soldiers galloped across the people's fields; he punished them on the spot by binding and flogging.
translations.idiomatic: When garrison soldiers galloped across the people's fields, he punished them on the spot by binding and flogging them.

sentences.zh: 治績上聞，世宗特召引見，擢溫州知府。

translations.literal: His administrative achievements were reported upward; the Yongzheng Emperor specially summoned him for an audience and promoted him to prefect of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his achievements were reported to the throne, the Yongzheng Emperor specially summoned him for an audience and promoted him to prefect of Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 故事，貢柑，歲期至。

translations.literal: By precedent, tangerines were presented as tribute each year when the season came.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, tangerines were presented as tribute when the season arrived each year.

sentences.zh: 織造封園，民以為累。

translations.literal: The weaving manufacture sealed off orchards, and the people considered it a burden.
translations.idiomatic: The weaving manufacture sealed off the orchards, and the people regarded it as a burden.

sentences.zh: 复傳第取足供貢，不使擾民。

translations.literal: Fuchuan took only enough to supply the tribute and would not let the people be disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchuan took only enough to meet the tribute quota and would not disturb the people further.

sentences.zh: 府境私鹽充斥，設三團，集灶戶，平其直，私販息，官鹽不督自行。

translations.literal: Private salt filled the prefecture's territory; he established three groups, gathered salt-makers, leveled prices, private trafficking ceased, and official salt sold without compulsion.
translations.idiomatic: Private salt was rampant in the prefecture; he established three cooperatives, gathered salt-makers, stabilized prices, private trafficking ceased, and official salt sold without coercion.

sentences.zh: 天台山東南有山曰玉環，在海中，總督李衛欲開田設治，檄复傳往勘，以徒費無益，陳請罷之。

translations.literal: Southeast of Tiantai Mountain there is a mountain called Yuhuan, in the sea; Governor-General Li Wei wished to open fields and establish administration; he ordered Fuchuan to go survey; stating it would waste effort without benefit, he memorialized requesting cancellation.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast of Tiantai Mountain lies Yuhuan Island, in the sea. Governor-General Li Wei wished to open fields and establish an administration there and ordered Fuchuan to survey the site; Fuchuan reported that the project would waste resources without benefit and memorialized requesting its cancellation.

sentences.zh: 衛怒，檄他吏往，意必行。

translations.literal: Wei was angry and ordered another official to go, determined it must proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was furious and sent another official instead, determined to proceed.

sentences.zh: 時山中田僅二萬畝，乃割天台、樂清兩縣民田隸玉環，經費不足，則捐通省官俸，又加關津一切雜稅以給之。

translations.literal: At that time cultivated land in the mountains was only twenty thousand mu; they then cut off fields from Tiantai and Yueqing counties to attach to Yuhuan; when funds were insufficient they donated salaries of officials throughout the province, and added all miscellaneous taxes at passes and fords to supply it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time only twenty thousand mu of land on the island could be cultivated; fields were then carved from Tiantai and Yueqing counties and attached to Yuhuan. When funds proved insufficient, officials throughout the province donated their salaries, and every miscellaneous tax at passes and fords was added to support the project.

sentences.zh: 弛山禁，漁者往來並稅，曰塗稅。

translations.literal: They relaxed the mountain prohibition; fishermen coming and going were all taxed, called "path tax."
translations.idiomatic: The mountain prohibition was relaxed, and fishermen traveling back and forth were all taxed—this was called the "path tax."

sentences.zh: 既而漁者不入，山者度關納稅，亦徵其塗稅。

translations.literal: Later fishermen did not enter; mountain people crossing passes paid tax, and were also levied the path tax.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when fishermen no longer came, mountain people crossing the passes paid tax and were also charged the path tax.

sentences.zh: 复傳爭曰「是重稅也」，是牘凡七上。

translations.literal: Fuchuan protested saying "this is double taxation"; such memorials went up seven times in all.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchuan protested, "This is double taxation," and submitted such memorials seven times in all.

sentences.zh: 衛益怒，以為阻撓玉環墾田事，蜚語頗聞。

translations.literal: Wei grew still angrier, holding that he was obstructing Yuhuan land reclamation; slanderous words were widely heard.
translations.idiomatic: Wei grew still angrier, accusing him of obstructing the Yuhuan land-reclamation project, and slanderous rumors spread.

sentences.zh: 劉統勳奉使視海塘，過溫州，語之曰：「君與李宮保，兩雄不相下，不移不屈，君之謂乎？

translations.literal: Liu Tongxun, on imperial mission to inspect the seawall, passing Wenzhou said to him: "You and Lord Li are two heroes who will not yield—'if you do not move, you will not bend'—is that your saying?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tongxun, on an imperial mission to inspect the seawall, passed through Wenzhou and said to him, "You and Lord Li are two heroes who will not yield to each other—'if you do not move, you will not bend'—does that describe you?"

sentences.zh: 尋擢溫處道。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Wenzhou-Taizhou circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to intendant of the Wenzhou–Taizhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 會銅商積弊敗露，复傳持法，又揭劾知府尹士份不職，士份反誣以阻商誤銅，大吏故嫉之，遂並劾复傳。

translations.literal: When accumulated abuses of the copper merchants were exposed, Fuchuan upheld the law and also impeached Prefect Yin Shifen for incompetence; Shifen in turn slandered him for obstructing merchants and delaying copper; the grand coordinators deliberately envied him and jointly impeached Fuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: When long-standing abuses among the copper merchants came to light, Fuchuan upheld the law and also impeached Prefect Yin Shifen for incompetence. Shifen retaliated by accusing him of obstructing merchants and delaying copper shipments; the senior officials, who already resented him, jointly impeached Fuchuan as well.

sentences.zh: 解任，總督趙弘恩質訊，坐失察關吏舞弊奪職。

translations.literal: He was relieved of office; Governor-General Zhao Hong'en conducted an inquiry and, convicted of failure to investigate customs officials' malfeasance, his post was taken.
translations.idiomatic: He was relieved of office; Governor-General Zhao Hong'en conducted an inquiry and stripped him of his post for failing to detect malfeasance among customs officials.

sentences.zh: 會高宗登極，詔仍留浙江辦銅，事竣，例得復官，以親喪歸，遂不出。

translations.literal: When Gaozong ascended the throne, an edict had him remain in Zhejiang to handle copper; when the affair concluded, by precedent he could recover his post, but he returned home on account of his parent's death and did not reenter office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianlong Emperor ascended the throne, an edict ordered him to remain in Zhejiang to handle copper affairs. When the work was finished, by precedent he could have been restored to office, but he returned home upon a parent's death and never served again.

sentences.zh: 家居三十餘年，卒，年九十有四。

translations.literal: At home for more than thirty years, he died at age ninety-four.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home for more than thirty years and died at the age of ninety-four.

sentences.zh: =蔣林=蔣林，字元楚，廣西全州人。

translations.literal: Jiang Lin. Jiang Lin, courtesy name Yuanchu, was a native of Quanzhou in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Lin, courtesy name Yuanchu, was a native of Quanzhou in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十四年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year of Kangxi he passed the jinshi, was selected a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifty-fourth year of the Kangxi reign (1715), was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 直南書房，十年不遷。

translations.literal: He served in the Southern Studio; for ten years he was not promoted.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Southern Studio and went ten years without promotion.

sentences.zh: 大將軍年羹堯欲闢為幕僚，林急告歸。

translations.literal: General-in-chief Nian Gengyao wished to recruit him as staff; Lin urgently petitioned to return home.
translations.idiomatic: When General-in-Chief Nian Gengyao wished to recruit him as a staff member, Lin urgently petitioned to return home.

sentences.zh: 尋調戶部郎中，出為福建邵武知府，以事解職，詔發浙江，歷杭州、嚴州、金華三府。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to director in the Ministry of Revenue, then went out as prefect of Shaowu in Fujian; relieved of office over an affair, by edict sent to Zhejiang, serving successively at Hangzhou, Yanzhou, and Jinhua prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to director in the Ministry of Revenue, then appointed prefect of Shaowu in Fujian. Relieved of office over an affair, he was sent by imperial order to Zhejiang and served successively as prefect of Hangzhou, Yanzhou, and Jinhua.

sentences.zh: 在杭州，值織造隆升建議改海門尖山海口，別開河以固海塘。

translations.literal: At Hangzhou, when the weaving manufacture Long Sheng proposed altering the Haikou at Jianshan, Haimen, and opening a new river to strengthen the seawall.
translations.idiomatic: While at Hangzhou, the weaving commissioner Long Sheng proposed altering the estuary at Jianshan in Haimen and cutting a new channel to strengthen the seawall.

sentences.zh: 林極言不可，曰：「能使海不潮，則役可興。

translations.literal: Lin strongly stated it was impossible, saying: "If the sea could be made tideless, then the labor could be undertaken."
translations.idiomatic: Lin argued forcefully against it, saying, "Only if the sea could be made tideless would such labor be worth undertaking."

sentences.zh: 否則勞民傷財，萬無成理。

translations.literal: Otherwise it would weary the people and waste wealth, and there is absolutely no principle of success.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise it will weary the people and waste resources, and there is no prospect of success whatsoever.

sentences.zh: 」上書督撫，俱不省。

translations.literal: He submitted memorials to governor-general and governor; none took heed.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted memorials to the governor-general and governor, but neither paid heed.

sentences.zh: 雍正十二年三月二十五日夜，牒下，索杭夫萬五千人，合旁郡無慮數万人。

translations.literal: On the night of the twenty-fifth day of the third month, twelfth year of Yongzheng, an urgent dispatch arrived demanding fifteen thousand Hangzhou laborers, together with neighboring prefectures no fewer than tens of thousands of men.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the twenty-fifth day of the third month in the twelfth year of Yongzheng (1734), an urgent dispatch arrived demanding fifteen thousand laborers from Hangzhou, and from neighboring prefectures no fewer than tens of thousands of men in all.

sentences.zh: 期三日集海上。

translations.literal: They were to assemble at the seashore within three days.
translations.idiomatic: They were to assemble at the seashore within three days.

sentences.zh: 林又爭曰：「田蠶方亟，期會迫，萬一勿戢，奈何？

translations.literal: Lin protested again: "The fields and silkworms are at a critical season; the deadline is pressing—if they are not restrained, what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Lin protested again: "The fields and silkworms are at a critical season, and the deadline is pressing—if the people are not restrained, what then?"

sentences.zh: 必不得已，俟蠶功畢。

translations.literal: If it must be done, wait until the silkworm work is finished.
translations.idiomatic: If it must be done, at least wait until the silkworm season is over.

sentences.zh: 」隆升怒，督益急，以抗旨脅之。

translations.literal: Long Sheng was angry and pressed supervision all the more urgently, threatening him with defiance of the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: Long Sheng was furious and pressed the work all the more urgently, threatening him with defiance of the imperial will.

sentences.zh: 四月，送役往，面詰以工不可成狀。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he sent laborers; face to face he questioned them on the conditions making the work impossible.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he sent the laborers out and confronted Long Sheng in person with the reasons the work could not succeed.

sentences.zh: 隆升益怒，留林督役以困之。

translations.literal: Long Sheng grew still angrier and detained Lin to supervise the labor and thereby wear him down.
translations.idiomatic: Long Sheng grew still angrier and detained Lin to supervise the labor himself, hoping to wear him down.

sentences.zh: 冒雨撫循，泥深沒脛，役人感其誠，咸盡力。

translations.literal: In the rain he comforted and led them; mud was deep to the shins; the laborers were moved by his sincerity and all gave their utmost.
translations.idiomatic: He worked in the rain to comfort and guide them; mud came up to their shins; moved by his sincerity, the laborers all gave their utmost.

sentences.zh: 隆升复虐使，動以捶撻，眾屢譁噪。

translations.literal: Long Sheng again treated them cruelly, constantly flogging; the crowd repeatedly clamored.
translations.idiomatic: Long Sheng again treated them cruelly, constantly flogging them, and the crowd repeatedly erupted in uproar.

sentences.zh: 微林，事幾殆。

translations.literal: Without Lin, the affair nearly came to disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Without Lin, the affair would nearly have ended in disaster.

sentences.zh: 役迄無成，隆升得罪去。

translations.literal: When the labor ended without success, Long Sheng was punished and left.
translations.idiomatic: When the labor ended without success, Long Sheng was punished and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，召至京，入對，即日擢長蘆鹽運使。

translations.literal: Early in Qianlong he was summoned to the capital, entered audience, and the same day was promoted salt transport commissioner of Changlu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign he was summoned to the capital, received an audience, and the same day was promoted to salt transport commissioner of Changlu.

sentences.zh: 曩時院司歲各費數万緡，林率以儉，歲費百緡而已，羨餘悉歸公。

translations.literal: Formerly each year the yamen officials each spent tens of thousands of strings of cash; Lin was frugal throughout, yearly expense only a hundred strings; surplus all returned to the public.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the yamen officials each spent tens of thousands of strings of cash per year; Lin practiced frugality throughout, spending only a hundred strings annually and returning all surplus to the public coffers.

sentences.zh: 居四年，以親老乞養。

translations.literal: After four years, he petitioned to retire and nourish his aged parents.
translations.idiomatic: After four years he petitioned to retire and care for his aged parents.

sentences.zh: 高宗曰：「世乃有不原久為長蘆運使者耶？

translations.literal: Gaozong said: "In this world are there truly those who do not wish to remain salt transport commissioner of Changlu for long?"
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor said, "In this world are there truly people who do not wish to remain salt transport commissioner of Changlu for long?"

sentences.zh: 」久之，卒於家。

translations.literal: After a long time, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while, he died at home.

sentences.zh: =閻堯熙=閻堯熙，字涑陽，河南夏邑人，原籍山西太原。

translations.literal: Yan Yaoxi. Yan Yaoxi, courtesy name Suyang, was a native of Xiayi in Henan, with original household registration in Taiyuan, Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yaoxi, courtesy name Suyang, was a native of Xiayi in Henan; his original household registration was in Taiyuan, Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十五年進士，五十二年，授直隸藁城知縣。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year of Kangxi he passed the jinshi; in the fifty-second year he was appointed magistrate of Gaocheng in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the forty-fifth year of the Kangxi reign and in the fifty-second year was appointed magistrate of Gaocheng in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 滹沱常以秋溢，築堤樹木椿，以捍其衝，夾岸種柳，堤固，水不為患。

translations.literal: The Hutuo often overflowed in autumn; he built dikes and planted wooden piles to withstand the rush, and planted willows along both banks; the dike held firm and the water no longer caused harm.
translations.idiomatic: The Hutuo River often overflowed in autumn; he built dikes and drove wooden piles to withstand the flood, planted willows along both banks, and the embankment held firm so the water no longer caused harm.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，調南宮，擢晉州知州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was transferred to Nangong and promoted to prefect of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongzheng reign he was transferred to Nangong and promoted to prefect of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 州瀕滹沱河，河決徙道，盪析民居。

translations.literal: The prefecture bordered the Hutuo River; the river burst its banks and changed course, sweeping away the dwellings of the people.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture bordered the Hutuo River; when the river burst its banks and changed course, it swept away the homes of the people.

sentences.zh: 堯熙為籌安集，民免於患，扶攜老稚來謝。

translations.literal: Yaoxi planned relief and resettlement; the people were spared disaster, and the old and young came leaning on one another to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoxi planned relief and resettlement so the people were spared disaster; the elderly and children came leaning on one another to thank him.

sentences.zh: 堯熙曰：「此朝廷恩，我何與？

translations.literal: Yaoxi said: "This is the court's grace—what have I to do with it?"
translations.idiomatic: Yaoxi said, "This is the court's grace—what have I to do with it?"

sentences.zh: 」令望闕拜，人給百錢，以資裹糧，散錢十萬，咸感泣曰：「真父母也！

translations.literal: He had them face the palace gate and bow; each person was given a hundred cash for travel provisions; he distributed a hundred thousand cash in all; all wept with emotion and said: "A true parent indeed!"
translations.idiomatic: He had them face the palace gate and bow; each person received a hundred cash for travel provisions; he distributed a hundred thousand cash in all, and all wept with emotion, saying, "A true parent to the people!"

sentences.zh: 」怡賢親王奉使過境，聞其名，奏循良第一。

translations.literal: Prince Yixian, on imperial mission passing through the region, heard his name and memorialized him as foremost among exemplary officials.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yixian, passing through on an imperial mission, heard of his reputation and memorialized him as the foremost exemplary official.

sentences.zh: 擢山東青州知府，未之官，改授浙江嘉興。

translations.literal: He was promoted to prefect of Qingzhou in Shandong but did not take up the post; he was reassigned to Jiaxing in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Qingzhou in Shandong but never took up the post and was reassigned to Jiaxing in Zhejiang instead.

sentences.zh: 俗健訟，良懦不得直。

translations.literal: The local custom favored litigation; the good and weak could not obtain justice.
translations.idiomatic: Litigation was rampant locally, and the honest and weak could not obtain justice.

sentences.zh: 訟府，下縣，或不理，奸猾益無忌。

translations.literal: When suits went to the prefecture and were sent down to the counties, sometimes they were not handled, and the cunning grew ever more fearless.
translations.idiomatic: When cases were sent from the prefecture to the counties, some were left unhandled, and the cunning grew ever bolder.

sentences.zh: 堯熙始至，日受狀三百。

translations.literal: When Yaoxi first arrived, he received three hundred petitions a day.
translations.idiomatic: When Yaoxi first arrived, he received three hundred petitions each day.

sentences.zh: 比對簿，自請息者二百餘，庭折數十，各得其情。

translations.literal: Comparing with the registers, more than two hundred petitioners of their own accord asked to withdraw; he settled dozens in court, each according to its merits.
translations.idiomatic: Comparing the petitions with the registers, more than two hundred litigants voluntarily withdrew their suits; he settled dozens in open court, each according to its true merits.

sentences.zh: 豪民張某稔惡，訊實，杖殺之，民皆稱快。

translations.literal: A powerful man surnamed Zhang, long steeped in evil, was found guilty on investigation and beaten to death; the people all rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: A powerful man surnamed Zhang, long steeped in wickedness, was found guilty on investigation and beaten to death; the people all rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 屬縣賦重，名目糾紛，裡胥因緣為奸。

translations.literal: The subordinate counties had heavy levies with tangled item names; village clerks took advantage to commit malfeasance.
translations.idiomatic: The subordinate counties bore heavy levies with tangled item names, and village clerks took advantage to commit fraud.

sentences.zh: 民完如額，官不知，民亦不自知，官累以缺賦課殿去。

translations.literal: The people paid in full as required, yet the magistrate did not know it, nor did the people themselves know; the magistrate was repeatedly demoted for shortfalls in tax delivery.
translations.idiomatic: The people paid in full as required, yet the magistrate did not know it, nor did the people themselves realize it; magistrates were repeatedly demoted for shortfalls in tax delivery.

sentences.zh: 堯熙巡行清理，民始知額，歲無逋賦。

translations.literal: Yaoxi toured and cleared up the accounts; the people first learned the proper quotas, and each year there were no arrears.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoxi toured the counties and cleared up the accounts; the people first learned the proper quotas, and thereafter there were no arrears each year.

sentences.zh: 海鹽縣塘工不就，總督李衛聽浮言，欲開引河洩潮。

translations.literal: In Haiyan County the seawall work would not succeed; Governor-General Li Wei, listening to irresponsible talk, wished to open a diversion channel to release the tide.
translations.idiomatic: In Haiyan County the seawall work would not succeed; Governor-General Li Wei, listening to irresponsible talk, wished to open a diversion channel to release the tide.

sentences.zh: 堯熙言：「滷水入內河，田皆傷，非等壞廬舍、糜帑金已也。

translations.literal: Yaoxi said: "Brackish water entering the inner rivers would ruin all the fields—this is not merely a matter of damaging houses and wasting treasury funds."
translations.idiomatic: Yaoxi said, "If brackish water enters the inner rivers, all the fields will be ruined—this is not merely a matter of damaging houses and wasting public funds."

sentences.zh: 」議遂罷。

translations.literal: The proposal was then abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was then abandoned.

sentences.zh: 營弁緝私鹽，縱其梟，持他人抵罪。

translations.literal: Garrison officers suppressed private salt but indulged the ringleaders and had others bear the guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison officers suppressed private salt but indulged the ringleaders while having innocent people bear the guilt.

sentences.zh: 堯熙言其誣，總督不聽，庭爭再三，總督乃自勘，釋之，愈以賢堯熙。

translations.literal: Yaoxi stated they had been falsely accused; the governor-general would not listen; he argued repeatedly in court; the governor-general then investigated in person and released them, esteeming Yaoxi all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoxi stated they had been falsely accused; the governor-general would not listen until Yaoxi argued repeatedly in open court; the governor-general then investigated in person, released the victims, and esteemed Yaoxi all the more.

sentences.zh: 累擢湖北按察使、四川布政使，皆持大體，有惠政。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to surveillance commissioner of Hubei and financial commissioner of Sichuan; in each post he upheld broad principles and enacted benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to surveillance commissioner of Hubei and financial commissioner of Sichuan; in each post he upheld broad principles and enacted benevolent policies.

sentences.zh: 乾隆七年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qianlong he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Qianlong reign he died in office.

sentences.zh: 堯熙質直，好面折人過，雖上官不少避。

translations.literal: Yaoxi was plain and direct, fond of confronting others' faults to their faces, and did not shrink even from superiors.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoxi was plainspoken and direct, fond of confronting others' faults to their faces, and did not shrink even from superiors.

sentences.zh: 然勇於從善，在川籓多得成都知府王時翔之助，人兩賢之。

translations.literal: Yet he was bold in following what was right; in Sichuan he gained much assistance from Chengdu Prefect Wang Shixiang, and people praised both men.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was bold in following what was right; in Sichuan he gained much assistance from Chengdu Prefect Wang Shixiang, and people praised both men.

sentences.zh: 時翔，字皋謨，江蘇鎮洋人。

translations.literal: Shixiang, courtesy name Gaomo, was a native of Zhenjiang in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shixiang, courtesy name Gaomo, was a native of Zhenjiang in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 為諸生，績學未遇。

translations.literal: As a licentiate he pursued learning diligently but did not meet with success.
translations.idiomatic: As a licentiate he pursued learning diligently but did not meet with success in the examinations.

sentences.zh: 雍正六年，世宗重選守令，命中外官各舉一人，同州人沈起元，官興化知府，以時翔應詔，即授福建晉江知縣。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongzheng the Yongzheng Emperor emphasized selecting prefects and magistrates and ordered officials inside and outside to each recommend one person; Shen Qiyuan of the same prefecture, serving as prefect of Xinghua, recommended Shixiang in response to the edict, and he was immediately appointed magistrate of Jinjiang in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Yongzheng reign the emperor emphasized selecting prefects and magistrates and ordered officials throughout the empire each to recommend one person; Shen Qiyuan of the same prefecture, then prefect of Xinghua, recommended Shixiang in response to the edict, and he was immediately appointed magistrate of Jinjiang in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 時福建吏治頹廢，遣使按視，多更諸守令有司，頗尚操切。

translations.literal: At that time administration in Fujian was decadent; an envoy was sent to inspect, and many prefects and magistrates were replaced; they tended rather toward harsh severity.
translations.idiomatic: At that time administration in Fujian was decadent; an imperial envoy was sent to inspect, and many prefects and magistrates were replaced, with a tendency toward harsh severity.

sentences.zh: 晉江民好訟，時翔至，曰：「此吾赤子，忍以盜賊視乎？

translations.literal: The people of Jinjiang were fond of litigation; when Shixiang arrived he said: "These are my children—how can I treat them as bandits?"
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jinjiang were fond of litigation; when Shixiang arrived he said, "These are my own children—how can I treat them as bandits?"

sentences.zh: 」一以寬和為治。

translations.literal: He governed entirely with leniency and harmony.
translations.idiomatic: He governed entirely with leniency and harmony.

sentences.zh: 坐堂皇，呴呴作家人語。

translations.literal: He sat in the main hall and spoke gently in the tones of family conversation.
translations.idiomatic: He sat in the main hall and spoke gently in the tones of family conversation.

sentences.zh: 曲直既判，令兩造釋忿，相對揖，由是訟者日衰。

translations.literal: Once right and wrong were decided, he ordered both parties to release their anger and bow to each other; from this litigation daily declined.
translations.idiomatic: Once right and wrong were decided, he ordered both parties to release their anger and bow to each other; from this litigation daily declined.

sentences.zh: 觀風整俗使劉師恕按泉州，委時翔鞫疑獄二十餘事，語人曰：「晉江長者，決獄又何精敏也！

translations.literal: Liu Shishu, commissioner for reforming local customs, inspected Quanzhou and entrusted Shixiang with trying more than twenty doubtful cases; he told people: "The elder of Jinjiang—how keen and sharp his judgments are!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shishu, commissioner for reforming local customs, inspected Quanzhou and entrusted Shixiang with trying more than twenty doubtful cases; he told people, "The elder of Jinjiang—how keen and sharp his judgments are!"

sentences.zh: 」尋調政和，又調甌寧。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Zhenghe, then to Ouning.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Zhenghe, then to Ouning.

sentences.zh: 擢漳州府同知，駐南勝。

translations.literal: He was promoted to subprefect of Zhangzhou Prefecture, stationed at Nansheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to subprefect of Zhangzhou Prefecture, stationed at Nansheng.

sentences.zh: 南勝民族居峒中，多械鬥。

translations.literal: The native peoples of Nansheng lived in mountain stockades and frequently fought with weapons.
translations.idiomatic: The native peoples of Nansheng lived in mountain stockades and frequently fought with weapons.

sentences.zh: 有賴唱者，糾眾奪犯，匿險自固。

translations.literal: There was one Lai Chang who gathered a crowd to seize a prisoner and hid in rugged terrain to hold fast.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Lai Chang who gathered a crowd to seize a prisoner and hid in rugged terrain to hold fast.

sentences.zh: 時翔親入山諭之曰：「汝諸賴萬人，奈何庇一人而以死殉耶？

translations.literal: Shixiang personally entered the mountains and admonished them, saying: "You Lai number ten thousand men—why shelter one man and die for him?"
translations.idiomatic: Shixiang personally entered the mountains and admonished them, saying, "You Lai number ten thousand men—why shelter one man and die for him?"

sentences.zh: 為我縛唱來即無事。

translations.literal: Bind Chang and bring him to me and there will be no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Bind Chang and bring him to me and there will be no trouble.

sentences.zh: 」唱不得已自縛出，始如律。

translations.literal: Chang had no choice but to bind himself and come out; only then was the law applied.
translations.idiomatic: Chang had no choice but to bind himself and come out; only then was the law applied.

sentences.zh: 瀨子坑民葉揚煽亂，時翔謂緩之可一紙定，或張其事，大吏檄入山剿之。

translations.literal: The people of Laizikeng, Ye Yang, stirred up disorder; Shixiang said that if handled gently it could be settled with a single document, but someone exaggerated the affair and the grand coordinators ordered a punitive expedition into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Yang of Laizikeng stirred up disorder; Shixiang said that if handled gently it could be settled with a single document, but someone exaggerated the affair and the grand coordinators ordered a punitive expedition into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 事平，意不自得，乞病歸。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was ill at ease and petitioned to return home on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled he was ill at ease and petitioned to return home on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，以薦起山西蒲州府同知，擢成都知府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, on recommendation he was appointed subprefect of Puzhou Prefecture in Shanxi and promoted to prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qianlong reign, on recommendation he was appointed subprefect of Puzhou in Shanxi and promoted to prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 以廉率屬，善審機要。

translations.literal: He led his subordinates with integrity and was skilled at judging what was essential.
translations.idiomatic: He led his subordinates with integrity and was skilled at judging what was essential.

sentences.zh: 錢價騰，布政使榜平其直，市大譁。

translations.literal: The price of cash rose sharply; the financial commissioner posted notices to level the price, and the market erupted in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: The price of cash rose sharply; the financial commissioner posted notices to level the price, and the market erupted in uproar.

sentences.zh: 時翔方在假，召成都、華陽二令曰：「市直當順民情，抑之，錢閉不出，奈何？

translations.literal: Shixiang was then on leave; he summoned the magistrates of Chengdu and Huayang and said: "Market price should follow the people's wishes—if you suppress it, cash will not come out; what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Shixiang was then on leave; he summoned the magistrates of Chengdu and Huayang and said, "Market price should follow the people's wishes—if you suppress it, cash will not circulate; what then?"

sentences.zh: 」言於布政撤其榜，錢價尋平。

translations.literal: He spoke to the financial commissioner, who withdrew the notices, and the price of cash soon stabilized.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke to the financial commissioner, who withdrew the notices, and the price of cash soon stabilized.

sentences.zh: 議徙涼州兵於成都，拓駐防城，當奪民居二千家。

translations.literal: It was proposed to transfer troops from Liangzhou to Chengdu and expand the garrison city, which would require seizing two thousand civilian dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: It was proposed to transfer troops from Liangzhou to Chengdu and expand the garrison city, which would require seizing two thousand civilian dwellings.

sentences.zh: 時翔檢故牘，請曰：「城故容兵三千，現兵一千五百，尚虛其半。

translations.literal: Shixiang searched the old records and petitioned: "The city originally could hold three thousand troops; present troops number one thousand five hundred—half still stands empty."
translations.idiomatic: Shixiang searched the old records and petitioned, "The city originally could hold three thousand troops; present troops number only fifteen hundred—half the space still stands empty."

sentences.zh: 第出現所侵地足矣，奚拓為？

translations.literal: Simply recover the land presently occupied—that is enough; why expand?"
translations.idiomatic: Simply recover the land presently occupied—that is enough; why expand?"

sentences.zh: 」已而涼州兵亦不果徙。

translations.literal: Before long the transfer of Liangzhou troops also did not take place.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the transfer of Liangzhou troops also did not take place.

sentences.zh: 成都當康熙時，人稀穀賤，旗兵利得銀。

translations.literal: In Chengdu during the Kangxi period people were sparse and grain was cheap; banner soldiers preferred to receive silver.
translations.idiomatic: In Chengdu during the Kangxi period people were sparse and grain was cheap; banner soldiers preferred to receive silver.

sentences.zh: 至雍正以後，生聚多，穀貴，又原得穀。

translations.literal: From the Yongzheng period onward the population grew and grain became dear; they again wished to receive grain.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yongzheng period onward the population grew and grain became dear; they again wished to receive grain.

sentences.zh: 或徇其意，令民受銀，購穀給兵。

translations.literal: Some indulged their wishes and had the people accept silver and purchase grain to supply the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Some indulged their wishes and had the people accept silver and purchase grain to supply the troops.

sentences.zh: 未幾，漢兵亦欲仿行，時翔曰：「旗兵例不出城，語言與土人殊，故代購。

translations.literal: Before long the Han troops also wished to follow suit; Shixiang said: "Banner troops by regulation do not leave the city; their speech differs from the natives, hence grain is purchased on their behalf."
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Han troops also wished to follow suit; Shixiang said, "Banner troops by regulation do not leave the city; their speech differs from the natives, hence grain is purchased on their behalf."

sentences.zh: 漢兵皆土著，奚代為？

translations.literal: Han troops are all natives—why purchase on their behalf?"
translations.idiomatic: Han troops are all natives—why purchase on their behalf?"

sentences.zh: 」二事亦賴布政力主其議得止。

translations.literal: These two matters also relied on the financial commissioner vigorously upholding the proposals to halt them.
translations.idiomatic: These two matters also relied on the financial commissioner vigorously upholding the proposals to halt them.

sentences.zh: 至七年，江南、湖廣災，巡撫奏運蜀米四十萬石濟之。

translations.literal: By the seventh year, disasters struck Jiangnan and Huguang; the governor memorialized to transport four hundred thousand piculs of Sichuan rice for relief.
translations.idiomatic: By the seventh year, disasters struck Jiangnan and Huguang; the governor memorialized to transport four hundred thousand piculs of Sichuan rice for relief.

sentences.zh: 湖廣急米，來領運，江南則否。

translations.literal: Huguang urgently needed the grain and came to take charge of transport; Jiangnan did not.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang urgently needed the grain and came to take charge of transport; Jiangnan did not.

sentences.zh: 巡撫乃檄下縣餽運，舳艫蔽江，商賈不通，成都薪炭俱絕。

translations.literal: The governor then ordered the counties to supply transport; boats covered the river and merchants could not pass; in Chengdu even fuel and charcoal were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The governor then ordered the counties to supply transport; boats covered the river and merchants could not pass; in Chengdu even fuel and charcoal were cut off.

sentences.zh: 時翔謂江南運可緩，徒病蜀。

translations.literal: Shixiang said Jiangnan transport could be delayed and would only harm Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiang said Jiangnan transport could be delayed and would only harm Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 請獨運楚，而聽商人自運江南。

translations.literal: He requested transporting only to Chu and allowing merchants to transport to Jiangnan on their own.
translations.idiomatic: He requested transporting only to Huguang and allowing merchants to transport to Jiangnan on their own.

sentences.zh: 時堯熙既沒，竟無用其言者。

translations.literal: By then Yaoxi had already died, and in the end no one adopted his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yaoxi had already died, and in the end no one adopted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 時翔在成都，屢雪疑獄，時稱神明。

translations.literal: Shixiang in Chengdu repeatedly cleared doubtful cases and was at the time called divine in judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiang in Chengdu repeatedly cleared doubtful cases and was at the time called divine in judgment.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he died.

sentences.zh: =藍鼎元=藍鼎元，字玉霖，福建漳浦人。

translations.literal: Lan Dingyuan. Lan Dingyuan, courtesy name Yulin, was a native of Zhangpu in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Dingyuan, courtesy name Yulin, was a native of Zhangpu in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 少孤力學，通達治體，嘗泛海考求閩、浙形勢。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he studied diligently, mastered principles of governance, and once crossed the sea to investigate the terrain of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he studied diligently, mastered principles of governance, and once crossed the sea to investigate the terrain of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 巡撫張伯行器之，曰：「藍生經世之良材，吾道之羽翼也。

translations.literal: Governor Zhang Boxing valued him and said: "Student Lan is fine timber for governing the age—a wing to our way."
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhang Boxing valued him and said, "Student Lan is fine timber for governing the age—a wing to our way."

sentences.zh: 康熙六十年，台灣朱一貴倡亂，鼎元從兄南澳鎮總兵廷珍率師進討，多出贊畫，七日台灣平。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year of Kangxi, Zhu Yigui raised rebellion in Taiwan; Dingyuan's cousin Tingzhen, regional commander of Nan'ao, led troops to attack; Dingyuan largely planned the campaign; in seven days Taiwan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year of the Kangxi reign, Zhu Yigui raised rebellion in Taiwan; Dingyuan's cousin Tingzhen, regional commander of Nan'ao, led troops to attack; Dingyuan largely planned the campaign, and in seven days Taiwan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 復從廷珍招降人，殄遺孽，撫流民，綏番社，歲餘始返。

translations.literal: He again followed Tingzhen in receiving those who surrendered, exterminating remnant rebels, comforting displaced people, and pacifying aboriginal communities; only after more than a year did he return.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Tingzhen in receiving those who surrendered, exterminating remnant rebels, comforting displaced people, and pacifying aboriginal communities; only after more than a year did he return.

sentences.zh: 著論言治台之策，大意謂：「土地有日闢、無日蹙，經營疆理，則為戶口貢賦之區；

translations.literal: He wrote a treatise on governing Taiwan, stating in general: "Land may daily be opened but never daily shrinks; if frontiers are managed, it becomes a region of households and tax revenue;"
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a treatise on governing Taiwan, stating in general, "Land may daily be opened but never daily shrinks; if frontiers are managed, it becomes a region of households and tax revenue;"

sentences.zh: 廢置空虛，則為盜賊倡亂之所。

translations.literal: if left vacant and abandoned, it becomes a place where bandits and rebels arise.
translations.idiomatic: if left vacant and abandoned, it becomes a place where bandits and rebels arise.

sentences.zh: 山高地肥，最利墾闢。

translations.literal: The mountains are high and the soil fertile—most favorable for reclamation.
translations.idiomatic: The mountains are high and the soil fertile—most favorable for reclamation.

sentences.zh: 利之所在，人所必趨。

translations.literal: Where profit lies, people will surely rush.
translations.idiomatic: Where profit lies, people will surely rush.

sentences.zh: 不歸之民，則歸之番與賊。

translations.literal: If it does not go to the people, it will go to the aborigines and bandits.
translations.idiomatic: If it does not go to the people, it will go to the aborigines and bandits.

sentences.zh: 即使內亂不生，寇自外來，將有日本、荷蘭之患，不可不早為措置。

translations.literal: Even if internal disorder does not arise, when invaders come from outside there will be trouble from Japan and Holland—measures must be taken early.
translations.idiomatic: Even if internal disorder does not arise, when invaders come from outside there will be trouble from Japan and Holland—measures must be taken early.

sentences.zh: 」時議者謂台灣鎮當移澎湖，鼎元力言不可，大吏採其說，見諸施行。

translations.literal: At the time debaters held that the Taiwan garrison should be moved to Penghu; Dingyuan strongly stated this was impossible; the grand coordinators adopted his view and put it into practice.
translations.idiomatic: At the time debaters held that the Taiwan garrison should be moved to Penghu; Dingyuan strongly stated this was impossible; the grand coordinators adopted his view and put it into practice.

sentences.zh: 鼎元復為台灣道條十九事，曰「信賞罰、懲訟師、除草竊、治客民、禁惡俗、儆吏胥、革規例、崇節儉、正婚嫁、興學校、修武備、嚴守禦、教樹畜、寬租賦、行墾田、复官莊、卹澎民、撫土番、招生番。

translations.literal: Dingyuan also drafted nineteen items for the Taiwan circuit, namely: trust rewards and punishments, punish litigation masters, eliminate grass theft, govern guest settlers, prohibit evil customs, warn yamen runners, abolish irregular fees, esteem frugality, correct marriage customs, establish schools, repair military preparedness, strictly defend frontiers, teach forestry and livestock, lighten land tax, carry out land reclamation, restore official estates, relieve Penghu people, pacify native tribes, and recruit aboriginal peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Dingyuan also drafted nineteen items for the Taiwan circuit, namely: trust rewards and punishments, punish litigation masters, eliminate grass theft, govern guest settlers, prohibit evil customs, warn yamen runners, abolish irregular fees, esteem frugality, correct marriage customs, establish schools, repair military preparedness, strictly defend frontiers, teach forestry and livestock, lighten land tax, carry out land reclamation, restore official estates, relieve Penghu people, pacify native tribes, and recruit aboriginal peoples.

sentences.zh: 」後之治台者，多以為法。

translations.literal: Later governors of Taiwan mostly took these as their model.
translations.idiomatic: Later governors of Taiwan mostly took these as their model.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，以選拔入京師，分修一統志。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, selected for advancement he entered the capital and took part in compiling the unified gazetteer.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongzheng reign, selected for advancement he entered the capital and took part in compiling the unified gazetteer.

sentences.zh: 六年，大學士硃軾薦之，引見，奏陳時務六事，世宗善之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Grand Secretary Zhu Shi recommended him; he was received in audience and memorialized on six matters of state; the Yongzheng Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Grand Secretary Zhu Shi recommended him; he was received in audience and memorialized on six matters of state; the Yongzheng Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 尋授廣東普寧知縣，在官有惠政，聽斷如神。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed magistrate of Puning in Guangdong; in office he enacted benevolent policies and judged cases like a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed magistrate of Puning in Guangdong; in office he enacted benevolent policies and judged cases with uncanny insight.

sentences.zh: 集邑士秀異者講明正學，風俗一變。

translations.literal: He gathered the outstanding scholars of the county to expound orthodox learning, and local customs were wholly transformed.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the outstanding scholars of the county to expound orthodox learning, and local customs were wholly transformed.

sentences.zh: 調權潮陽縣事，歲薦飢，多逋賦，減耗糧，除苛累，民爭趨納。

translations.literal: Transferred temporarily to handle affairs in Chaoyang County; that year famine was recommended and many taxes were in arrears; he reduced wastage in grain transport and abolished harsh exactions; the people competed to pay.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred temporarily to handle affairs in Chaoyang County; that year famine was reported and many taxes were in arrears; he reduced wastage in grain transport and abolished harsh exactions; the people competed to pay.

sentences.zh: 妖女林妙貴惑眾，寘之法。

translations.literal: The sorceress Lin Miaogui deluded the masses and was punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: The sorceress Lin Miaogui deluded the masses and was punished by law.

sentences.zh: 籍其居，建棉陽書院。

translations.literal: Her residence was confiscated and the Mianyang Academy was built there.
translations.idiomatic: Her residence was confiscated and the Mianyang Academy was built there.

sentences.zh: 以忤監司罷職，總督鄂彌達疏白其誣，徵詣闕。

translations.literal: Because he offended the surveillance commissioner he was dismissed; Governor E'erduo memorialized clearing him of false accusation and he was summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: Because he offended the surveillance commissioner he was dismissed; Governor E'erduo memorialized clearing him of false accusation and he was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 逾年，命署廣州知府，抵官一月，卒。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was ordered to serve as acting prefect of Guangzhou; one month after reaching his post he died.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was ordered to serve as acting prefect of Guangzhou; one month after reaching his post he died.

sentences.zh: 鼎元尤善治盜及訟師，多置耳目，劾捕不稍貸，而斷獄多所平反，論者以為嚴而不殘。

translations.literal: Dingyuan was especially skilled at governing bandits and litigation masters; he placed many informants, impeached and arrested without leniency, yet in trying cases often reversed wrongful convictions; critics held him strict but not cruel.
translations.idiomatic: Dingyuan was especially skilled at governing bandits and litigation masters; he placed many informants, impeached and arrested without leniency, yet in trying cases often reversed wrongful convictions; critics held him strict but not cruel.

sentences.zh: 志在經世，而不竟其用。

translations.literal: His aim was to govern the age, yet he did not fully realize his capacity.
translations.idiomatic: His aim was to govern the age, yet he did not fully realize his capacity.

sentences.zh: 著鹿洲集、東征集、平台紀略、棉陽學準、鹿洲公案傳於世。

translations.literal: He authored the Luzhou Collection, Dongzheng Collection, Pingtai Jilue, Mianyang Xuezhun, and Luzhou Gong'an, which circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Luzhou Collection, Dongzheng Collection, Pingtai Jilue, Mianyang Xuezhun, and Luzhou Gong'an, which circulate in the world.

sentences.zh: =葉新=葉新，字惟一，浙江金華人。

translations.literal: Ye Xin. Ye Xin, courtesy name Weiyi, was a native of Jinhua in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Xin, courtesy name Weiyi, was a native of Jinhua in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十一年，順天舉人。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year of Kangxi he became a provincial graduate of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year of the Kangxi reign he became a provincial graduate of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 從蠡縣李恭受業，立日譜自檢，尤嚴義利之辨。

translations.literal: He studied under Li Gong of Lixian, kept a daily record for self-examination, and was especially strict in distinguishing righteousness from profit.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Li Gong of Lixian, kept a daily record for self-examination, and was especially strict in distinguishing righteousness from profit.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，以知縣揀發四川，授仁壽縣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng he was selected as magistrate and sent to Sichuan, appointed to Renshou County.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Yongzheng reign he was selected as magistrate and sent to Sichuan, appointed to Renshou County.

sentences.zh: 有與鄰縣爭地界者，當會勘，鄉保因閽人以賄請，新怒，悉下之獄。

translations.literal: There were those disputing boundary land with neighboring counties; when a joint survey was to be held, village wardens tried to bribe through gatekeepers. Ye Xin was angered and had them all thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: When people from neighboring counties disputed their boundaries and a joint survey was ordered, village wardens tried to bribe the gatekeepers. Ye Xin was furious and had every one of them thrown in jail.

sentences.zh: 勘畢，各按其罪，由是吏民斂手奉法。

translations.literal: When the survey was finished, each was punished according to his crime; from this officials and people restrained their hands and obeyed the law.
translations.idiomatic: After the survey was completed, each man was punished according to his offense, and from then on officials and commoners alike kept their hands to themselves and obeyed the law.

sentences.zh: 署嘉定州，故有沒水田，多逋賦。

translations.literal: While serving as acting magistrate of Jiading Prefecture, there was formerly submerged paddy land with much tax in arrears.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as acting magistrate of Jiading Prefecture, he found fields that had long lain submerged under water and carried heavy tax arrears.

sentences.zh: 新視曠土可耕者，召民墾闢，以新科抵賦額，舊逋悉免。

translations.literal: Ye Xin looked at fallow land that could be cultivated, summoned the people to open and reclaim it, offsetting the tax quota with new assessments, and all old arrears were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Xin identified fallow land that could be farmed, summoned the people to reclaim it, applied the new assessments against the old tax quotas, and remitted all outstanding arrears.

sentences.zh: 時仁壽採木，部匠倚官為暴，民勿堪，糾眾相抗，縣以變告，檄新往治之，抵匠頭及首糾眾者於法，餘釋不問。

translations.literal: At that time Renshou was harvesting timber; department craftsmen relied on official power to commit violence, and the people could not bear it. They gathered in a crowd to resist; the county reported it as a disturbance and dispatched Ye Xin to handle it. He punished the craftsman chief and the chief agitators according to law, and released the rest without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Renshou was harvesting timber, and ministry craftsmen abused official backing to terrorize the people until they could bear it no longer and rose up together. The county reported a disturbance and sent Ye Xin to deal with it. He punished the head craftsman and the ringleaders under the law and released the rest without further inquiry.

sentences.zh: 遷工卩州知州，再遷夔州府同知，署龍安及成都知府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be magistrate of Gongzhou, then again to vice-prefect of Kuizhou Prefecture, and served as acting prefect of Long'an and Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to magistrate of Gongzhou, then transferred again to vice-prefect of Kuizhou Prefecture, and served as acting prefect of Long'an and Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 又署瀘州知州，訟者至，立剖決，滯獄一空。

translations.literal: Again he served as acting magistrate of Luzhou; when litigants arrived, he immediately decided cases, and the backlog of pending cases was completely cleared.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as acting magistrate of Luzhou, where litigants who came before him had their cases decided on the spot until the backlog of pending suits was completely cleared.

sentences.zh: 治瀘兩載，俗一變焉。

translations.literal: After governing Luzhou for two years, the local customs changed entirely.
translations.idiomatic: After two years governing Luzhou, the local customs were wholly transformed.

sentences.zh: 新自授夔州同知，閱五載，始一蒞任。

translations.literal: From the time Ye Xin was appointed vice-prefect of Kuizhou, five years passed before he once took office.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Ye Xin received appointment as vice-prefect of Kuizhou, five years passed before he finally took up the post even once.

sentences.zh: 尋又署保寧、順慶兩府，擢雅州知府，母憂歸。

translations.literal: Soon he again served as acting prefect of Baoning and Shunqing, was promoted to prefect of Yazhou, and returned home upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served again as acting prefect of Baoning and Shunqing, was promoted to prefect of Yazhou, and then returned home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十年，服闋，補江西建昌。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Qianlong, when the mourning period had ended, he was appointed to Jianchang in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Qianlong reign, after his mourning period ended, he was appointed magistrate of Jianchang in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 修盱江書院，招引文士與講論學術。

translations.literal: He repaired the Xujiang Academy and invited scholars to discuss learning with him.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the Xujiang Academy and invited literary men to join him in discussing scholarship.

sentences.zh: 复南城黃孝子祠，以勵民俗。

translations.literal: He restored the Huang Filial Son Shrine in Nancheng to encourage local custom.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the Huang Filial Son Shrine in Nancheng to encourage proper local conduct.

sentences.zh: 十三年，南豐令報縣民饒令德謀反，令德好拳勇，令以風聞遣役往偵，誤探其仇，謂謀反有據，遂往逮令德，適他往，乃逮其弟繫獄。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, the Nanfeng magistrate reported that a county resident, Rao Lingde, was plotting rebellion. Lingde was fond of boxing and martial courage. On hearsay the magistrate sent runners to investigate; they mistakenly investigated his enemy, claimed there was evidence of rebellion, and went to arrest Lingde. He happened to be away, so they arrested his younger brother and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, the magistrate of Nanfeng reported that a county man named Rao Lingde was plotting rebellion. Lingde was fond of boxing and martial prowess. Acting on rumor, the magistrate sent runners to investigate; they mistakenly looked into his enemy, declared the rebellion proven, and went to arrest Lingde. He happened to be away, so they seized his younger brother and threw him in jail.

sentences.zh: 令德歸，自詣縣，受刑誣服，雜引親故及鄰境知識為同謀，追捕蔓及旁郡。

translations.literal: When Lingde returned, he went to the county of his own accord, was tortured and falsely confessed, and randomly implicated relatives, friends, and acquaintances from neighboring districts as co-conspirators. The pursuit spread to adjoining prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingde returned, he presented himself at the yamen, was tortured into a false confession, and randomly named relatives, friends, and acquaintances from neighboring districts as co-conspirators until the dragnet spread into adjoining prefectures.

sentences.zh: 新得報，集諸囚親鞫，株連者已七十餘人，言人人殊。

translations.literal: When Ye Xin received the report, he gathered the prisoners for personal interrogation. Those implicated already numbered more than seventy, and each person's account differed.
translations.idiomatic: When Ye Xin received the report, he gathered the prisoners for personal interrogation. More than seventy people had already been implicated, and no two accounts matched.

sentences.zh: 新詰縣役捕令德弟狀，役言初至其家，獲一篋，疑有金寶匿之。

translations.literal: Ye Xin questioned the county runners about the arrest of Lingde's brother. The runners said that when they first arrived at the house, they seized a box, suspecting that gold and treasures were hidden in it.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Xin questioned the county runners about how Lingde's brother had been arrested. They said that on first reaching the house they had seized a box, suspecting gold and treasure were hidden inside.

sentences.zh: 及發視，無所有，棄之野。

translations.literal: When it was opened and examined, there was nothing inside, and they discarded it in the wild.
translations.idiomatic: When they opened it and looked inside, there was nothing there, so they threw it away in the open country.

sentences.zh: 令聞，意篋有反跡，訊以刑。

translations.literal: When the magistrate heard of this, he suspected the box had contained evidence of rebellion and interrogated them under torture.
translations.idiomatic: When the magistrate heard of this, he assumed the box had held evidence of rebellion and had the runners tortured for answers.

sentences.zh: 妄稱發篋得簿劄，納賄毀之矣。

translations.literal: They falsely claimed that upon opening the box they had found documents and letters, which had been destroyed after bribes were accepted.
translations.idiomatic: They falsely claimed that opening the box had revealed documents and letters, which had been destroyed after bribes changed hands.

sentences.zh: 令謂實然，遂逼令德誣服。

translations.literal: The magistrate believed it was indeed so and thus forced Lingde to falsely confess.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate took this for the truth and forced Lingde into a false confession.

sentences.zh: 新於是盡釋七十餘人縲線，命隨往南昌。

translations.literal: Ye Xin then released all more than seventy people from their bonds and ordered them to accompany him to Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Xin then released all seventy-odd prisoners from their bonds and ordered them to accompany him to Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 戒之曰：「有一逋者，吾代汝死矣。

translations.literal: He warned them, saying, "If even one person is missing, I will die in your place.
translations.idiomatic: He warned them: "If even one of you is missing, I will die in your place.

sentences.zh: 」及至，七十餘人則皆在。

translations.literal: " When they arrived, all more than seventy people were present.
translations.idiomatic: " When they arrived, all seventy-odd men were there.

sentences.zh: 謁巡撫，具道所以，巡撫愕不信，集才能之吏會勘，益雜逮諸所牽引，卒無據，而巡撫已於得報時遽上奏。

translations.literal: He visited the governor and fully explained the reasons. The governor was astonished and disbelieving, gathered capable officials for a joint investigation, further indiscriminately arrested those who had been implicated, and ultimately found no evidence—but the governor had already hastily submitted a memorial upon first receiving the report.
translations.idiomatic: He went before the governor and explained the whole affair. The governor was astonished and refused to believe him, gathered capable officials for a joint review, and indiscriminately arrested still more of those who had been named—yet in the end no evidence was found. By then, however, the governor had already rushed a memorial to the throne upon first receiving the report.

sentences.zh: 朝命兩江總督委官就讞，新為一一剖解得白，所全活二百餘人。

translations.literal: The court ordered the Governor-General of Liangjiang to appoint officials to review the case on the spot. Ye Xin explained each point one by one and cleared them; more than two hundred lives were saved.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the Governor-General of Liangjiang to appoint officials to review the case on the spot. Ye Xin explained each point in turn until the accused were cleared, saving more than two hundred lives.

sentences.zh: 十七年，調贛州，有贛縣搶奪拒捕之獄，值改例，新舊輕重懸殊。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was transferred to Ganzhou. There was a case in Gan County of robbery and resisting arrest; it coincided with a change in the penal code, and the old and new punishments differed greatly in severity.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was transferred to Ganzhou, where a case of robbery and resisting arrest in Gan County coincided with a revision of the penal code, so that the old and new punishments differed sharply in severity.

sentences.zh: 新謂事在例前，當依舊比，爭之不得。

translations.literal: Ye Xin argued that since the matter occurred before the new code, it should be judged by the old precedents, but he could not prevail in the dispute.
