translations.idiomatic: Ye Xin argued that because the offense predated the new code, the old precedents should apply, but he could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 復以寧都民獄事，與​​同官持異同，不得直，謝事閉門候代。

translations.literal: Again, over a civilian case in Ningdu, he held views differing from his colleagues and could not obtain justice, so he resigned his duties, closed his doors, and awaited replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Then, in a civilian case in Ningdu, he again found himself at odds with his colleagues and unable to obtain justice, so he resigned his duties, shut his doors, and waited to be replaced.

sentences.zh: 上官慰喻，不從，遂以任性被劾免歸。

translations.literal: Superiors tried to comfort and persuade him, but he would not comply, and was impeached for willfulness and dismissed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: His superiors tried to comfort and persuade him, but he would not yield and was impeached for obstinacy and dismissed to return home.

sentences.zh: 欣然曰：「今而後可無疚於心矣！

translations.literal: He said happily, "From now on I can be without guilt in my heart!
translations.idiomatic: He said with satisfaction, "From now on I can live without guilt in my heart!

sentences.zh: 」家居十餘年，卒。

translations.literal: " He lived at home for more than ten years, then died.
translations.idiomatic: " He lived at home for more than ten years, then died.

sentences.zh: =施昭庭=施昭庭，字筠瞻，江蘇吳縣人。

translations.literal: Shi Zhaoting. Shi Zhaoting, courtesy name Yunzhan, was a native of Wuxian in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhaoting, courtesy name Yunzhan, was a native of Wuxian in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十四年進士，授江西萬載​​知縣。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the fifty-fourth year of Kangxi, he was appointed magistrate of Wanzai in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in the fifty-fourth year of the Kangxi reign, he was appointed magistrate of Wanzai in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 地僻多山，客民自閩、粵來，居之累年，積三萬餘人，號曰「棚民」。

translations.literal: The place was remote and mountainous. Migrant settlers from Fujian and Guangdong came and lived there for years, accumulating more than thirty thousand people, called "shed dwellers."
translations.idiomatic: The district was remote and mountainous. Migrant settlers from Fujian and Guangdong had lived there for years until their numbers exceeded thirty thousand; they were called "shed dwellers."

sentences.zh: 溫尚貴者，台灣逸盜也，亦處山中。

translations.literal: Wen Shanggui was an escaped pirate from Taiwan and also dwelt in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Shanggui, an escaped pirate from Taiwan, also hid in the mountains.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，福建移捕盜黨急，尚貴謀為變。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, Fujian urgently moved to capture the bandit gang, and Shanggui plotted an uprising.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongzheng reign, as Fujian stepped up its hunt for the bandit gang, Shanggui plotted an uprising.

sentences.zh: 始昭庭之至也，以棚民為慮，厚禮縣人易廉野使偵之。

translations.literal: When Zhaoting first arrived, he was concerned about the shed dwellers and generously rewarded a county man, Yi Lianye, to spy on them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaoting first took office, he was worried about the shed dwellers and handsomely rewarded a local man named Yi Lianye to spy on them.

sentences.zh: 廉野積粟貸棚民，不取息，或免償，得棚民心。

translations.literal: Lianye stored grain and lent it to the shed dwellers without charging interest, sometimes forgiving repayment, and won their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Lianye stored grain and lent it to the shed dwellers without interest, sometimes forgiving repayment altogether, and won their trust.

sentences.zh: 其才者嚴林生、羅老滿，從廉野遊，盡得山中要領。

translations.literal: Among the talented were Yan Linsheng and Luo Laoman, who associated with Lianye and fully learned the essentials of the mountain region.
translations.idiomatic: Among the able men were Yan Linsheng and Luo Laoman, who worked with Lianye and came to know every important feature of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 尚貴將舉事，廉野以聞，昭庭、林生、老滿率勇敢三百人待之。

translations.literal: When Shanggui was about to act, Lianye reported it. Zhaoting, Linsheng, and Laoman led three hundred brave men to await him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shanggui was about to rise, Lianye reported it. Zhaoting, together with Linsheng and Laoman, led three hundred brave men to await him.

sentences.zh: 尚貴有眾二千肆掠，昭庭曰：「賊易破也，然慮其擾傍縣。

translations.literal: Shanggui had two thousand men plundering wildly. Zhaoting said, "The bandits are easy to break, but I worry they will trouble neighboring counties.
translations.idiomatic: Shanggui had two thousand men rampaging through the countryside. Zhaoting said, "The bandits are easy to defeat, but I fear they will ravage neighboring counties.

sentences.zh: 」撫賊​​諜使誑尚貴趨萬載。

translations.literal: " He worked on a bandit spy and had him deceive Shanggui into hurrying toward Wanzai.
translations.idiomatic: " He won over a bandit spy and had him trick Shanggui into hurrying toward Wanzai.

sentences.zh: 乃張疑兵於山徑，賊不敢入，由官道來。

translations.literal: Then he deployed decoy troops on the mountain paths; the bandits dared not enter and came by the official road.
translations.idiomatic: He then posted decoy troops along the mountain paths so the bandits dared not enter them and came instead by the main road.

sentences.zh: 預設伏叢棘中，伺賊過，突出擊殺。

translations.literal: He pre-set ambushes in thickets, waited for the bandits to pass, then burst out to attack and kill.
translations.idiomatic: He laid ambushes in the thickets, waited for the bandits to pass, then burst out and struck them down.

sentences.zh: 賊數中伏，疑駭，逆擊之，一戰獲尚貴。

translations.literal: Many bandits fell into ambush, suspicious and terrified; they counterattacked, and in one battle Shanggui was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the bandits walked into the ambush, panicked and suspicious, and though they counterattacked, Shanggui was captured in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 尚貴起二日而敗，又二日而撫標兵至。

translations.literal: Shanggui had risen for two days and then was defeated; two days later the provincial troops arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Shanggui had been in rebellion for only two days before he was defeated; two days later the provincial troops arrived.

sentences.zh: 初，棚民與市人積嫌，事起，道路洶洶，指目棚民。

translations.literal: At first the shed dwellers and townspeople had accumulated resentments. When the incident arose, the roads were in uproar and fingers were pointed at the shed dwellers.
translations.idiomatic: The shed dwellers and townspeople had long nursed grievances against one another, and when trouble broke out the roads buzzed with accusation and every eye turned on the shed dwellers.

sentences.zh: 昭庭以免死帖與諸降者，取棚民不從賊者結狀，兵至搜山，不戮一人。

translations.literal: Zhaoting gave certificates of spared death to those who surrendered, obtained sworn statements from shed dwellers who had not followed the bandits, and when troops arrived to search the mountains, not a single person was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoting issued certificates sparing the lives of those who surrendered, collected sworn statements from shed dwellers who had not joined the bandits, and when troops came to search the mountains, not one person was killed.

sentences.zh: 巡撫初到官，張其事入奏，既見縣申狀不合，欲改之，昭庭不可。

translations.literal: The governor had just taken office and exaggerated the matter in a memorial. Seeing that the county report did not match, he wanted to revise it, but Zhaoting refused.
translations.idiomatic: The governor had only just taken office and inflated the affair in a memorial to the throne. When he saw that the county report did not match his account and wanted to revise it, Zhaoting refused.

sentences.zh: 又謂棚民匿盜從亂，今雖赦之，必驅歸本籍。

translations.literal: He also said the shed dwellers had harbored bandits and joined the rebellion; though pardoned now, they must be driven back to their native places.
translations.idiomatic: The governor also argued that the shed dwellers had sheltered bandits and joined the rebellion, and that even though they were pardoned, they must be driven back to their native districts.

sentences.zh: 昭庭曰：「棚民種植自給，非刀手老瓜賊之比。

translations.literal: Zhaoting said, "The shed dwellers farm to support themselves—they are not like armed thugs and melon-stealing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoting replied, "The shed dwellers grow their own food. They are not armed ruffians or petty melon thieves.

sentences.zh: 歷年多，生齒眾，間與居民爭訐細故，不必深懲。

translations.literal: They have lived here for many years and their population has grown; occasionally they quarrel with residents over trivial matters—there is no need for severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: They have lived here for many years, their numbers have grown, and they occasionally quarrel with local residents over trifles. That does not call for harsh punishment.

sentences.zh: 今亂由台灣逸盜，而平盜悉資棚民。

translations.literal: Today's disorder was caused by the escaped Taiwan pirate, and suppressing the bandits relied entirely on the shed dwellers.
translations.idiomatic: Today's trouble came from an escaped Taiwan pirate, and putting down the bandits depended entirely on the shed dwellers.

sentences.zh: 」力請：「覈戶口，編保甲，泯其主客之形，寬其衣食之路，長治久安，於計便。

translations.literal: " He strongly petitioned: "Verify household registers, organize mutual-responsibility units, erase the distinction between hosts and guests, and widen their paths to food and clothing—for long-term peace and stability this is the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: " He strongly petitioned: "Verify household registers, organize them into mutual-responsibility units, erase the distinction between locals and newcomers, and give them room to earn their living. That is the surest path to lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 」總督查弼納許之，巡撫尋亦悟，如昭庭策，棚民乃安。

translations.literal: " Governor-General Cha Yinna approved it; the governor soon also understood, and following Zhaoting's plan, the shed dwellers were settled.
translations.idiomatic: " Governor-General Cha Yinna approved the plan; the governor soon came round as well, and by following Zhaoting's policy the shed dwellers were finally settled.

sentences.zh: 事聞，世宗諭九卿曰：「知縣以數年心力辦賊，巡撫到官幾日，豈得有其功耶？

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Emperor Shizong told the Nine Ministers, "The magistrate spent years of effort handling the bandits—how can the governor, who has been in office only a few days, claim the credit?
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was reported, Emperor Shizong told the Nine Ministers, "The magistrate spent years of effort suppressing the bandits. How can a governor who has been in office only a few days claim the credit?

sentences.zh: 」獨下總督疏，議敘，以主事知州用。

translations.literal: " Only the governor-general's memorial was forwarded for merit consideration; he was recommended for appointment as department director with the rank of prefect.
translations.idiomatic: " Only the governor-general's memorial was forwarded for honors, and Zhaoting was recommended for appointment as a department director with the rank of prefect.

sentences.zh: 尋引疾歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: Soon he retired citing illness and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he retired on grounds of illness and died at home.

sentences.zh: =陳慶門=陳慶門，字容駟，陝西盩厔人。

translations.literal: Chen Qingmen. Chen Qingmen, courtesy name Rongsi, was a native of Zhouzhi in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qingmen, courtesy name Rongsi, was a native of Zhouzhi in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the first year of Yongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in the first year of the Yongzheng reign.

sentences.zh: 從鄠王心敬講學，養親不仕。

translations.literal: He studied under Wang Xinjing of Hu and supported his parents without taking office.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Wang Xinjing of Hu and stayed home to care for his parents rather than enter official service.

sentences.zh: 母王趣之，乃謁選。

translations.literal: His mother Wang urged him, whereupon he went to await appointment.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Wang pressed him to serve, and he then went to await appointment.

sentences.zh: 七年，授安徽廬江知縣，修建文廟，規制悉備。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed magistrate of Lujiang in Anhui; he built the Confucian temple with complete regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed magistrate of Lujiang in Anhui, where he rebuilt the Confucian temple to full standard.

sentences.zh: 大濬城壕。

translations.literal: He greatly dredged the city moat.
translations.idiomatic: He undertook a major dredging of the city moat.

sentences.zh: 置義田二百畝有奇。

translations.literal: He established charitable fields of more than two hundred mu.
translations.idiomatic: He set aside more than two hundred mu of charitable fields.

sentences.zh: 贍養煢獨，立社倉四所，積穀以貸平民。

translations.literal: Supporting the orphaned and alone, he established four community granaries and stored grain to lend to common people.
translations.idiomatic: To support the orphaned and destitute, he established four community granaries and stored grain to lend to common people.

sentences.zh: 縣民舊習，止知平疇種稻，高阜皆為棄壤。

translations.literal: Local custom was only to plant rice on flat fields; elevated mounds were all abandoned land.
translations.idiomatic: By local custom people planted rice only on flat fields, while higher ground was left as waste land.

sentences.zh: 因市牛具，仿北方種植法，躬督墾闢，遂享其利。

translations.literal: He therefore purchased oxen and tools, imitated northern planting methods, personally supervised reclamation, and the people soon enjoyed the benefits.
translations.idiomatic: He bought oxen and farm tools, introduced northern planting methods, personally supervised reclamation, and the people soon reaped the benefit.

sentences.zh: 尋署無為州事。

translations.literal: Soon he served as acting magistrate of Wuwei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served as acting magistrate of Wuwei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州瀕江，上下二百里，率當水沖，前人築壩四，常沒於水。

translations.literal: The prefecture bordered the river; for two hundred li upstream and downstream, areas were mostly subject to flooding. Predecessors had built four dikes, but they were often submerged.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture lay along the river, and for two hundred li upstream and downstream the banks were constantly threatened by flood. Earlier officials had built four dikes, but they were often washed away.

sentences.zh: 慶門於鮑魚橋、匋魚口二處，樹椿編竹，實土為坦坡；

translations.literal: At Baoyu Bridge and Taoyukou, Qingmen drove piles and wove bamboo, filling with earth to make gentle slopes;
translations.idiomatic: At Baoyu Bridge and Taoyukou, Qingmen drove piles, wove bamboo mats, and packed them with earth to form gentle slopes;

sentences.zh: 又取亂石填擲水中，水停沙淤，久而成洲，民免墊溺之患。

translations.literal: he also threw rubble into the water; the water slowed, sand silted up, and over time land emerged, sparing the people from being washed away and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: he also had rubble thrown into the water. The current slowed, sand accumulated, and in time new land formed, sparing the people from being swept away and drowned.

sentences.zh: 又署六安州，舊有水塘，議者欲墾塘以為田，將絕灌溉之利。

translations.literal: Again he served as acting magistrate of Lu'an Prefecture. There were old ponds; some proposed reclaiming the ponds for fields, which would cut off irrigation benefits.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as acting magistrate of Lu'an Prefecture, where old ponds stood. Some proposed converting them into fields, which would have destroyed their value for irrigation.

sentences.zh: 慶門力言於上官，事乃寢。

translations.literal: Qingmen strongly argued to his superiors, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Qingmen argued forcefully before his superiors, and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 十一年，擢亳州知府，俗悍，好群鬥，倚蠹役，表里為姦。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to prefect of Bozhou. The customs were fierce; people loved group fights and relied on corrupt runners who colluded inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to prefect of Bozhou, where the people were violent, prone to gang fights, and protected by corrupt clerks who worked with them inside and out.

sentences.zh: 慶門廉得其魁黨，先後杖遣數百人。

translations.literal: Qingmen investigated and found the ringleaders and their gangs, successively flogging and banishing several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Qingmen investigated the ringleaders and their gangs and, one after another, flogged and banished several hundred of them.

sentences.zh: 又好訟，仿古鄉約法，使之宣導排解。

translations.literal: They also loved litigation; he modeled the ancient village covenant law and had them preach and mediate disputes.
translations.idiomatic: The people were also litigious, so he revived the ancient village covenant system and had local leaders preach and mediate disputes.

sentences.zh: 勤於聽斷，日決數十事。

translations.literal: Diligent in hearing cases, he decided dozens of matters each day.
translations.idiomatic: Diligent in hearing cases, he decided dozens of suits every day.

sentences.zh: 不數月，澆風一變。

translations.literal: Within a few months, debased customs changed entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months the corrupt local ways were wholly transformed.

sentences.zh: 州瀕湖，地窪下，用秦中收淀之犁法，督民挑濬，地下者漸高，水歸其壑，農田賴焉。

translations.literal: The prefecture bordered a lake; the land was low. Using the Qin region's pond-draining plow method, he supervised the people in dredging. Lower ground gradually rose, water returned to its channels, and farmland benefited.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture bordered a lake on low ground. Using the Qin region method of draining ponds with plows, he supervised dredging until the lower land gradually rose, water returned to its proper channels, and the farmland prospered.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，服闋，以大臣薦，補四川達州知州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, when the mourning period had ended, recommended by a senior official, he was appointed magistrate of Dazhou in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qianlong reign, after his mourning ended and on the recommendation of a senior official, he was appointed magistrate of Dazhou in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 境環萬山，歲常苦旱，教民種旱稻，始無艱食之憂。

translations.literal: The territory was ringed by ten thousand mountains; every year it suffered drought. He taught the people to plant drought-resistant rice, and they finally had no worry of food shortage.
translations.idiomatic: The district was encircled by mountains and suffered drought year after year. He taught the people to plant drought-resistant rice, and at last they were freed from fear of hunger.

sentences.zh: 鄰郡巴州，桑柘素饒，乃買桑遍植，教以分繭繅絲之法，獲利與巴州等。

translations.literal: Neighboring Bazhou was rich in mulberry and paper mulberry; he bought mulberry trees and planted them widely, teaching methods of separating cocoons and reeling silk, and profits equaled those of Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring Bazhou was rich in mulberry and paper mulberry, so he bought mulberry trees, planted them widely, and taught the people how to sort cocoons and reel silk until their profits matched those of Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 時川東多流民，官廩不給，遂釐剔腴田之被隱佔者，為義產以贍之，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: At the time eastern Sichuan had many displaced people and official granaries could not supply them; he investigated and reclaimed fertile fields that had been concealed and encroached upon, establishing charitable estates to support them, and saved many lives.
translations.idiomatic: At the time eastern Sichuan was full of displaced people and the official granaries could not feed them. He investigated concealed encroachments on fertile land, set up charitable estates to support the refugees, and saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 建宣漢書院，聘名流教授，文風漸振。

translations.literal: He built the Xuanhan Academy, hired renowned scholars to teach, and literary culture gradually revived.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the Xuanhan Academy, engaged distinguished scholars to teach there, and local literary culture gradually revived.

sentences.zh: 未幾，乞病歸。

translations.literal: Before long he requested leave citing illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he asked to retire on grounds of illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 著仕學一貫錄，世以儒吏稱之。

translations.literal: He authored Records of Consistent Learning in Office and Study, and the world called him a Confucian official.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Records of Consistent Learning in Office and Study, and posterity honored him as a Confucian official.

sentences.zh: =週人龍=週人龍，字云上，直隸天津人。

translations.literal: Zhou Renlong. Zhou Renlong, courtesy name Yunshang, was a native of Tianjin in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Renlong, courtesy name Yunshang, was a native of Tianjin in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十八年進士，授山西屯留知縣。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the forty-eighth year of Kangxi, he was appointed magistrate of Tunliu in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in the forty-eighth year of the Kangxi reign, he was appointed magistrate of Tunliu in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 興學賑荒，有聲。

translations.literal: He promoted education and relief during famine and gained renown.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted education and famine relief and won a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 調清源，境內洞渦、嶑峪諸河入汾，常有水患，濬渠築堰，民賴之。

translations.literal: Transferred to Qingyuan; within its borders the Dongwo, Gaoyu, and other rivers entered the Fen and frequently caused floods. He dredged channels and built dikes, and the people relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Qingyuan, he found that the Dongwo, Gaoyu, and other rivers within the district emptied into the Fen and caused frequent floods. He dredged channels and built dikes, to the people's great benefit.

sentences.zh: 歷忻州直隸州知州、蒲州知府。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Xinzhou Direct Prefecture and prefect of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as magistrate of Xinzhou Direct Prefecture and prefect of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 蒲郡瀕黃河，河水遷徙無常。

translations.literal: Puzhou bordered the Yellow River; the river's course shifted constantly.
translations.idiomatic: Puzhou bordered the Yellow River, whose course shifted without warning.

sentences.zh: 山、陝兩省民隔河爭地，訟數十年不結。

translations.literal: People of Shanxi and Shaanxi provinces disputed land across the river, and lawsuits went unresolved for decades.
translations.idiomatic: People of Shanxi and Shaanxi disputed land across the river, and lawsuits dragged on unresolved for decades.

sentences.zh: 人龍請於大吏曰：「臨河灘地，當以河為界。

translations.literal: Renlong petitioned the senior officials, saying, "For riverside beach land, the river should serve as the boundary.
translations.idiomatic: Renlong petitioned the senior officials, saying, "For land along the river's edge, the river itself should be the boundary.

sentences.zh: 河東遷，則山西無地之糧歸陝西；

translations.literal: When the river shifts east, Shanxi's landless grain tax goes to Shaanxi;
translations.idiomatic: When the river shifts east, grain tax owed on land that no longer exists in Shanxi should go to Shaanxi;

sentences.zh: 河西遷，則陝西無地之糧歸山西。

translations.literal: when the river shifts west, Shaanxi's landless grain tax goes to Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: when it shifts west, grain tax owed on land that no longer exists in Shaanxi should go to Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 糧隨地起，不缺正賦。

translations.literal: Grain tax follows the land; regular tax levies are not shortchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Tax follows the land, and the regular levy is never shorted.

sentences.zh: 因地納糧，無累民生。

translations.literal: According to the land, grain is paid in; the people's livelihood is not burdened.
translations.idiomatic: Grain dues would follow the land itself, without burdening people's livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 山、陝沿河二千餘裡，凡兩省湮沒之地，令地方官照糧查地，按地過糧。

translations.literal: Along more than two thousand li of the Shanxi and Shaanxi riverbanks, for all submerged land in the two provinces, local officials are to investigate land according to grain registers and transfer grain obligations according to the land.
translations.idiomatic: Along more than two thousand li of the Shanxi and Shaanxi riverbanks, for all submerged lands in both provinces, local officials should trace holdings according to existing grain registers and reassign tax obligations to match the actual land.

sentences.zh: 除鹵咸者照例題請免徵，其餘水退之地，招令沿河民認糧承種，庶事無偏枯，爭訟可息。

translations.literal: Except for saline land, which is to be memorialized for exemption as usual, the rest of the land where waters have receded is to be offered to riverside people to accept grain obligations and undertake cultivation, so that matters will not be one-sided, and lawsuits can cease.
translations.idiomatic: Saline tracts would be memorialized for exemption as usual; all other lands reclaimed as the waters receded would be offered to riverside farmers to accept the attached grain dues and take up cultivation — so that neither province would be unfairly burdened and the endless lawsuits might finally cease.

sentences.zh: 」大吏從其議，至今便之。

translations.literal: "The high officials followed his proposal; to this day it has been convenient."
translations.idiomatic: The provincial authorities adopted his proposal, and the arrangement has served well ever since.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，有言丁糧歸地，便於無力之丁，不便於有田之家。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongzheng, some said that merging poll tax with land tax would benefit ding without means but would inconvenience households with fields.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongzheng reign, critics argued that merging the poll tax into the land tax would help landless commoners but would disadvantage families who owned fields.

sentences.zh: 人龍駁之，略曰：「有田者，尚以輸納為艱，豈無田者反易？

translations.literal: Renlong refuted this, saying in summary: "Those with fields already find payment difficult — could those without fields find it easier instead?"
translations.idiomatic: Renlong rebutted them, writing in essence: "If even landowners already struggle to meet their tax payments, how could those with no land find the burden easier?"

sentences.zh: 君子平其政，焉得人人而悅之？

translations.literal: The noble person balances his governance — how can he please every single person?
translations.idiomatic: "A gentleman sets policy straight — he cannot please every individual."

sentences.zh: 今不悅者，不過紳衿富戶；

translations.literal: Those displeased now are no more than gentry and wealthy households;
translations.idiomatic: Those displeased today are only the gentry and wealthy households;

sentences.zh: 而大悅者，乃在煢煢無告之小民。

translations.literal: while those greatly pleased are the isolated common people with none to plead for them.
translations.idiomatic: while those who rejoice most are the poorest commoners, alone and without anyone to speak for them.

sentences.zh: 若因其控告而不行，則豪強得志，而窮民終於無告。

translations.literal: If because of their complaints it is not carried out, then the powerful will have their way, and the poor will ultimately have none to plead for them.
translations.idiomatic: If the reform were abandoned because of their complaints, the powerful would triumph and the poor would remain utterly without recourse.

sentences.zh: 此議在當日未行則已耳，今行之數年，勢難中止。

translations.literal: This proposal, if not carried out at the time, would have been one thing; now that it has been in effect for several years, it would be hard to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Had the policy never been adopted, that would be one matter; but now that it has been in force for several years, it would be difficult to stop.

sentences.zh: 窮民狃於數年樂利，必不安於一旦變更。

translations.literal: The poor, accustomed to several years of benefit, would certainly not be at ease with sudden change.
translations.idiomatic: The poor, having grown accustomed to years of relief, would not accept a sudden reversal.

sentences.zh: 且富民少而窮民多，不當以彼易此。

translations.literal: Moreover, the wealthy are few and the poor many — one should not exchange this for that.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the wealthy are few and the poor are many — one must not sacrifice the many for the few.

sentences.zh: 」議上，事乃定。

translations.literal: "When the memorial was submitted, the matter was settled."
translations.idiomatic: When his memorial reached the throne, the matter was decided.

sentences.zh: 以憂去官。

translations.literal: He left office on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn a parent.

sentences.zh: 服闋，補湖北安陸。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed to Anlu in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, he was posted to Anlu in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 數月，擢江西督糧道，未行，江水決鍾祥三官廟堤及天門沙溝垸，招集鄰縣民，諭以利害，同築禦。

translations.literal: Several months later he was promoted to grain commissioner of Jiangxi, but before he departed, the Yangtze burst the dikes at the Three Officials' Temple in Zhongxiang and at Shagou Yuan in Tianmen; he summoned people from neighboring counties, explained the stakes, and together they built defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he was promoted to grain intendant of Jiangxi, but before he could leave, the Yangtze breached the dikes at the Three Officials' Temple in Zhongxiang and at Shagou Yuan in Tianmen. He summoned laborers from neighboring counties, explained what was at stake, and led them in building defenses together.

sentences.zh: 踴躍荷畚鍤至者數万人，親冒風雨，率以施工。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands eagerly came bearing hoes and shovels; he personally braved wind and rain and led the work.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands came eagerly bearing hoes and shovels; he personally braved wind and rain to direct the work.

sentences.zh: 或勸其「已遷官，何自苦」，人龍曰：「助夫由我招至，我去即散矣。

translations.literal: Some urged him, "You have already been transferred — why trouble yourself?" Renlong said, "The laborers were summoned by me; if I leave, they will disperse at once.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him: "You have already been transferred — why torment yourself?" Renlong replied: "I summoned these workers; if I leave, they will disperse at once.

sentences.zh: 伏汛一至，民何以堪？

translations.literal: When the summer flood arrives, how can the people bear it?"
translations.idiomatic: When the summer flood arrives, how will the people endure it?"

sentences.zh: 」閱兩月工成，安陸人屍祝之。

translations.literal: "After two months the work was finished, and the people of Anlu worshipped him as a departed spirit."
translations.idiomatic: Two months later the work was complete, and the people of Anlu venerated him as they would a tutelary spirit.

sentences.zh: 江西漕糧徵運素多弊，嚴立規條，宿蠹一清。

translations.literal: Grain transport and collection in Jiangxi had long been rife with abuses; he strictly established regulations, and longstanding corruption was completely cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Transport and collection of grain tribute in Jiangxi had long been riddled with abuses; he imposed strict regulations and swept away entrenched corruption.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十年，乞病歸，卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Qianlong he requested leave on grounds of illness and returned home, then died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Qianlong reign (1745), he retired on grounds of illness and died at home.

sentences.zh: =童華=童華，字心樸，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Tong Hua. Tong Hua, courtesy name Xinpu, was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Hua. Tong Hua, courtesy name Xinpu, was from Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 年未冠為諸生，長習名法家言，出佐郡邑治。

translations.literal: Before he came of age he became a licentiate; as he grew up he studied the legalists and went out to assist in county and prefectural governance.
translations.idiomatic: He became a licentiate before coming of age; as he matured he studied legalist administrative practice and went out to assist in local government.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，入貲為知縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongzheng, he purchased appointment as county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongzheng reign he purchased appointment as a county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 時方修律例，大學士硃軾薦其才，世宗召見，命察賑直隸。

translations.literal: At the time the legal code was being revised; Grand Secretary Zhu Shi recommended his talent; the Emperor Shizong summoned him and ordered him to inspect famine relief in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: While the legal code was being revised, Grand Secretary Zhu Shi recommended his abilities; the Yongzheng Emperor summoned him and sent him to inspect famine relief in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 樂亭、盧龍兩縣報飢口不實，華倍增其數。

translations.literal: Leting and Lulong counties reported famine victims inaccurately; Hua doubled their numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Leting and Lulong counties had underreported the number of famine victims; Hua doubled their figures.

sentences.zh: 怡賢親王與硃軾治營田水利，至永平，問灤河形勢，華對甚晰，王器之。

translations.literal: Prince Yixian and Zhu Shi were managing reclamation and waterworks; when they reached Yongping and asked about the lay of the Luan River, Hua answered with great clarity, and the prince valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yixian and Zhu Shi were overseeing land reclamation and waterworks; when they reached Yongping and inquired about the Luan River, Hua answered with such clarity that the prince took him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 尋授平山知縣，邑災，不待報，遽出倉粟七千石貸民。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed magistrate of Pingshan; when the county suffered disaster, without awaiting approval he immediately released seven thousand shi of grain from the granary to lend to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed magistrate of Pingshan; when disaster struck the county, he immediately released seven thousand shi of grain from the public granary to lend to the people, without waiting for authorization.

sentences.zh: 擢真定知府，權按察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to prefect of Zhending and served concurrently as acting surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Zhending and concurrently served as acting surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以前在平山發粟事，部議免官，特詔原之。

translations.literal: On account of his earlier release of grain at Pingshan, the Board recommended dismissal, but an especial edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his unauthorized grain release at Pingshan, the Board recommended his dismissal, but the emperor issued a special edict pardoning him.

sentences.zh: 怡賢親王奏以華理京南局水利，華度真定城外得泉十八，疏為渠，溉田六百畝，先後營田三百餘頃。

translations.literal: Prince Yixian memorialized to have Hua manage waterworks for the Southern Bureau; Hua surveyed outside Zhending city and found eighteen springs, dredged channels, irrigated six hundred mu of fields, and successively reclaimed more than three hundred qing of land.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yixian memorialized to put Hua in charge of Southern Bureau waterworks; Hua surveyed outside Zhending and found eighteen springs, dredged them into irrigation channels covering six hundred mu, and over time reclaimed more than three hundred qing of land.

sentences.zh: 滏陽河發源磁州，州民欲獨擅其利。

translations.literal: The Fuyang River rises in Cizhou; the people of the prefecture wished to monopolize its benefits.
translations.idiomatic: The Fuyang River rises in Cizhou, whose residents sought to monopolize its water.

sentences.zh: 自春徂秋，閉閘蓄水，下游永年、曲周滴涓不得。

translations.literal: From spring through autumn they closed the sluice gates to store water; downstream, Yongnian and Quzhou received not even a trickle.
translations.idiomatic: From spring through autumn they closed the sluice gates to hoard the water, so that downstream Yongnian and Quzhou received scarcely a drop.

sentences.zh: 時改州歸直隸，以便控制。

translations.literal: At the time the prefecture was transferred to Zhili to facilitate control.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had recently been transferred to Zhili to make control easier.

sentences.zh: 華建議仿唐李泌、明湯紹恩西湖三江兩閘遺規，計板放水，數縣爭水之端永息。

translations.literal: Hua proposed following the legacy regulations of Li Bi of Tang and Tang Shao'en of Ming for the West Lake's Three Rivers and Two Sluices, using measured board releases of water, so that the disputes over water among several counties would cease forever.
translations.idiomatic: Hua proposed following the Tang precedent of Li Bi and the Ming precedent of Tang Shao'en at West Lake — regulating release by sluice boards — so that water disputes among the counties would end for good.

sentences.zh: 華又以北人不食稻，請發錢買水田穀運通倉，省漕費，民得市稷黍以為食，從之。

translations.literal: Hua also, because northerners do not eat rice, requested funds to buy rice from paddy fields and transport it to the Tong Granary, saving transport costs, so the people could buy millet and sorghum for food; his request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Hua also argued that northerners did not eat rice, and requested funds to purchase paddy grain for transport to the Tong Granary, saving tribute transport costs so that people could buy millet and sorghum instead; the proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 調江蘇蘇州，會清查康熙五十一年以來江蘇負課千二百餘萬，巡撫督責急，逮捕追比無虛日，華固請寬之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Suzhou in Jiangsu; it happened that an audit found Jiangsu owed more than twelve million in taxes since the fifty-first year of Kangxi; the governor-general pressed urgently, and arrests and collection pursued daily without respite; Hua firmly requested leniency.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Suzhou in Jiangsu just as an audit revealed more than twelve million taels in back taxes accumulated since the fifty-first year of Kangxi. The governor-general pressed the recovery urgently, with arrests and coercive collection day after day; Hua firmly petitioned for leniency.

sentences.zh: 巡撫怒曰：「汝敢逆旨耶？

translations.literal: The governor-general angrily said, "Do you dare defy the imperial command?"
translations.idiomatic: The governor-general fumed: "Do you dare defy the imperial will?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「華非逆旨，乃遵旨也，上知有積欠，不命嚴追而命清查，正欲晰其來歷，查其委曲，或在官，或在役，或在民，或應徵，或應免，了然分曉，奏請上裁，乃稱詔書意。

translations.literal: He replied, "Hua is not defying the command but obeying it. The emperor, knowing there are accumulated arrears, did not order harsh collection but ordered an audit — precisely to clarify their origins and investigate the details, whether they lie with officials, clerks, or commoners, whether they should be collected or exempted, making everything clear and distinct, then memorializing for the emperor's decision — that is what the edict intends.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "I am not defying the emperor but following him. His Majesty, knowing of these arrears, did not order harsh collection but an audit — precisely to trace their origins and examine the circumstances: whether the debt lies with officials, clerks, or commoners; whether it should be collected or remitted. Only when everything is clear should we memorialize for the throne's decision — that is the edict's intent.

sentences.zh: 今奉行者不顧名思義，徒以十五年積欠立求完納，是暴徵，非清查也。

translations.literal: Those carrying it out now ignore the name and meaning, merely demanding immediate full payment of fifteen years of accumulated arrears — this is violent collection, not audit.
translations.idiomatic: Those implementing the order ignore what 'audit' actually means and simply demand immediate payment of fifteen years of arrears — that is extortion, not investigation.

sentences.zh: 今請寬三月限，當部居別白，分牒以報。

translations.literal: I now request a three-month extension; within the department I will sort and clarify matters and dispatch reports separately.
translations.idiomatic: Grant me three months, and I will sort out each case within the department and report separately.

sentences.zh: 」巡撫從其請，乃盡釋獄系千餘人，次第造冊請奏。

translations.literal: "The governor-general acceded to his request, then released more than a thousand prisoners and successively compiled registers to memorialize."
translations.idiomatic: The governor-general granted his request, released more than a thousand prisoners, and began compiling registers for memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷亦聞江南清查不善，下詔切責，如華言。

translations.literal: At the time the court also heard that the Jiangnan audit was poorly conducted and issued an edict sternly censuring it, just as Hua had said.
translations.idiomatic: The court had likewise heard that the Jiangnan audit was being mishandled and issued an edict of stern rebuke — just as Hua had argued.

sentences.zh: 浙江總督李衛嘗捕人於蘇，華以無牒不與，衛怒，蜚語上聞。

translations.literal: Zhejiang Governor-General Li Wei once came to Suzhou to arrest someone; Hua refused without an official warrant; Wei was angry and spread slanderous reports to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang Governor-General Li Wei once came to Suzhou to seize someone; Hua refused without an official warrant. Wei was furious and sent slanderous reports to the throne.

sentences.zh: 世宗召見，責以沽名幹譽，對曰：「臣竭力為國，近沽名；

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong summoned him and rebuked him for courting reputation; he replied, "Your subject strives with all his strength for the state — that resembles courting reputation;
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Emperor summoned him and accused him of courting fame. He replied: "In serving the state with all my strength, I may appear to court fame;

sentences.zh: 實心為民，近幹譽。

translations.literal: in sincerely serving the people — that resembles courting reputation."
translations.idiomatic: in serving the people with a true heart, I may appear to invite praise."

sentences.zh: 」上意解，命往陝西以知府用。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was eased and he ordered him to Shaanxi to serve as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger softened, and he sent Hua to Shaanxi as prefect.

sentences.zh: 署肅州，佐經略鄂爾泰屯田事，鑿通九家窯五山，引水穿渠，溉田萬頃。

translations.literal: He served as acting prefect of Suzhou Prefecture, assisted Commissioner-General Ortai in land reclamation, opened through Jiujia Yao and Wushan, led water through channels, and irrigated ten thousand qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: As acting prefect of Suzhou in Gansu, he assisted Commissioner-General Ortai in land reclamation, opening Jiujia Yao and Wushan, cutting channels to bring in water, and irrigating ten thousand qing of land.

sentences.zh: 以忤巡撫被劾罷官。

translations.literal: Because he offended the governor-general he was impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He offended the governor-general, was impeached, and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，起福州知府，調漳州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was recalled as prefect of Fuzhou and transferred to Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qianlong reign (1736) he was recalled as prefect of Fuzhou and then transferred to Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 頗好長生術，招集方士，習丹家言，复劾罷歸。

translations.literal: He was rather fond of immortality arts, gathered alchemists, studied alchemical doctrines, and was again impeached and dismissed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He grew fond of immortality practices, gathered alchemists, and studied elixir lore — and was again impeached and sent home.

sentences.zh: 數年卒。

translations.literal: Several years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died several years later.

sentences.zh: 華剛而忤時，屢起屢蹶。

translations.literal: Hua was upright and at odds with the times; he was repeatedly raised and repeatedly cast down.
translations.idiomatic: Hua was upright and defiant of the times; he rose and fell again and again.

sentences.zh: 在蘇州，民德之尤深，以比明知府況鍾。

translations.literal: In Suzhou the people esteemed him especially deeply, comparing him to the wise prefect Kuang Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: In Suzhou the people revered him above all others, comparing him to the renowned Ming prefect Kuang Zhong.

sentences.zh: 當世宗治畿輔營田時，所用者多一時賢守令，有黃世發，名與華相媲雲。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong managed reclamation in the capital region, those employed were mostly worthy magistrates and prefects of the time; there was Huang Shifa, whose fame rivaled Hua's.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongzheng Emperor promoted land reclamation in the capital region, he drew on many capable local officials of the day — among them Huang Shifa, whose reputation matched Hua's.

sentences.zh: 世發，字成憲，貴州印江人。

translations.literal: Shifa, courtesy name Chengxian, was a native of Yinjiang in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Shifa, courtesy name Chengxian, was from Yinjiang in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十五年舉人，授直隸肅寧知縣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Kangxi he passed the provincial examination and was appointed magistrate of Sunning in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the thirty-fifth year of the Kangxi reign (1696) and was appointed magistrate of Sunning in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 舊例，錢糧加一二作耗銀，世發亦收之而不自用，雜派畝銀三四錢悉除之。

translations.literal: By old custom, one or two parts were added to grain and cash taxes as meltage silver; Shifa also collected it but did not use it himself, and completely abolished miscellaneous per-mu levies of three or four cash.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, one or two parts were added to tax payments as meltage silver; Shifa collected this surcharge but never kept it for himself, and abolished all miscellaneous per-mu levies of three or four cash.

sentences.zh: 縣有役事，若修學校、繕城垣及上官別有攤派，即以耗銀應。

translations.literal: When the county had corvée duties such as repairing schools, city walls, or other assignments from superiors, he met them with the meltage silver.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the county faced labor obligations — repairing schools or city walls, or other assignments from superiors — he covered the costs from the meltage fund.

sentences.zh: 河間府檄修府城，親齎餱糧，出錢僱役，不以擾社甲。

translations.literal: When Hejian Prefecture ordered repairs to the prefectural city, he personally brought provisions, paid for hired labor, and did not disturb the community registers.
translations.idiomatic: When Hejian Prefecture ordered repairs to the prefectural city, he personally brought provisions, hired labor with his own funds, and never shifted the burden onto the community tithing registers.

sentences.zh: 視民如家人，教以生計。

translations.literal: He regarded the people as his own family and taught them livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: He treated the people as his own family and taught them how to make a living.

sentences.zh: 坑鹼荒地，令穿井耕種。

translations.literal: On saline wasteland he had wells dug for cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: On alkaline wasteland he had wells dug so that farming could begin.

sentences.zh: 綠城植桑柳樹萬株，凡水車、蠶箔、糞灌、紡績，悉為經畫。

translations.literal: He planted ten thousand mulberry and willow trees around the city; water wheels, sericulture trays, manure irrigation, and spinning — he planned them all.
translations.idiomatic: He planted ten thousand mulberry and willow trees around the city walls and systematically organized water wheels, silkworm trays, fertilization, irrigation, and spinning.

sentences.zh: 復辟護城廢地，穿池種稻以導之。

translations.literal: He also reopened waste land around the city walls, dug ponds and planted rice to guide it.
translations.idiomatic: He reclaimed abandoned land within the moat, dug ponds, and planted rice to improve the soil.

sentences.zh: 建社學，教以孝親敬長，贖官田九十餘畝，以其租為學者膏火。

translations.literal: He built a community school teaching filial piety and respect for elders, redeemed more than ninety mu of official land, and used its rent as stipends for students.
translations.idiomatic: He founded a community school to teach filial piety and respect for elders, redeemed more than ninety mu of official land, and used the rent to fund students' lamp oil and supplies.

sentences.zh: 旬三日集諸生講學會文，士有自鄰縣來學者。

translations.literal: Every ten days he gathered students for lectures and composition meetings; scholars came from neighboring counties to study.
translations.idiomatic: Every ten days he gathered scholars for lectures and composition exercises; students came from neighboring counties to study.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年，水災，大吏遣官履勘，世發不能得其意，被劾罷。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongzheng there was a flood disaster; the high officials sent officials to inspect on site; Shifa could not grasp their intent and was impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Yongzheng reign a flood struck; senior officials sent investigators, and Shifa, failing to satisfy them, was impeached and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 士民呼籥挽留，特詔复官，加四品銜。

translations.literal: Scholars and common people petitioned to retain him; a special edict restored him to office and added a fourth-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and commoners clamored to keep him; a special edict restored him to office and granted him fourth-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 已，晉授按察使兼直隸營田觀察使，巡行勸民農桑，察水利可興者。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to surveillance commissioner and concurrently Zhili land-reclamation intendant, touring to encourage agriculture and sericulture and inspecting waterworks that could be developed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to surveillance commissioner and concurrently Zhili land-reclamation intendant, touring the region to promote farming and sericulture and to identify waterworks worth developing.

sentences.zh: 所至剴切宣諭，民多興起。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he earnestly proclaimed and instructed, and many among the people took action.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went he preached earnestly, and the people responded in large numbers.

sentences.zh: 修堤墾田，變汙下為沃壤。

translations.literal: He repaired dikes and reclaimed fields, transforming low wetland into fertile soil.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired dikes, reclaimed land, and turned foul low ground into rich farmland.

sentences.zh: 最後開易州水峪田，經營年餘，以勞卒。

translations.literal: Finally he opened fields at Shuiyu in Yizhou; after more than a year of effort he died from overwork.
translations.idiomatic: His last project was opening farmland at Shuiyu in Yizhou; after more than a year of labor he died from exhaustion.

sentences.zh: =李渭=李渭，字菉涯，直隸高邑人。

translations.literal: Li Wei. Li Wei, courtesy name Lüya, was a native of Gaoyi in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei. Li Wei, courtesy name Lüya, was from Gaoyi in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 父兆齡，康熙中官福建閩清知縣，以廉能稱。

translations.literal: His father Zhaoling served as magistrate of Minqing in Fujian during Kangxi and was known for integrity and ability.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhaoling had served as magistrate of Minqing in Fujian during the Kangxi reign and was known for integrity and competence.

sentences.zh: 渭，康熙六十年進士，授內閣中書，遷刑部主事。

translations.literal: Wei, in the sixtieth year of Kangxi a jinshi, was appointed secretary in the Grand Secretariat and transferred to a clerkship in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Wei received his jinshi degree in the sixtieth year of the Kangxi reign (1721), was appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat, and was later transferred to a clerkship in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，出為湖南岳州知府，詔許密摺奏事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng he went out as prefect of Yuezhou in Hunan; an edict permitted him to submit secret memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Yongzheng reign (1724) he was appointed prefect of Yuezhou in Hunan, with permission to submit secret memorials directly to the throne.

sentences.zh: 忤大吏，左遷武昌府同知，未之任，丁母憂。

translations.literal: He offended the high officials, was demoted to sub-prefect of Wuchang, but before taking up the post mourned his mother.
translations.idiomatic: After offending senior officials he was demoted to sub-prefect of Wuchang, but before assuming the post he left to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，授四川嘉定知府，復以爭冤獄忤上官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed prefect of Jiading in Sichuan, and again for contesting an unjust case offended his superiors.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he was appointed prefect of Jiading in Sichuan, and again offended his superiors by contesting a wrongful conviction.

sentences.zh: 渭曰：「吾官可棄，殺人媚人不為也。

translations.literal: Wei said, "I can abandon my office, but I will not kill men to please others."
translations.idiomatic: Wei declared: "I would surrender my office, but I will not execute the innocent to please my superiors."

sentences.zh: 」奉檄賑重慶水災，多所全活。

translations.literal: Ordered to relieve the Chongqing flood disaster, he saved many lives.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatched to relieve the Chongqing flood, he saved many lives.

sentences.zh: 父憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 後補河南彰德，萬金渠源出善應山，環府城，入洹河，灌田千數百頃，山水暴發易淤。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed to Zhangde in Henan; the Wanjin Canal rises at Shanying Mountain, encircles the prefectural city, enters the Huan River, irrigates more than a thousand qing of fields, and is easily silted when mountain waters surge.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was posted to Zhangde in Henan. The Wanjin Canal rose on Mount Shanying, wound around the prefectural city, and emptied into the Huan River, irrigating more than a thousand qing — but flash floods from the hills silting it easily.

sentences.zh: 渭履勘濬治，增開支河，建閘啟閉，定各村分日用水，歲以有秋。

translations.literal: Wei inspected on foot, dredged and repaired, opened branch channels, built sluice gates for opening and closing, fixed each village's allotted days for water use, and the harvests were good every year.
translations.idiomatic: Wei surveyed the canal on foot, dredged and repaired it, opened branch channels, built sluice gates, allotted each village its days for drawing water — and the region enjoyed good harvests year after year.

sentences.zh: 漳河當孔道，舊設草橋於臨漳，道回遠，移於豐樂鎮，行旅便之。

translations.literal: The Zhang River lay on a major route; a pontoon bridge had been set at Linzhang on a roundabout path; he moved it to Fengle Town, and travelers found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang River crossed a major thoroughfare; a pontoon bridge had stood at Linzhang on a roundabout route. He moved it to Fengle Town, to travelers' great convenience.

sentences.zh: 雪武安民班某誣殺族兄獄。

translations.literal: He cleared a Mr. Ban of Wu'an who had been falsely accused of killing a clansman.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared a man surnamed Ban in Wu'an who had been falsely convicted of murdering a clansman.

sentences.zh: 林縣富室毆人死，賂屍屬以病死報。

translations.literal: In Lin County a wealthy man beat someone to death and bribed the corpse's kin to report death by illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Lin County a wealthy man beat someone to death and bribed the victim's family to report the death as illness.

sentences.zh: 渭驗屍腿骨盡碎，治如律。

translations.literal: Wei examined the corpse — the leg bones were entirely shattered — and punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Wei examined the corpse, found the leg bones shattered, and punished the killer according to law.

sentences.zh: 舉卓異。

translations.literal: He was recommended as outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended as an outstanding official.

sentences.zh: 乾隆九年，擢山東鹽運使，時議增鹽引，渭以增引則商不能賠，必增鹽價，商、民且兩病，持不可。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Qianlong he was promoted to salt transport commissioner of Shandong; at the time there was discussion of increasing salt quotas; Wei held that if quotas increased merchants could not cover costs and salt prices would have to rise, harming both merchants and people, and maintained it should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Qianlong reign (1744) he was promoted to salt transport commissioner of Shandong. When officials proposed raising salt quotas, Wei argued that merchants could not absorb the cost and prices would rise — harming both merchants and the public — and refused to agree.

sentences.zh: 十二年，山東大水，大吏檄渭勘災，至益都、博興、樂安​​諸縣，餓莩載途，而有司先以未成災報，已入告，難之；

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Shandong suffered great flood; the high officials ordered Wei to inspect the disaster; arriving at Yidu, Boxing, Le'an and other counties, starving corpses filled the roads, but the local officials had first reported that disaster had not yet formed and had already memorialized upward, making it difficult;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year (1747) a great flood struck Shandong. Senior officials ordered Wei to survey the damage. In Yidu, Boxing, Le'an, and other counties, corpses of the starved lined the roads — yet local officials had already reported that no disaster had occurred, and their memorials were on record, which made corrective action awkward.

sentences.zh: 乃請以藉作賑，異日免追，民乃蘇。

translations.literal: He then requested using the registers for relief, with exemption from repayment later, and the people revived.
translations.idiomatic: He requested distributing relief through the tax registers, with repayment waived afterward, and the people were saved.

sentences.zh: 十三年，就遷按察使，折獄平。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promptly transferred to surveillance commissioner; his judgments in cases were fair.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to surveillance commissioner; his rulings were even-handed.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「古人言求其生而不得，今俗吏移易獄詞，何求生不得之有？

translations.literal: He once said, "The ancients spoke of seeking to preserve life but failing to obtain it; today vulgar officials alter case records — where is the failure to obtain life?"
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "The ancients spoke of striving to preserve a man's life yet failing; today corrupt officials simply alter trial records — where is the struggle to save life?"

sentences.zh: 然如死者何！

translations.literal: But what of the dead!
translations.idiomatic: But what of the dead!

sentences.zh: 此婦寺之仁，非持法之正。

translations.literal: This is the kindness of women and eunuchs, not the rectitude of upholding the law.
translations.idiomatic: That is the mercy of the weak-hearted, not the justice of the law.

sentences.zh: 尋遷安徽布政使，禁革徵糧長單差催法，以杜詭寄。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to administrative commissioner of Anhui, abolished the practice of grain-tax chiefs and runner collection, and stopped fraudulent registration of tax liability.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to administrative commissioner of Anhui, abolished the grain-tax chief and runner collection system, and curbed fraudulent tax registration.

sentences.zh: 調山東，墾荒，令客民帶完舊欠，免鄰保代賠逃戶之累，民便之。

translations.literal: Transferred to Shandong, he promoted land reclamation, requiring migrant settlers to settle old arrears while exempting neighboring guarantors from covering absconded households — the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Shandong, he promoted land reclamation, requiring migrant settlers to clear old arrears while freeing neighboring guarantors from liability for absconded households — to the people's great relief.

sentences.zh: 為政持大體，不吝出納，不輕揭一官，馭吏嚴而不念舊過。

translations.literal: In governing he grasped the larger principles, was not stingy with disbursements, did not lightly impeach a single official, and managed subordinates strictly without dwelling on old faults.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with an eye to essentials, spent freely when the public good required it, impeached no official on slight grounds, and kept his staff in strict order while refusing to nurse old grudges.

sentences.zh: 十九年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of his reign he died at his post.

sentences.zh: 子經芳，乾隆中官至湖北施南知府，亦廉謹守其家風。

translations.literal: His son Jingfang, during the Qianlong reign rose to prefect of Shinan in Hubei, likewise maintaining the family's tradition of integrity and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingfang, under Qianlong, rose to prefect of Shinan in Hubei and upheld the same frugal, upright household tradition.

sentences.zh: =謝仲坃=謝仲坃，字孔六，廣東陽春人。

translations.literal: Xie Zhongxun. Xie Zhongxun, courtesy name Kongliu, was a native of Yangchun in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zhongxun. Xie Zhongxun, styled Kongliu, was from Yangchun in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年舉人，登明通榜。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate in the first year of Yongzheng, he passed the secondary Mingtong examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examinations in the first year of Yongzheng (1723) and was placed on the Mingtong supplementary list.

sentences.zh: 初官長寧教諭，乾隆初，擢授湖南常寧知縣，峻卻餽遺。

translations.literal: His first post was instructor at Changning; at the beginning of Qianlong he was promoted to magistrate of Changning in Hunan, sternly refusing gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He began as an instructor at Changning; early in Qianlong he was promoted to magistrate of Changning in Hunan, where he flatly refused all presents.

sentences.zh: 履鄉自裹行糧，嚼生萊菔供饌。

translations.literal: On tours of the countryside he carried his own travel rations, chewing raw radishes for meals.
translations.idiomatic: When touring the district he carried his own provisions and ate raw radishes to get by.

sentences.zh: 月兩課士，以節行相勸勉。

translations.literal: Twice monthly he examined the scholars, exhorting them on integrity and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Twice each month he tested the local scholars and urged them toward moral discipline.

sentences.zh: 調平江，再調衡陽。

translations.literal: Transferred to Pingjiang, then again to Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Pingjiang, and then to Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 前令李澎徵漕米浮收斛面，糧儲道謝濟世發其奸。

translations.literal: The previous magistrate Li Peng overcharged on tribute grain by inflating the measuring surface; grain commissioner Xie Jishi exposed the fraud.
translations.idiomatic: The former magistrate Li Peng had skimmed tribute grain by padding the measure; Grain Intendant Xie Jishi uncovered the scheme.

sentences.zh: 時巡撫許容方以浮收誣劾濟世，總督孫嘉淦亦徇巡撫意，故濟世與澎並免。

translations.literal: At the time Governor-General Xu Rong was framing Xie Jishi with false charges of overcharging; Governor Sun Jiagan also followed the governor-general's wishes, so both Xie Jishi and Li Peng were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Xu Rong was then falsely impeaching Xie Jishi for the same overcharging, and Governor Sun Jiagan went along; both Xie Jishi and Li Peng lost their posts.

sentences.zh: 言官論奏，朝命侍郎阿里袞往按。

translations.literal: Censorial officials memorialized on the matter; the court ordered Vice Minister Ali Gun to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials debated the case in memorials, and the throne dispatched Vice Minister Ali Gun to conduct an inquiry.

sentences.zh: 署糧道倉德又因布政使函囑改換衡陽浮收詳文，據以上揭，詔責切究。

translations.literal: Acting grain commissioner Cang De, at the administrative commissioner's written request, altered the Hengyang overcharge report and submitted it upward; the emperor decreed a thorough investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Grain Intendant Cang De, on written orders from the provincial treasurer, rewrote the Hengyang overcharge report and forwarded it upward; the emperor ordered a rigorous investigation.

sentences.zh: 事急，澎則盡出賄贈簿以脅上官，阿里袞重興大獄，欲出澎浮收罪，與濟世俱复官。

translations.literal: As the case grew urgent, Li Peng produced his bribery ledger to blackmail his superiors; Ali Gun reopened a major prosecution, seeking to clear Li Peng of overcharging and restore both him and Xie Jishi to office.
translations.idiomatic: When matters came to a head, Li Peng produced his ledger of bribes to intimidate his superiors; Ali Gun reopened the case on a grand scale, aiming to absolve Li Peng of overcharging and restore both men to office.

sentences.zh: 仲坃乃重治澎丁役，以決罰過當被劾罷官。

translations.literal: Zhongxun then severely punished Li Peng's runners and retainers; for excessive sentencing he was impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxun thereupon punished Li Peng's runners and retainers with unusual severity; impeached for excessive penalties, he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 逾年，特起為衡山知縣。

translations.literal: A year later he was specially recalled as magistrate of Hengshan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was specially recalled to serve as magistrate of Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 以讞巴陵獄，巡撫與按察使互奏，奉旨引見，擢荊州府通判。

translations.literal: For his judgment in the Baling case, the governor-general and surveillance commissioner submitted conflicting reports; summoned for audience, he was promoted to assistant prefect of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After his ruling in the Baling case set the governor-general and surveillance commissioner at odds in competing memorials, he was summoned to audience and promoted to assistant prefect of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 又以歸州縱盜冤良之獄，自巡撫按察以下皆被重譴，仲坃承審時，堅不會印，特旨召對。

translations.literal: Again, in the Guizhou case where bandits were released and the innocent condemned, all from the governor-general and surveillance commissioner downward were severely censured; when Zhongxun conducted the retrial he steadfastly refused to affix his seal, and was specially summoned for imperial audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guizhou case, where bandits had been set free and the innocent condemned, officials from the governor-general and surveillance commissioner on down were heavily censured; Zhongxun, presiding at retrial, steadfastly refused to seal the verdict and was summoned for a special audience with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 擢常德府同知，歷署襄陽、寶慶、宜昌、武昌、永順、岳州、永州七府知府，護衡永郴桂道。

translations.literal: Promoted to sub-prefect of Changde, he served successively as acting prefect of Xiangyang, Baqing, Yichang, Wuchang, Yongshun, Yuezhou, and Yongzhou — seven prefectures — and administered the Heng-Yong-Chen-Gui circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to sub-prefect of Changde, he acted in turn as prefect of seven prefectures — Xiangyang, Baqing, Yichang, Wuchang, Yongshun, Yuezhou, and Yongzhou — and administered the Heng-Yong-Chen-Gui circuit.

sentences.zh: 正躬率屬，屏絕請託，暇輒延耆士論學不倦。

translations.literal: Upright in person, he led his subordinates by example, shut out all solicitations; in leisure hours he constantly invited elderly scholars to discuss learning without tiring.
translations.idiomatic: He led by personal example, barred all favor-seeking, and in his spare time never tired of gathering elder scholars to discuss the classics.

sentences.zh: 仲坃官湖南先後三十年，長於折獄，大吏倚重。

translations.literal: Zhongxun served in Hunan for some thirty years in all, excelling at resolving cases; senior officials relied heavily on him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxun spent some thirty years in Hunan altogether, distinguished for unraveling difficult cases on which the province's highest officials came to depend.

sentences.zh: 歷奉檄鞫獄二百餘，多所平反，以直戇名。

translations.literal: Over the years he received commissions to investigate more than two hundred cases, reversing many wrongful convictions, and was known for blunt integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioned to retry more than two hundred cases over the years, he reversed many wrongful convictions and earned a name for blunt, uncompromising honesty.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十七年，在永州議改淮引食粵鹽，格於例不行，遂以目疾請告。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year of Qianlong, while at Yongzhou he proposed replacing Huai salt with Guangdong salt, but the plan was blocked by statute; he then requested retirement on grounds of eye ailment.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year of Qianlong (1772), while at Yongzhou, he proposed switching from Huai to Guangdong salt, but existing regulations blocked the change; he then retired citing failing eyesight.

sentences.zh: 解組日，貧如故，卒於家。

translations.literal: On the day he relinquished office he was as poor as ever; he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: When he laid down office he was as poor as when he had taken it up, and he died at home.

sentences.zh: =李大本=李大本，字立齋，山東安丘人。

translations.literal: Li Daben. Li Daben, courtesy name Lizhai, was a native of Anqiu in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daben. Li Daben, styled Lizhai, was from Anqiu in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 雍正十三年舉人。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate in the thirteenth year of Yongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examinations in the thirteenth year of Yongzheng (1735).

sentences.zh: 乾隆九年，銓授湖北棗陽知縣，改湖南益陽。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Qianlong he was appointed by the Board of Personnel as magistrate of Zaoyang in Hubei, then transferred to Yiyang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Qianlong (1744) the Board of Personnel assigned him magistrate of Zaoyang in Hubei, then transferred him to Yiyang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 居官自奉儉約，勤於吏事。

translations.literal: In office he lived frugally and applied himself diligently to administrative duties.
translations.idiomatic: He lived sparingly and threw himself into the work of government.

sentences.zh: 益陽人不知蠶，大本教之樹桑，後賴其利。

translations.literal: The people of Yiyang did not know sericulture; Daben taught them to plant mulberry trees, and afterward they relied on the profit.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yiyang knew nothing of sericulture; Daben taught them to plant mulberry trees, and afterward they prospered from the trade.

sentences.zh: 調長沙，遷寶慶府理瑤同知。

translations.literal: Transferred to Changsha, then promoted to sub-prefect for Yao affairs at Baqing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Changsha, then promoted to sub-prefect for Yao affairs under Baqing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 所隸通水峒有苗僧行賈臨桂，知縣田志隆見之，意為賊黨。

translations.literal: In his jurisdiction at Tongshui Pass, a Miao monk traveling as a merchant reached Lingui; Magistrate Tian Zhilong saw him and suspected him of being connected to bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In his jurisdiction at Tongshui Pass a Miao monk peddling goods reached Linggui; Magistrate Tian Zhilong took him for an accomplice of bandits.

sentences.zh: 吳方曙者，從馬朝桂謀叛，時方繪圖懸購者也。

translations.literal: Wu Fangshu had joined Ma Chaogui in plotting rebellion — the very man for whom wanted posters were then being circulated.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fangshu had joined Ma Chaogui's plot to rebel — the very fugitive whose likeness was then being posted and priced.

sentences.zh: 僧畏刑誣服，又訊朝桂所在，妄言在峒中。

translations.literal: The monk, fearing torture, falsely confessed; questioned about Ma Chaogui's whereabouts, he fabricatingly said he was in the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified of torture, the monk confessed to crimes he had not committed; pressed for Ma Chaogui's whereabouts, he invented a story that the rebel was hiding in the pass.

sentences.zh: 廣西巡撫定長立上奏，率兵出，命大本從行。

translations.literal: Guangxi Governor Ding Changli memorialized the throne and led troops out; Daben was ordered to accompany the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi Governor Ding Changli memorialized the throne and marched out with troops, ordering Daben to accompany the campaign.

sentences.zh: 大本曰：「僧言真偽不可知，大兵猝至，苗必駭，且生變，請潛訪之。

translations.literal: Daben said: "Whether the monk's words are true cannot be known; if troops arrive suddenly the Miao will be terrified and disturbances may follow — I beg leave to investigate in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Daben said, "We cannot know whether the monk speaks truth; if an army descends suddenly the Miao will panic and trouble will follow. I ask permission to investigate quietly.

sentences.zh: 」既而白僧言實妄，巡撫疑未釋，复欲以兵往，大本力諫乃止。

translations.literal: " Subsequently he reported that the monk's account was indeed false; the governor-general's suspicions were not yet dispelled and he again wished to send troops, but Daben remonstrated forcefully until he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " He soon reported that the monk had lied; the governor's suspicions lingered and he again wanted to march, but Daben argued him down.

sentences.zh: 後廷訊苗僧果誣如大本言。

translations.literal: Later, at court interrogation, the Miao monk was indeed found to have falsely confessed, just as Daben had said.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at an imperial hearing, the Miao monk was indeed shown to have confessed under duress, exactly as Daben had maintained.

sentences.zh: 橫嶺峒苗乏食，籥官求粟，大本多方賑之。

translations.literal: The Miao at Hengling Pass were short of food; the pass officer sought grain, and Daben found many ways to provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Miao at Hengling Pass ran short of food and the pass officer appealed for grain, Daben found many ways to feed them.

sentences.zh: 復為苗民籌生計，請於上官曰：「橫嶺峒自逆渠授首，安插餘苗，因惡其人，故薄其產，每口授田才三十欑至四十欑。

translations.literal: He also devised livelihoods for the Miao, petitioning his superiors: "Since the rebel chief surrendered at Hengling Pass and the remaining Miao were resettled, because of hatred for them their allotments were kept small — only thirty to forty kuan per person.
translations.idiomatic: He also sought a livelihood for the Miao, writing his superiors: "After the rebel leader surrendered at Hengling Pass and the remaining Miao were resettled, hatred kept their allotments miserly — only thirty to forty kuan of land per person.

sentences.zh: 每欑上田穫米六升，中田五升，下田四升，得米無多。

translations.literal: Each kuan of superior land yields six sheng of rice, middling land five sheng, inferior land four sheng — the rice obtained is not much.
translations.idiomatic: A kuan of top-grade land yields six sheng of rice, middling land five, poor land four — scarcely enough to live on.

sentences.zh: 又峒田稍腴者盡與堡卒，極惡者方畀苗民，歲入不足，男則斫柴易米，女則★L9蕨為粉，給口食。

translations.literal: Moreover, the better pass lands were all given to garrison soldiers; only the worst plots were allotted to the Miao; annual income was insufficient — men chopped firewood to trade for rice, women gathered fern roots to make flour for sustenance.
translations.idiomatic: The better fields in the pass went entirely to garrison troops; only the worst scraps were left to the Miao. Income fell short year after year — men felled firewood to barter for rice, women pounded fern root into flour to fill their mouths.

sentences.zh: 年來生齒日繁，材木竭，米價益昂，飢餓愁嘆，深可憐憫，恐不可坐視而不為之所。

translations.literal: In recent years population has grown daily, timber is exhausted, rice prices rise ever higher; hunger and lamentation are deeply pitiable — we cannot simply watch and do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Population has swelled, timber is gone, and rice grows dearer by the year; hunger and despair are heartbreaking. We cannot stand by and do nothing.

sentences.zh: 現有入官苗田一千三百四十八畝，舊募漢民佃種，出租供餉，姦良不一，屢經淘汰。

translations.literal: There are presently 1,348 mu of confiscated Miao land, formerly leased to Han tenant farmers with rents supporting supplies; honest and dishonest tenants mixed, repeatedly culled.
translations.idiomatic: There are 1,348 mu of confiscated Miao land now farmed by Han tenants recruited to pay rents toward military supplies; good and bad tenants have been sifted out again and again.

sentences.zh: 請視苗民家貧丁眾者書諸簿，有漢佃應除者，即書簿之苗丁次第受種，出租如故，則苗民得食而餉亦無虧，乃補救之一端。

translations.literal: I request recording Miao households that are poor with many mouths; where Han tenants should be removed, let the Miao listed in the register receive seed land in turn, with rents as before — thus the Miao obtain food and supplies suffer no loss; this is one means of remedy."
translations.idiomatic: Register the poorest Miao households with the most mouths; where a Han tenant should be removed, let the Miao on the register take the plot in turn, paying the same rent — so the Miao gain food and supplies lose nothing. It is at least a start."

sentences.zh: 」議上，不許。

translations.literal: The proposal was submitted but rejected.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal went up and was denied.

sentences.zh: 後巡撫陳宏謀見之，曰：「此識時務之言也。

translations.literal: Later Governor Chen Hongmou saw it and said: "These are words that grasp the needs of the times.
translations.idiomatic: Later Governor Chen Hongmou read the memorial and said, "This is the speech of a man who understands his age.

sentences.zh: 」將陳其事，會他遷，未果。

translations.literal: " He was about to memorialized the matter when he was transferred elsewhere; it came to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: " He was about to take it up when he was transferred elsewhere, and the plan died.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，題請升授知府，因病足歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was nominated for promotion to prefect; he returned home due to leg ailment and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was recommended for promotion to prefect; crippled by leg ailment he went home and died there.

sentences.zh: =牛運震=牛運震，字階平，山東滋陽人。

translations.literal: Niu Yunzhen. Niu Yunzhen, courtesy name Jieping, was a native of Ziyang in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Yunzhen. Niu Yunzhen, styled Jieping, was from Ziyang in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 雍正十一年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the eleventh year of Yongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examinations in the eleventh year of Yongzheng (1733).

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，召試博學鴻詞，不遇。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was summoned to the special examination in erudite learning and polished prose but was not selected.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong (1736) he was called to the special erudite-learning examination but was not chosen.

sentences.zh: 尋授甘肅秦安知縣，開九渠，溉田萬畝。

translations.literal: Soon afterward appointed magistrate of Qin'an in Gansu; he opened nine canals, irrigating ten thousand mu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed magistrate of Qin'an in Gansu, where he opened nine canals and irrigated ten thousand mu.

sentences.zh: 縣北玉鍾峽山崩塞河，水溢為災。

translations.literal: North of the county Mount Yuzhong Gorge collapsed and blocked the river; the overflow became a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: North of the county a landslide at Yuzhong Gorge dammed the river and sent floodwaters raging through the land.

sentences.zh: 運震率丁夫開濬，凡四日夜，水退。

translations.literal: Yunzhen led corvée laborers to dredge; in four days and nights the water receded.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhen mobilized corvée labor to dredge the channel; in four days and nights the waters fell.

sentences.zh: 緣山步行，以錢米給災戶。

translations.literal: He walked along the mountains on foot, distributing cash and grain to afflicted households.
translations.idiomatic: He walked the mountain paths on foot, distributing cash and grain to stricken households.

sentences.zh: 縣聚曰西固，去治二百餘裡，輸糧苦運艱，多積逋。

translations.literal: A cluster of settlements called Xigu lay more than two hundred li from the seat; grain transport was hard and arrears accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: The settlement cluster of Xigu lay more than two hundred li from the county seat; grain transport was arduous and tax arrears piled up.

sentences.zh: 運震許以銀代納，民便之。

translations.literal: Yunzhen permitted silver payment in lieu of grain; the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhen allowed payment in silver instead of grain, to the people's great relief.

sentences.zh: 先是巡檢某誣馬得才兄弟五人為盜，前令弗察，得才自刎死。

translations.literal: Previously a patrol inspector falsely accused the five Ma Decai brothers of banditry; the former magistrate did not investigate, and Decai killed himself by cutting his throat.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a patrol inspector had falsely accused the five Ma Decai brothers of banditry; the previous magistrate never looked into it, and Decai cut his own throat.
