sentences.zh: 其兄馬都上控，令又誘而斃之獄。

translations.literal: His elder brother Madu appealed upward; the magistrate again coaxed him and had him beaten to death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Madu appealed to higher authority; the magistrate lured him back and had him beaten to death in jail.

sentences.zh: 其三人者將解府，運震鞫得其情，昭雪之。

translations.literal: The three remaining brothers were about to be sent to the prefecture when Yunzhen interrogated them and learned the truth, clearing their names.
translations.idiomatic: The three surviving brothers were bound for the prefectural yamen when Yunzhen examined the case, learned the truth, and cleared them.

sentences.zh: 又清水縣某令冤武生杜其陶父子謀殺罪，上官檄運震覆治，驗死者得自刎狀，以移屍罪其陶而釋其子。

translations.literal: Again, a magistrate of Qingshui County had wrongly convicted the military licentiate Du Qitao and his son of conspiracy to murder; a superior ordered Yunzhen to retry the case; examination showed the deceased had killed himself; Qitao was convicted of moving the corpse while his son was released.
translations.idiomatic: Again, a Qingshui magistrate had wrongly convicted the military licentiate Du Qitao and his son of plotting murder; ordered to retry the case, Yunzhen found the dead man had killed himself, convicted Qitao of moving the body to frame another, and released the son.

sentences.zh: 他訟獄多所平反。

translations.literal: In other lawsuits and cases he reversed many wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: In other suits and criminal cases he overturned many unjust verdicts.

sentences.zh: 官秦安八年，惠農通商。

translations.literal: Eight years as magistrate of Qin'an — benefiting farmers and promoting trade.
translations.idiomatic: For eight years at Qin'an he enriched the farmers and opened commerce.

sentences.zh: 暇則行視郊野，鑄農具，教民耕耨。

translations.literal: In leisure he toured the countryside, cast farm implements, and taught the people plowing and hoeing.
translations.idiomatic: In his spare time he walked the fields, cast farm tools, and taught the people how to plow and weed.

sentences.zh: 稱貸販褐戶，不求其息。

translations.literal: He lent money to brown-cloth peddlers without seeking interest.
translations.idiomatic: He lent money to peddlers of homespun brown cloth and asked no interest in return.

sentences.zh: 設隴川書院，日與諸生講習，民始向學。

translations.literal: He established Longchuan Academy, daily lecturing students; the people began to turn toward learning.
translations.idiomatic: He founded Longchuan Academy, lectured the students daily, and the people at last turned toward books.

sentences.zh: 兼攝徽縣，又攝兩當縣，舍於三縣之中，曰大門鎮，以聽訟。

translations.literal: He also administered Huixian and Liangdang counties, lodging at Damen Town midway among the three counties to hear cases.
translations.idiomatic: He also acted for Huixian and Liangdang, keeping court at Damen Town midway among the three counties.

sentences.zh: 徽縣多虎，募壯士殺虎二十六，道始通。

translations.literal: Huixian had many tigers; he recruited stalwarts who killed twenty-six tigers, and the roads became passable.
translations.idiomatic: Huixian swarmed with tigers; he recruited brave men who killed twenty-six of them, and the roads were safe again.

sentences.zh: 調平番，值縣境五道峴告饉，捐粟二百石以賑，民感之。

translations.literal: Transferred to Pingfan; when Wudao Pass in the county reported famine, he donated two hundred shi of grain for relief; the people were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Pingfan, he gave two hundred shi of grain when Wudao Pass reported famine, and the people were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 人輸一錢，製衣銘德，運震受衣返幣。

translations.literal: Each person contributed one cash; they made a garment inscribed with his virtues; Yunzhen accepted the garment but returned the money.
translations.idiomatic: Each person gave one cash; they had a robe made bearing his praises. Yunzhen accepted the robe but returned the money.

sentences.zh: 固原兵變四掠，督撫皆至涼州，檄召運震問方略。

translations.literal: When Garrison troops at Guyuan mutinied and plundered in four directions, governor-general and governor all came to Liangzhou and summoned Yunzhen for counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When Guyuan garrison troops mutinied and looted on four fronts, the governor-general and governor both reached Liangzhou and summoned Yunzhen for advice.

sentences.zh: 運震請勿以兵往，但屯城外為聲援，令城內捋出亂者。

translations.literal: Yunzhen asked that troops not be sent in, but only encamped outside the city as support, ordering those inside to drag out the ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhen urged that no troops enter the city, but camp outside as a show of force while those inside handed over the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 游擊某執三百餘人，眾忷懼，運震請釋無辜，入城慰喻。

translations.literal: A brigade commander arrested more than three hundred men; the crowd was alarmed; Yunzhen requested release of the innocent and entered the city to comfort and instruct.
translations.idiomatic: A brigade commander seized more than three hundred men; panic spread through the crowd. Yunzhen asked that the innocent be freed, then entered the city to reassure the people.

sentences.zh: 斬三人，監候四人，餘予杖徒有差，反側遂安。

translations.literal: Three were beheaded, four held awaiting execution, the rest given beatings and penal servitude in varying degrees; the unrest was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Three were beheaded, four held for execution, the rest beaten and sentenced to penal servitude in varying degrees, and the disturbance subsided.

sentences.zh: 有忌者摭前受萬民衣事，劾免官。

translations.literal: An envious man seized on his earlier acceptance of the garment from the myriad people and impeached him, leading to dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: A jealous rival dredged up his acceptance of the people's robe and impeached him out of office.

sentences.zh: 貧不能歸，留主皋蘭書院，教學得士心。

translations.literal: Too poor to return home, he stayed to head Gaolan Academy; his teaching won the hearts of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Too poor to travel home, he remained to head Gaolan Academy, where his teaching won every student's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 及歸，有走千里送至灞橋者。

translations.literal: When he finally returned, some traveled a thousand li to see him off at Ba Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: When he at last set out for home, some walked a thousand li to see him off at Ba Bridge.

sentences.zh: 運震居官，不假手幕下，事輒自治。

translations.literal: In office Yunzhen never delegated to secretarial staff; he handled affairs himself.
translations.idiomatic: In office Yunzhen never handed work to his secretaries; he managed everything himself.

sentences.zh: 所至嚴行保甲，鬥爭訟獄日即於少。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he strictly enforced the baojia system; brawls and lawsuits daily grew fewer.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he enforced the baojia system rigorously, and brawls and lawsuits dwindled day by day.

sentences.zh: 遇人幹訟，必嚴懲。

translations.literal: Those who meddled in litigation he always punished severely.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who stirred up lawsuits he punished without mercy.

sentences.zh: 治盜尤嚴，曰：「邊鄙風俗疵悍，不如此，則法不立；

translations.literal: He was especially strict on bandits, saying: "Frontier customs are rough and fierce; unless we act thus, the law cannot stand;
translations.idiomatic: He was fiercest against banditry, saying, "On the frontier people are wild and hard; unless we govern this way the law has no force;

sentences.zh: 令不行，民不可得而治。

translations.literal: orders go unenforced, and the people cannot be governed."
translations.idiomatic: orders go unheeded and the people cannot be ruled."

sentences.zh: 且與其輕刑十人，不如重處一人而九人畏，是懲一而恕九也。

translations.literal: Moreover, rather than light punishment for ten men, it is better to punish one severely so that nine fear — this is punishing one while sparing nine."
translations.idiomatic: Better to punish one man harshly and make nine afraid than to treat ten lightly — that is punishing one to warn nine."

sentences.zh: 」罷官歸後，閉門治經，搜考金石，所著經義、史論、文集及金石圖，皆行於世。

translations.literal: After dismissal and return, he shut his doors to study the classics, research epigraphy; his exegetical works, historical essays, collected writings, and rubbings all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: After his dismissal he shut his doors, immersed himself in the classics, and combed through epigraphy; his commentaries, historical essays, collected writings, and rubbings all found readers.

sentences.zh: 嘗主晉陽、河東兩書院，所造多名雋士，世稱「空山先生」。

translations.literal: He once headed the Jinyang and Hedong academies; his students included many outstanding talents; the world called him "Master Kongshan."
translations.idiomatic: He later headed the Jinyang and Hedong academies, trained many brilliant men, and was known in his age as Master Kongshan.

sentences.zh: =張甄陶=張甄陶，字希週，福建福清人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhentao. Zhang Zhentao, courtesy name Xizhou, was a native of Fuqing in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhentao. Zhang Zhentao, styled Xizhou, was from Fuqing in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 舉鴻博，補試未合格罷。

translations.literal: He entered the erudite learning examination; failing the supplementary test, he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the erudite-learning examination but failed the supplementary test and was sent home.

sentences.zh: 大學士硃軾、侍郎方苞薦修三禮，辭，而請受業於苞。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhu Shi and Vice Minister Fang Bao recommended him to compile the Three Rites; he declined and instead asked to study under Fang Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhu Shi and Vice Minister Fang Bao recommended him to help compile the Three Rites; he declined and asked instead to study under Fang Bao.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十年，成進士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Qianlong he became a metropolitan graduate.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Qianlong (1745) he passed the metropolitan examinations.

sentences.zh: 時方許極言直諫，甄陶對策，困極陳時務。

translations.literal: At the time frank remonstrance was permitted; Zhentao in his examination answers exhaustively laid out affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: The court then encouraged blunt counsel; in his examination essays Zhentao poured out his views on public affairs without reserve.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，授編修，尋改授廣東鶴山知縣。

translations.literal: Selected as Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler; soon transferred to magistrate of Heshan in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Chosen as a Hanlin bachelor and appointed compiler, he was soon sent out as magistrate of Heshan in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 歷香山、新會、高要、揭陽，皆劇邑，所至有聲。

translations.literal: He served at Xiangshan, Xinhui, Gaoyao, and Jieyang — all difficult counties — and wherever he went earned renown.
translations.idiomatic: He served at Xiangshan, Xinhui, Gaoyao, and Jieyang — all notoriously hard posts — and won a name at every one.

sentences.zh: 疆田疇，修堤圩，弛戶蠔蜆之禁，增建書院、社倉，平反冤獄，詰捕盜賊，為政務無怫逆於民。

translations.literal: He opened fields, repaired dikes and embankments, lifted restrictions on household oyster and clam gathering, added academies and community granaries, reversed wrongful convictions, hunted down bandits — governing always without opposing the people's will.
translations.idiomatic: He opened land, repaired dikes, lifted the ban on household oyster and clam harvests, built academies and community granaries, righted wrongful cases, and hunted bandits — governing always in harmony with the people's wishes.

sentences.zh: 以憂去官，服除，起授雲南昆明，弗獲於上官，坐事免。

translations.literal: He left office for mourning; when mourning ended he was appointed to Kunming in Yunnan but failed to get along with superiors and was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned for mourning; when the mourning period ended he was posted to Kunming in Yunnan, fell out with his superiors, and was dismissed after an incident.

sentences.zh: 主講五華書院，尹壯圖、錢灃皆其弟子。

translations.literal: He lectured at Wuhua Academy; Yin Zhuangtu and Qian Feng were both his students.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured at Wuhua Academy, where Yin Zhuangtu and Qian Feng were among his pupils.

sentences.zh: 复移掌貴州貴山書院，課士有法。

translations.literal: He then moved to head Guizhou Academy at Guishan, with systematic methods for examining students.
translations.idiomatic: He then took charge of Guishan Academy in Guizhou, where he tested students by rigorous, well-ordered methods.

sentences.zh: 總督劉藻疏薦，詔加國子監司業銜。

translations.literal: Governor-General Liu Zao memorialized recommending him; an edict added the rank of Vice Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Liu Zao recommended him by memorial, and an edict conferred on him the rank of Vice Director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 晚以病歸閩，主鼇峰書院。

translations.literal: In his later years he returned to Fujian due to illness and headed Aofeng Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years, ill, he returned to Fujian and headed Aofeng Academy.

sentences.zh: 以經義教閩士，於是咸通漢、唐注疏之學。

translations.literal: Teaching Fujian scholars through classical exegesis, he brought them all to mastery of Han and Tang commentarial learning.
translations.idiomatic: Teaching Fujian scholars through classical exegesis, he opened their eyes to the commentarial traditions of Han and Tang.

sentences.zh: 在滇時著經解百餘卷。

translations.literal: While in Yunnan he authored more than a hundred juan of classical commentary.
translations.idiomatic: During his years in Yunnan he wrote more than a hundred juan of commentary on the classics.

sentences.zh: 方甄陶之補外，人咸惜之。

translations.literal: Just as Zhang Zhentao was assigned to a provincial post outside the capital, everyone regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhentao was sent out to serve in the provinces, everyone lamented the loss.

sentences.zh: 大學士陳世倌贈以明呂坤呻吟語，甄陶讀其實政錄而慕之，在粵作學實政錄，見其書者，咸曰：「循吏之言也。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Chen Shiguang gave him the Ming work Groaning Words by Lü Kun; Zhentao read its Records of Actual Governance and admired them, and while in Guangdong wrote A Study of Records of Actual Governance; all who saw the book said, "These are the words of an exemplary official."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Chen Shiguang presented him with Lü Kun's Ming-dynasty Groaning Words. Zhentao read its Records of Actual Governance and was inspired to write his own Study of Records of Actual Governance in Guangdong. Everyone who read it declared: "This is how an exemplary official speaks."

sentences.zh: =邵大業=邵大業，字在中，順天大興人，舊籍浙江餘姚。

translations.literal: Shao Daye. Shao Daye, courtesy name Zaizhong, was a native of Daxing in Shuntian; his original household register was in Yuyao, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Daye. Shao Daye, courtesy name Zaizhong, was from Daxing in Shuntian; his original household register was in Yuyao, Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 雍正十一年進士，乾隆元年，授湖北黃陂知縣。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the eleventh year of Yongzheng; in the first year of Qianlong, he was appointed magistrate of Huangpi in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the eleventh year of the Yongzheng reign (1733) and, in the first year of Qianlong (1736), was appointed magistrate of Huangpi in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 初到官，投訟牒者坌至，不移晷，決遣立盡。

translations.literal: When he first took office, litigants poured in with petitions; before the sun had moved from its noon position, every case was decided and dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he took office, petitioners flooded in with lawsuits; before the sun had moved a hand's breadth from noon, he had decided and dispatched every case.

sentences.zh: 吏人一見問姓名，後無不識，眾莫敢弄以事。

translations.literal: The clerks, once they had asked his name, never failed to recognize him afterward, and no one dared to trifle with matters.
translations.idiomatic: After asking his name once, the clerks never failed to recognize him again, and no one dared to play games with the business of the court.

sentences.zh: 有兄弟爭產訟，皆頒白，貌相類。

translations.literal: Two brothers were suing over property; both were white-haired and looked alike.
translations.idiomatic: Two brothers were suing over an inheritance; both were white-haired and looked much alike.

sentences.zh: 令以鏡鏡面，問曰：「類乎？

translations.literal: He had them face the mirror and asked, "Do you look alike?"
translations.idiomatic: He had them look into a mirror and asked, "Do you look alike?"

translations.literal: They answered, "We do."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "We do."

sentences.zh: 」則進與為家人語曰：「吾新喪弟，獨不得如爾兩人白首相保也。

translations.literal: He then came forward and spoke to them as family: "I have just lost a younger brother and cannot enjoy what you two have — growing old together in mutual care."
translations.idiomatic: He then stepped forward and spoke to them like family: "I have just lost a younger brother and cannot enjoy what you two have — growing old together, each keeping the other safe."

sentences.zh: 」二人感動罷去。

translations.literal: Moved, the two withdrew and dropped the suit.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply moved, the two brothers withdrew and abandoned the lawsuit.

sentences.zh: 蛟水壞城，當壞處立，誓以殉，水驟止，拯溺餔飢，完堤岸，民得免患。

translations.literal: Floodwaters wrecked the city wall; he stood at the breach and vowed to die with it; the water suddenly stopped. He rescued the drowning, fed the hungry, repaired the dikes and banks, and the people were spared disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When catastrophic floods breached the city wall, he stood at the break and vowed to die with it; the waters suddenly subsided. He rescued the drowning, fed the hungry, restored the dikes and banks, and the people were spared further harm.

sentences.zh: 總督以其名上聞，會父憂去。

translations.literal: The governor-general memorialized his name to the throne; he then left when his father died.
translations.idiomatic: The governor-general submitted his name to the throne, but he then departed when his father died.

sentences.zh: 服闋，授河南禹州知州，調睢州。

translations.literal: After his mourning period ended, he was appointed prefect of Yuzhou in Henan, then transferred to Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, he was appointed prefect of Yuzhou in Henan and then transferred to Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 頻澇，請糶請賑，民以免患。

translations.literal: There were frequent floods; he petitioned for grain sales and relief, sparing the people from harm.
translations.idiomatic: Floods came again and again; he petitioned for grain release and famine relief, and the people were spared disaster.

sentences.zh: 濬惠濟河，以俸錢更直，擢江南蘇州知府。

translations.literal: He dredged the Huiji River, paying labor costs from his salary, and was promoted to prefect of Suzhou in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged the Huiji River, covering labor costs from his own salary, and was promoted to prefect of Suzhou in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 松江盜獄久不決，株連瘐斃者眾，奉檄鞫治。

translations.literal: A theft case in Songjiang had long gone unresolved; many implicated had died in prison from illness. Ordered to investigate, he took up the case.
translations.idiomatic: A robbery case in Songjiang had dragged on for years; many of those implicated had wasted away and died in custody. Ordered to investigate, he took up the case.

sentences.zh: 見群犯皆斷脛折踝，蹙然曰：「爾等亦人子，迫飢寒至此，猶茹刑顛倒首從，誣連非罪人，何益於爾？

translations.literal: Seeing the prisoners with broken legs and ankles, he said with distress, "You too are sons of men; driven by hunger and cold to this pass, you still endure torture while principal and accomplice are reversed and innocent people are implicated — what good does that do you?"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the prisoners with shattered shins and broken ankles, he said with anguish: "You too are someone's sons. Driven by hunger and cold to this, you still endure torture while leaders and followers are reversed and the innocent are dragged in — what good does that do you?"

sentences.zh: 」有盜幡然曰：「官以人類待我，我不忍欺。

translations.literal: One thief suddenly said, "The magistrate treats me as a human being — I cannot bear to deceive him."
translations.idiomatic: One of the robbers blurted out: "The magistrate treats me like a human being — I cannot bear to lie to him."

sentences.zh: 」獄辭立具。

translations.literal: The case record was immediately complete.
translations.idiomatic: The case record was completed at once.

sentences.zh: 兼署蘇松太道，尋攝布政使事，大吏交章薦。

translations.literal: He concurrently served as intendant of Su-Song-Tai; soon afterward he acted as provincial treasurer, and senior officials jointly recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: He concurrently served as intendant of Su-Song-Tai Circuit; soon he was acting provincial treasurer, and senior officials submitted joint recommendations on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 十六年，高宗南巡，御舟左右挽行，名嘏須纖。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, the Gaozong Emperor toured the south; tow ropes flanked the imperial barge on both sides — thick ropes known as gua-xu ropes.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, the Gaozong Emperor made his southern tour; thick tow ropes called gua-xu ropes were rigged on both sides of the imperial barge.

sentences.zh: 大業語從臣，除道增纖必病民，非所以宣上德意，遂改單纖。

translations.literal: Daye told the attending officials that clearing roads and adding tow ropes would surely burden the people — not the way to broadcast the emperor's benevolent intent — and the ropes were changed to single lines.
translations.idiomatic: Daye told the officials in attendance that clearing roads and adding tow ropes would only burden the people and was no way to proclaim the emperor's benevolent intent; the thick ropes were therefore replaced with single lines.

sentences.zh: 會積雨，治吳江帳殿未就，總督劾大業觀望。

translations.literal: Continuous rain fell; the temporary palace at Wujiang was not yet finished, and the governor-general impeached Daye for foot-dragging.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell without letup, and the temporary palace at Wujiang was still unfinished; the governor-general impeached Daye for dragging his feet.

sentences.zh: 及乘輿至​​，則供備已具，然大業卒因左遷。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage arrived, everything was already in readiness — yet Daye was still demoted in the end.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the imperial carriage arrived, all preparations were complete — yet Daye was demoted all the same.

sentences.zh: 尋授河南開封知府，屬縣封丘民被控侵占田畝，及勘丈，非侵占，而畝浮於額。

translations.literal: Soon appointed prefect of Kaifeng in Henan. In his subordinate county Fengqiu, peasants were accused of encroaching on fields; on survey it was not encroachment, but measured acreage exceeded the registered quota.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed prefect of Kaifeng in Henan. In Fengqiu, one of his subordinate counties, peasants were accused of encroaching on farmland; on resurvey there was no encroachment, but the measured acreage exceeded the registered quota.

sentences.zh: 大業考志乘，河南賦則，自明萬曆改並，中地十畝，作上地七畝；

translations.literal: Daye consulted local gazetteers and Henan's tax registers: since the Ming Wanli reforms, ten mu of middle-grade land were counted as seven mu of upper-grade land;
translations.idiomatic: Daye consulted local gazetteers and Henan's tax registers and found that since the Ming Wanli consolidation, ten mu of middle-grade land were counted as seven mu of upper-grade land;

sentences.zh: 下地十畝，作上地三畝。

translations.literal: ten mu of lower-grade land as three mu of upper-grade land.
translations.idiomatic: and ten mu of lower-grade land as three mu of upper-grade land.

sentences.zh: 上官以昔為下則，今則膏腴，議加賦。

translations.literal: Superiors held that what had once been lower-grade land was now fertile soil and proposed increasing the tax assessment.
translations.idiomatic: His superiors argued that land once taxed at the lower rate was now rich soil and proposed raising the assessment.

sentences.zh: 大業曰：「此河沖淤積，百姓以墳墓田廬所易之微利也。

translations.literal: Daye said: "This is land piled up by river deposition — the slight gain people exchanged graves, homesteads, and fields for.
translations.idiomatic: Daye said: "This is land built up by river silt — the small profit people traded for graves, homesteads, and fields.

sentences.zh: 今日為退灘淤地，異日即可為沙壓水沖。

translations.literal: Today it is retreat-shore silt land; tomorrow it may be buried under sand or washed away by water.
translations.idiomatic: Today it is reclaimed shoal; tomorrow it may be buried under sand or swept away by flood.

sentences.zh: 冬春播種，夏秋之收穫不可知。

translations.literal: They sow in winter and spring, but the autumn harvest is uncertain.
translations.idiomatic: They sow in winter and spring, but whether there will be an autumn harvest is anyone's guess.

sentences.zh: 上年河決，屋宇未盡葺，流亡未盡复，遽增歲額，何以堪？

translations.literal: Last year the river burst its banks; houses are not yet fully repaired and refugees have not all returned — how can they bear a sudden increase in the annual quota?"
translations.idiomatic: Last year the river broke its banks; houses are not yet fully rebuilt and refugees have not all returned — how can they bear a sudden increase in the annual quota?"

sentences.zh: 」旋從部議試種三年，次年果沒入水，乃止。

translations.literal: Following the ministry's proposal for a three-year trial planting, the next year the land was indeed submerged and the increase was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Following the ministry's plan for a three-year trial planting, the land was submerged the very next year, and the proposed increase was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以河溢，降江南六安州知州，又以盜案鐫級。

translations.literal: Before long, owing to river overflow, he was demoted to magistrate of Lu'an Prefecture in Jiangnan; he was further reduced in rank over a theft case.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, after river overflow, he was demoted to magistrate of Lu'an Prefecture in Jiangnan and further reduced in rank over a theft case.

sentences.zh: 引見，再還江南，署江寧府。

translations.literal: After an audience with the emperor, he returned again to Jiangnan and served as acting prefect of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: After an audience with the emperor, he returned once more to Jiangnan and served as acting prefect of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，授徐州知府，府城三面瀕黃河，西北隅尤當衝，雖有重堤，恃韓家山埽為固。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, appointed prefect of Xuzhou. The prefectural city bordered the Yellow River on three sides; the northwest corner bore the brunt. Though there were great dikes, security depended on the Hanjiashan embankment works.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed prefect of Xuzhou. The city bordered the Yellow River on three sides, with the northwest corner most exposed. Though there were major dikes, safety depended on the Hanjiashan embankment works.

sentences.zh: 大業按視得蘇公舊堤，起城西雲龍山，迄城北月堤，長三里，湮為民居，復其舊。

translations.literal: Daye inspected the site and found an old dike built by Su [Dongpo]: from Yunlong Mountain west of the city to Yue Dike north of the city, three li long — buried under dwellings. He restored it.
translations.idiomatic: Daye inspected the site and found an old dike built by Su Dongpo, running three li from Yunlong Mountain west of the city to Yue Dike north of the city — buried under houses. He restored it.

sentences.zh: 越歲，韓家山埽幾潰，民恃此堤以無恐。

translations.literal: The next year the Hanjiashan works nearly collapsed; the people relied on this dike and were unafraid.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Hanjiashan works nearly gave way; the people relied on this dike and were unafraid.

sentences.zh: 复濬荊山橋河，於水利宣洩，規畫盡善。

translations.literal: He also dredged the Jingshan Bridge River; for water control and drainage, the plan was thoroughly sound.
translations.idiomatic: He also dredged the Jingshan Bridge River; for drainage and flood control, the design was thoroughly sound.

sentences.zh: 治徐七年，間有水患，不病民。

translations.literal: He governed Xuzhou seven years; though floods occurred from time to time, the people were not afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Xuzhou for seven years; though floods came from time to time, the people were not ruined.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，坐妖匪割辮事罷職，謫戍軍台，數年卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, dismissed over the sorcerer-rebel queue-cutting affair, exiled to a military colony, and died there several years later.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year he was dismissed over the sorcerer-rebel queue-cutting affair, exiled to a military colony, and died there several years later.

sentences.zh: 大業所至以勸學為務，因黃陂二程子祠建義學，葺睢州洛學書院，集諸生親為之師焉。

translations.literal: Wherever Daye served, he made promoting learning his priority: at Huangpi he built a charity school at the shrine to the Two Chengs; at Suizhou he restored the Luoxue Academy; he gathered students and taught them personally.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Daye served, he made promoting learning his chief concern: at Huangpi he built a charity school at the shrine to the Two Chengs; at Suizhou he restored the Luoxue Academy; he gathered students and taught them himself.

sentences.zh: =周克開=周克開，字乾三，湖南長沙人。

translations.literal: Zhou Kekai. Zhou Kekai, courtesy name Qiansan, was from Changsha in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Kekai. Zhou Kekai, courtesy name Qiansan, was from Changsha in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十二年舉人。

translations.literal: Provincial graduate in the twelfth year of Qianlong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the twelfth year of the Qianlong reign (1747).

sentences.zh: 十九年，以明通榜授甘肅隴西知縣。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, appointed magistrate of Longxi in Gansu through the Mingtong register.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Qianlong (1754), he was appointed magistrate of Longxi in Gansu through the Mingtong register.

sentences.zh: 調寧朔，縣屬寧夏府，並河有三渠，曰漢來、唐延、大清，皆引河入渠灌田。

translations.literal: Transferred to Ningshuo, subordinate to Ningxia Prefecture. Along the river were three canals — Hanlai, Tangyan, and Daqing — all drawing river water into channels to irrigate fields.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Ningshuo, a county under Ningxia Prefecture. Along the river were three canals — Hanlai, Tangyan, and Daqing — all drawing Yellow River water into channels to irrigate the fields.

sentences.zh: 唐延渠所經地多沙易漫，克開治之使深狹，又頗改其水道，渠行得安。

translations.literal: The Tangyan Canal passed through sandy ground prone to flooding; Kekai made it deep and narrow and considerably altered its course, so the canal ran safely.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangyan Canal ran through sandy ground prone to silting and overflow; Kekai deepened and narrowed it and substantially altered its course until the canal ran safely.

sentences.zh: 渠有石竇，洩水於河，以備旱澇，民謂之暗洞。

translations.literal: The canal had stone sluices to release water into the river against drought and flood; the people called them "dark tunnels."
translations.idiomatic: The canal had stone sluices to discharge water into the river as a safeguard against drought and flood; the people called them "dark tunnels."

sentences.zh: 時暗洞崩塞，渠水不行，上官欲填暗洞而竭唐延入漢來，以便寧夏縣之引河，寧夏利而寧朔必病。

translations.literal: The dark tunnels had collapsed and blocked the canal; superiors wanted to fill them and divert all Tangyan water into Hanlai to ease Ningxia County's river draw — benefit to Ningxia but harm to Ningshuo.
translations.idiomatic: The dark tunnels had collapsed and the canal was blocked; superiors wanted to fill them and divert all Tangyan water into Hanlai to ease Ningxia County's river draw — a gain for Ningxia but a loss for Ningshuo.

sentences.zh: 克開恐夏、秋水盛無所宣洩，時新水將至，不可待。

translations.literal: Kekai feared that in summer and autumn, when waters swelled, there would be no outlet; with new water about to arrive, there was no time to wait.
translations.idiomatic: Kekai feared that in summer and autumn, when the waters rose, there would be no outlet; with the new flood about to arrive, there was no time to wait.

sentences.zh: 克開請五日為期，取故渠及廢閘之石，晝夜督工，五日而暗洞复，兩縣皆利。

translations.literal: Kekai asked for five days, took stone from old canals and abandoned sluices, and drove the work day and night; in five days the dark tunnels were restored and both counties benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Kekai asked for five days, took stone from old channels and abandoned sluices, and drove the work day and night; in five days the dark tunnels were restored and both counties benefited.

sentences.zh: 大清渠長三十餘裡，鑿自康熙間，久而石門首尾壞，民失其利，克開亦修之，皆費省而工速。

translations.literal: The Daqing Canal, over thirty li long, had been cut in the Kangxi era; in time the stone gates at both ends broke and the people lost the benefit. Kekai repaired them too — all at modest cost and with speed.
translations.idiomatic: The Daqing Canal, more than thirty li long, had been dug in the Kangxi era; in time the stone gates at both ends collapsed and the people lost its benefit. Kekai repaired them as well — all at modest cost and with speed.

sentences.zh: 再以卓異薦，擢固原知州，父憂去。

translations.literal: Recommended again for outstanding merit, promoted to prefect of Guyuan; left when his father died.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended again for outstanding merit, he was promoted to prefect of Guyuan; he then left office when his father died.

sentences.zh: 服闋，補洮州。

translations.literal: After mourning, assigned to Taozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, he was assigned to Taozhou.

sentences.zh: 尋擢貴州都勻知府。

translations.literal: Soon promoted to prefect of Duyun in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to prefect of Duyun in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 從總督吳達善、侍郎錢維城治貴州逆苗獄，用法有失當者，力爭無少遜。

translations.literal: Following Governor-General Wu Dashan and Vice Minister Qian Weicheng in handling the Guizhou Miao rebellion cases, wherever legal application was improper he argued forcefully without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: While assisting Governor-General Wu Dashan and Vice Minister Qian Weicheng in handling the Guizhou Miao rebellion cases, he forcefully contested every improper application of the law without yielding an inch.

sentences.zh: 調貴陽，亦以強直忤巡撫宮兆麟，因公累解職。

translations.literal: Transferred to Guiyang; his forthright character also offended Governor Gong Zhaolin, and he was dismissed over official matters.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Guiyang, he also offended Governor Gong Zhaolin with his uncompromising character and was dismissed over official matters.

sentences.zh: 引見，复授山西蒲州知府，調太原。

translations.literal: After an audience, reappointed prefect of Puzhou in Shanxi, then transferred to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After an audience with the emperor, he was reappointed prefect of Puzhou in Shanxi and then transferred to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 清釐積獄，修復風峪山堤堰，障山潦，導之入汾，民德之。

translations.literal: He cleared backlogged cases, restored the Fengyu Mountain dikes and barrages to block mountain floods and channel them into the Fen River; the people were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared backlogged cases and restored the Fengyu Mountain dikes and barrages to block mountain floods and channel them into the Fen River; the people were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 擢江西吉南贛寧道，署布政使，以王錫侯書案被議。

translations.literal: Promoted to intendant of Ji-Nan-Gan-Ning in Jiangxi and acted as provincial treasurer; implicated in the Wang Xihou dictionary case.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to intendant of Ji-Nan-Gan-Ning in Jiangxi and acted as provincial treasurer, but was implicated in the Wang Xihou dictionary case.

sentences.zh: 高宗知其賢，發江南，以同知用。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor knew his worth and sent him to Jiangnan to serve as a sub-prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozong Emperor knew his worth and sent him to Jiangnan to serve as a sub-prefect.

sentences.zh: 會南巡，克開署江寧府，迎駕，授江西九江知府，尋擢浙江糧儲道。

translations.literal: During the southern tour, Kekai acted as prefect of Jiangning to receive the imperial carriage; he was appointed prefect of Jiujiang in Jiangxi and soon promoted to grain intendant of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: During the southern tour, Kekai served as acting prefect of Jiangning to receive the imperial carriage; he was then appointed prefect of Jiujiang in Jiangxi and soon promoted to grain intendant of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 時巡撫王亶望貪黷，屬吏多重徵以奉上官。

translations.literal: At the time Governor Wang Tanwang was corrupt; subordinates heavily levied taxes to court superiors.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Governor Wang Tanwang was venal; subordinates levied heavy taxes to curry favor with their superiors.

sentences.zh: 克開至，誓不取一錢，請於巡撫，約與之同心。

translations.literal: When Kekai arrived, he swore to take not a single coin and asked the governor to pledge they would act in concert.
translations.idiomatic: When Kekai arrived, he swore to take not a single coin and asked the governor to pledge that they would work in concert.

sentences.zh: 亶望姑應之，心厭克開，乃奏克開才優，請移治海塘，於是調杭嘉湖道。

translations.literal: Tanwang assented for the moment but loathed Kekai; he memorialized that Kekai's talent was outstanding and asked to transfer him to manage sea dikes — so Kekai was moved to Hang-Jia-Hu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Tanwang assented for the moment but inwardly detested Kekai; he memorialized that Kekai's talent was outstanding and asked to transfer him to manage sea dikes — and so Kekai was moved to Hang-Jia-Hu Circuit.

sentences.zh: 會改建海岸石塘，總督欲徙柴塘近數百丈以避潮，克開曰：「海與河異，讓之則潮必益侵，無益也。

translations.literal: When stone seawalls were being rebuilt, the governor-general wanted to shift the brushwood revetment several hundred zhang closer to avoid the tide. Kekai said: "The sea differs from a river — yield to it and the tide will surely encroach further; there is no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: When stone seawalls were being rebuilt, the governor-general wanted to shift the brushwood revetment several hundred zhang landward to avoid the tide. Kekai said: "The sea is not a river — yield to it and the tide will only advance further; there is no benefit in this."

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: And the plan was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 年餘，以督工勞瘁卒。

translations.literal: A little over a year later, he died of exhaustion from overseeing the works.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later, he died of exhaustion from supervising the construction.

sentences.zh: 克開在寧朔治水績最著，生平治獄多平反。

translations.literal: Kekai's water-control achievements at Ningshuo were most notable; in his life he reversed many wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: Kekai's water-control achievements at Ningshuo were his most notable; throughout his life he reversed many wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 禮儒士，嘗以私錢興書院。

translations.literal: He honored scholars and once funded an academy from his own purse.
translations.idiomatic: He honored scholars and once founded an academy with his own money.

sentences.zh: 歿無餘貲，天下稱清吏。

translations.literal: He died without surplus wealth; all under Heaven called him an upright official.
translations.idiomatic: He died without surplus wealth, and all under Heaven called him an upright official.

sentences.zh: 當時守令以興水利著者，又有鄭基、康基淵、言如泗，後有周際華。

translations.literal: Among magistrates and prefects then famed for promoting waterworks were also Zheng Ji, Kang Jiyuan, and Yan Rusi; later came Zhou Jihua.
translations.idiomatic: Among the magistrates and prefects then famed for promoting waterworks were also Zheng Ji, Kang Jiyuan, and Yan Rusi; later came Zhou Jihua.

sentences.zh: 基，字築平，廣東香山人。

translations.literal: Ji, courtesy name Zhuping, was from Xiangshan in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, courtesy name Zhuping, was from Xiangshan in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 以諸生入貲為知縣。

translations.literal: As a licentiate he purchased appointment as magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: As a licentiate he purchased appointment as magistrate.

sentences.zh: 乾隆間銓授安徽鳳臺縣，東鄉有通川三：曰黑濠，曰濕泥，曰裔溝。

translations.literal: During Qianlong he was assigned to Fengtai in Anhui. In the eastern township were three connecting streams: Heihao, Shini, and Yigou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianlong reign he was assigned to Fengtai in Anhui. In the eastern township were three connecting streams: Heihao, Shini, and Yigou.

sentences.zh: 匯潁上、蒙城諸縣水以達淮，歲久盡湮，秋潦輒成巨浸。

translations.literal: They gathered waters from Yingshang, Mengcheng, and other counties to reach the Huai; over years they silted up entirely, and autumn floods became vast inundations.
translations.idiomatic: They gathered waters from Yingshang, Mengcheng, and other counties to reach the Huai; over the years they silted up completely, and autumn floods became vast inundations.

sentences.zh: 侍郎裘曰修奉使治淮、潁諸水，獨不及鳳臺。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Qiu Yuexiu was commissioned to manage the Huai and Ying waters but did not reach Fengtai.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Qiu Yuexiu was commissioned to manage the Huai and Ying waters but did not extend his work to Fengtai.

sentences.zh: 基具牘陳利害及工事甚悉，曰修允其請。

translations.literal: Ji submitted a detailed petition on benefits, harms, and the works; Qiu Yuexiu granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: Ji submitted a detailed petition on the benefits, harms, and engineering involved; Qiu Yuexiu granted his request.

sentences.zh: 基察土宜，穿故渠，三河交暢。

translations.literal: Ji studied soil conditions, reopened old channels, and the three streams flowed freely.
translations.idiomatic: Ji studied local soil conditions, reopened the old channels, and the three streams flowed freely once more.

sentences.zh: 釃上游諸水以通淮流，不逾時工成。

translations.literal: He diverted upstream waters to connect with the Huai; the work was finished in no time.
translations.idiomatic: He diverted upstream waters to connect with the Huai current, and the work was finished in no time.

sentences.zh: 魯松灣地遠淮而卑，頻患潦，捐俸倡築堤障，遂成膏腴。

translations.literal: Lusong Bay was far from the Huai and low-lying, often suffering floods; he donated his salary to lead dike construction, and the land became fertile.
translations.idiomatic: Lusong Bay lay far from the Huai and low in elevation, often suffering floods; he donated his salary to lead dike construction, and the land became fertile.

sentences.zh: 調定遠，舉卓異，擢壽州知州。

translations.literal: Transferred to Dingyuan, cited for outstanding merit, promoted to magistrate of Shouzhou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Dingyuan, cited for outstanding merit, he was promoted to magistrate of Shouzhou Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 安豐塘，古芍陂也。

translations.literal: Anfeng Pond was the ancient Quepi Reservoir.
translations.idiomatic: Anfeng Pond was the ancient Quepi Reservoir.

sentences.zh: 塘圮，基審覈舊制，繕復之，為水門三十六，為閘六，為橋一。

translations.literal: The pond had collapsed; Ji verified the old design and restored it — thirty-six water gates, six sluice gates, and one bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The pond had collapsed; Ji verified the old design and restored it — thirty-six water gates, six sluice gates, and one bridge.

sentences.zh: 其旁則為堨、為堰、為圩，啟閉以時，汙萊盡闢。

translations.literal: Alongside were embankments, weirs, and polders, opened and closed on schedule; marsh and wasteland were fully reclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Alongside were embankments, weirs, and polders, opened and closed on schedule; marsh and wasteland were fully reclaimed.

sentences.zh: 嘗循行阡陌，見沙地磽確多不治，教民種薯蕷，佐菽麥，俾無曠土。

translations.literal: Once walking the fields, he saw sandy barren land largely uncultivated; he taught the people to plant sweet potatoes alongside beans and wheat so no land lay idle.
translations.idiomatic: Walking the fields one day, he saw sandy barren land largely left uncultivated; he taught the people to plant sweet potatoes alongside beans and wheat so that no land lay idle.

sentences.zh: 壽州不知蠶織，而地多椿樗，可飼蠶。

translations.literal: Shouzhou had no tradition of sericulture, but the land had many ailanthus and chinaberry trees suitable for feeding silkworms.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhou had no tradition of sericulture, but the land had many ailanthus and chinaberry trees suitable for feeding silkworms.

sentences.zh: 購蠶種，教民飼之，農桑並興。

translations.literal: He bought silkworm eggs and taught the people to raise them; agriculture and sericulture flourished together.
translations.idiomatic: He purchased silkworm eggs and taught the people to raise them; agriculture and sericulture flourished together.

sentences.zh: 其後遇旱，獨鳳臺、壽州秋成稔於他縣，以水利修也。

translations.literal: Later, during drought, Fengtai and Shouzhou alone had autumn harvests richer than other counties — because waterworks had been kept in repair.
translations.idiomatic: Later, during drought, Fengtai and Shouzhou alone enjoyed autumn harvests richer than other counties — because their waterworks had been kept in repair.

sentences.zh: 遷泗州直隸州知州。

translations.literal: Transferred to magistrate of Sizhou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Sizhou Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 賑水災，飢而不害。

translations.literal: He relieved flood disasters; though hungry, the people were not ruined.
translations.idiomatic: He relieved flood disasters; though the people went hungry, they were not ruined.

sentences.zh: 擢江蘇淮安知府，淮安為眾水所聚，於城東濬澗市河，於北開漁濱山字河，於西開護城河，壅滯悉通，民便之。

translations.literal: Promoted to prefect of Huai'an in Jiangsu. Huai'an gathers many waters; he dredged the Jianshi River east of the city, opened the Yubin Shanzi River to the north and a moat to the west — all stagnation cleared, to the people's convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to prefect of Huai'an in Jiangsu, he found a city where many waters converged; he dredged the Jianshi River east of the city, opened the Yubin Shanzi River to the north and a moat to the west — clearing every blockage to the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 基博覽前史，於河渠水利圖經，丹鉛殆遍，施行輒有成效。

translations.literal: Ji read widely in earlier histories and annotated nearly every map and classic on rivers and water control; whenever he put plans into action, they succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Ji read widely in earlier histories and annotated nearly every map and classic on rivers and water control; whenever he put a plan into action, it succeeded.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十一年，擢江南守巡道，命甫下而卒。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Qianlong, promoted to Jiangnan circuit intendant; the appointment had barely been issued when he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year of Qianlong he was promoted to Jiangnan circuit intendant, but the appointment had barely been issued when he died.

sentences.zh: 基淵，字靜溪，山西興縣人。

translations.literal: Jiyuan, courtesy name Jingxi, was from Xing County in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan, courtesy name Jingxi, was from Xing County in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十七年進士，歸班銓授河南嵩縣知縣。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the seventeenth year of Qianlong; after returning to the roster, assigned magistrate of Song County in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the seventeenth year of Qianlong (1752) and, after returning to the roster, was assigned magistrate of Song County in Henan.

sentences.zh: 舊傍伊水有渠十一，久湮絕。

translations.literal: Formerly eleven canals lay beside the Yi River; long obliterated.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly eleven canals lay beside the Yi River, but they had long been obliterated.

sentences.zh: 基淵按行舊址，勸民修復。

translations.literal: Jiyuan toured the old sites and urged the people to restore them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan toured the old sites and urged the people to restore them.

sentences.zh: 山澗諸流可引溉者，皆為開渠。

translations.literal: For all mountain streams that could be diverted for irrigation, he opened channels.
translations.idiomatic: Every mountain stream that could be put to use for irrigation, he turned into a channel.

sentences.zh: 渠身高下不一者，分段設閘以蓄洩之。

translations.literal: Where channel beds rose and fell at different levels, he installed sluice gates in sections to store and release water.
translations.idiomatic: Where the channels ran at uneven heights, he divided them into sections and fitted each with sluice gates to hold or release the water as needed.

sentences.zh: 田高渠下者，則教為水車引溉。

translations.literal: For fields higher than the channels, he taught people to use water wheels to draw irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: For land that stood above the waterline, he taught the farmers to lift water with wheels for irrigation.

sentences.zh: 凡開新、舊渠十八，灌田六萬二千餘畝。

translations.literal: In all he opened eighteen new and old channels, irrigating more than sixty-two thousand mu of fields.
translations.idiomatic: Altogether he opened eighteen channels, old and new, watering more than sixty-two thousand mu of farmland.

sentences.zh: 巡撫上其事，優詔議敘，尋以憂去。

translations.literal: The provincial governor reported his achievements; an edict commended him and considered promotion; soon afterward he left office to observe mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial governor memorialized his work; the throne responded with a commendatory edict and consideration for promotion. Before long he left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，授甘肅鎮原，調皋蘭，擢肅州直隸州知州。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed to Zhenyuan in Gansu, transferred to Gaolan, and promoted to magistrate of Suzhou Directly Governed Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, he was posted to Zhenyuan in Gansu, then transferred to Gaolan and promoted to magistrate of Suzhou Directly Governed Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 洪水渠岸峻易崩，基淵度勢於南石岡引鑿渠口，以避衝陷之害。

translations.literal: The banks of the Hongshui Channel were steep and prone to collapse; Jiyuan surveyed the terrain and cut the channel mouth at South Stone Ridge to avoid damage from flooding.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongshui Channel had steep banks that collapsed easily. Jiyuan read the lay of the land and cut the intake at South Stone Ridge so the current would not smash the works.

sentences.zh: 野豬溝有荒田，無水久廢。

translations.literal: There was abandoned farmland in Wild Boar Ditch that had long lain fallow for lack of water.
translations.idiomatic: Wild Boar Ditch held abandoned fields that had lain waste for years without water.

sentences.zh: 基淵詢訪耆舊，加寬柳樹閘龍口，別開子渠。

translations.literal: Jiyuan consulted the elders, widened the sluice mouth at Willow Tree Gate, and opened a subsidiary channel.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan questioned the old residents, widened the sluice at Willow Tree Gate, and cut a branch channel.

sentences.zh: 界荒田為七區，招民佃種，區取租十二石，給各社學，名曰新文渠。

translations.literal: He divided the abandoned land into seven districts, recruited tenants to farm it, collected twelve shi of rent from each district for the community schools, and named the project the Xinwen Channel.
translations.idiomatic: He parceled the wasteland into seven districts, brought in tenant farmers, set the rent from each district at twelve shi for the community schools, and called the new works the Xinwen Channel.

sentences.zh: 州東南九家窯，鑿山後渠開屯田，​​舊駐州判主之，久之田益薄瘠，民租入不足支官役；

translations.literal: At Jiujia Yao southeast of the prefecture, a channel was cut through the mountain to open military colonies; a deputy prefect had long been stationed there to oversee it, but over time the land grew thinner and poorer, and civilian rent could not cover official expenses;
translations.idiomatic: Southeast of the prefectural seat at Jiujia Yao, a channel had been cut through the hills to open military colonies, with a deputy prefect long stationed to supervise them. In time the soil grew thin and barren, and the tenants' rent no longer covered official costs;

sentences.zh: 基淵請汰州判，改屯昇科，為籌歲修費，民於是有恆產。

translations.literal: Jiyuan petitioned to abolish the deputy prefect's post, converted the colony lands to taxable civilian fields, and raised funds for annual repairs, so the people at last had secure holdings.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan petitioned to abolish the deputy prefecture, converted the colony fields to regular taxable land, and set aside funds for yearly upkeep, so the people at last had land they could count on.

sentences.zh: 基淵治官事如家事，博求利病。

translations.literal: Jiyuan handled official business as though it were family affairs, and broadly sought out what harmed or benefited the people.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan ran public affairs as he would his own household, and looked everywhere for what hurt the people and what might help them.

sentences.zh: 在嵩縣，植桑教蠶，出絲甲於他邑。

translations.literal: In Song County he planted mulberry and taught sericulture; the silk produced there ranked first among neighboring districts.
translations.idiomatic: At Song County he planted mulberry and taught sericulture; the silk it produced outranked that of every neighboring district.

sentences.zh: 以無業之地，建社學三十二所。

translations.literal: On unused land he built thirty-two community schools.
translations.idiomatic: On idle ground he erected thirty-two community schools.

sentences.zh: 在肅州，開郊外廢灘，種楊十餘萬株。

translations.literal: In Suzhou he reclaimed abandoned shoals outside the city and planted more than a hundred thousand poplar trees.
translations.idiomatic: At Suzhou he reclaimed derelict flats beyond the city walls and planted more than a hundred thousand poplars.

sentences.zh: 遍諭鄉堡種樹，薪樵取給，建社學二十一所。

translations.literal: He urged every township and fort to plant trees so firewood would be locally available, and built twenty-one community schools.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed every township and stockade to plant trees so fuel would be close at hand, and founded twenty-one community schools.

sentences.zh: 又於金佛、清水兩鄉建倉，以免徵糧借囤民房之累。

translations.literal: He also built granaries in Jin Fo and Qingshui townships so grain levies would not have to be stored in private homes.
translations.idiomatic: He also built granaries in the townships of Jin Fo and Qingshui, sparing the people the burden of storing tax grain in their own houses.

sentences.zh: 革番、民採買需索，皆有實惠。

translations.literal: He reformed the exactions imposed on Tibetans and Han when purchasing supplies, to the real benefit of all.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the squeeze placed on Tibetans and Han alike when government purchases were made, and the people felt a genuine benefit.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，擢江西廣信知府，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Qianlong, he was promoted to prefect of Guangxin in Jiangxi and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year of Qianlong (1779), he was promoted to prefect of Guangxin in Jiangxi and died still in post.

sentences.zh: 如泗，字素園，江蘇昭文人，言子七十五世孫。

translations.literal: Rusi, courtesy name Suyuan, was a native of Zhaowen in Jiangsu and a seventy-fifth-generation descendant of Yanzi.
translations.idiomatic: Rusi, styled Suyuan, came from Zhaowen in Jiangsu and was a seventy-fifth-generation descendant of Master Yan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年，高宗臨雍，如泗以賢裔陪祀，賜恩貢生，充正黃旗官學教習。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianlong, when the Gaozong Emperor lectured at the Imperial Academy, Rusi attended the sacrificial ceremony as a worthy descendant of a sage; he was granted status as a tribute student by imperial favor and served as instructor at the Banner School of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qianlong (1738), when the Gaozong Emperor lectured at the Imperial Academy, Rusi took part in the sacrifice as a worthy descendant of a sage. He was granted status as an En tribute student and served as instructor at the Banner School of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 十四年，銓授山西垣曲知縣，城濱黃河，修石堤以捍水。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he received appointment as magistrate of Yuanqu in Shanxi; the county seat lay on the Yellow River, and he built stone embankments to hold back the water.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Qianlong (1749), he was appointed magistrate of Yuanqu in Shanxi. The county seat stood on the Yellow River, and he built stone dikes to hold the flood back.

sentences.zh: 亳河故有數渠，复於上游濬之，分以溉田，民稱「言公渠」。

translations.literal: The Bo River had once had several channels; he dredged them again upstream and divided the water to irrigate fields, and the people called the project "Lord Yan's Canal."
translations.idiomatic: The Bo River had once had several irrigation channels. He dredged them again upstream and split the flow to water the fields, and the people called the work "Lord Yan's Canal."

sentences.zh: 調聞喜，涑水湍急，舊渠多圮，別濬新渠，食其利者五村。

translations.literal: Transferred to Wenxi, he found the Suishui River swift and many old channels ruined; he cleared a new channel, and five villages reaped the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Wenxi, he found the Suishui swift and the old channels mostly in ruins. He cut a new channel, and five villages shared the benefit.

sentences.zh: 舉卓異，擢保德直隸州知州。

translations.literal: Rated outstanding in performance, he was promoted to magistrate of Baode Directly Governed Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Rated outstanding in his evaluations, he was promoted to magistrate of Baode Directly Governed Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 新疆軍興，徵調過境，值歉歲，如泗經畫曲當，民無所累。

translations.literal: When military operations began in Xinjiang and requisitions passed through his district during a famine year, Rusi arranged everything fittingly and the people suffered no undue burden.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xinjiang campaign began and requisitioned troops passed through during a bad harvest, Rusi managed the arrangements so carefully that the people were not crushed by the burden.

sentences.zh: 陝西巡撫明德聞其能而薦之，乞養歸。

translations.literal: Shaanxi provincial governor Mingde heard of his ability and recommended him, but Rusi requested leave to care for his parents and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Governor Mingde of Shaanxi heard of his talents and recommended him, but Rusi asked leave to nurse his parents and went home.

sentences.zh: 父喪除，補解州。

translations.literal: After his father's mourning ended, he was assigned to Xiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning for his father was complete, he was posted to Xiezhou.

sentences.zh: 白沙河在城南，地如建瓴，南決則害鹽池，北決則壞城。

translations.literal: The Baisha River lay south of the city on land steep as a tilted jar; if it burst south it would ruin the salt pans, and if north it would destroy the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: The Baisha River ran south of the city across ground steep as a tilted water jar: a breach to the south would wreck the salt pans, and one to the north would ruin the walls.

sentences.zh: 如泗請於大吏，用鹽帑修築兩岸石堰，長五里。

translations.literal: Rusi petitioned his superiors to use salt revenue to build stone dikes on both banks, five li in length.
translations.idiomatic: Rusi petitioned his superiors to spend salt revenue on stone dikes along both banks, five li long.

sentences.zh: 又姚暹渠本以護鹽池，民田不能灌溉。

translations.literal: The Yao Xian Canal had originally been built to protect the salt pans, so civilian fields could not be irrigated.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao Xian Canal had been built chiefly to shield the salt pans, so the people's fields could not be watered from it.

sentences.zh: 故事，商民分修，商盡諉之於民，力爭，乃仍舊貫。

translations.literal: By custom merchants and civilians were to share repairs, but the merchants shifted all responsibility onto the people; Rusi fought hard on the issue until the old arrangement was restored.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent merchants and commoners were to share upkeep, but the merchants tried to push the whole burden onto the people. Rusi fought the matter through until the old practice was restored.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，擢湖北襄陽知府。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, he was promoted to prefect of Xiangyang in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of Qianlong (1764), he was promoted to prefect of Xiangyang in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 如泗愛士恤民而治盜嚴，在解州，民間夜不閉戶。

translations.literal: Rusi cherished scholars and cared for the people while treating banditry with severity; in Xiezhou people did not lock their doors at night.
translations.idiomatic: Rusi loved scholars, cared for the people, and dealt harshly with thieves. At Xiezhou people left their doors unbolted at night.

sentences.zh: 襄陽素為盜藪，聞其至，盜皆遠遁。

translations.literal: Xiangyang had long been a thieves' nest, but when word came of his arrival the bandits all fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang had long been a robbers' den, but when word spread that he was coming, the outlaws fled far away.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，因失察屬員罷職。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, he was dismissed for failing to supervise a subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year of Qianlong (1769), he was dismissed for lax supervision of a subordinate.

sentences.zh: 尋以皇太后萬壽祝嘏復原官，遂不出。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was restored to his former rank on the occasion of the empress dowager's birthday celebration, but he never returned to office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was restored to rank on the empress dowager's birthday celebration, but he never took office again.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十一年，卒於家，年九十一。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jiaqing, he died at home at the age of ninety-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Jiaqing (1806), he died at home at the age of ninety-one.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，祀名宦。

translations.literal: During the Guangxu reign he was enshrined among distinguished officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangxu reign he was entered in the shrine of distinguished officials.

sentences.zh: 際華，字石籓，貴州貴築人。

translations.literal: Jihua, courtesy name Shifan, was a native of Guizhu in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jihua, styled Shifan, was from Guizhu in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶六年進士，授內閣中書，親老乞改教職。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the sixth year of Jiaqing, he was appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat; when his parents grew old he requested transfer to an educational post.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Jiaqing (1801) and was appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat. When his parents aged, he asked to be moved to an educational post.

sentences.zh: 歷遵義、都勻兩府教授，以薦擢知縣。

translations.literal: He served in succession as director of studies in Zunyi and Duyun prefectures, and on recommendation was promoted to magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as director of studies in Zunyi and Duyun, and on recommendation was promoted to magistrate.

sentences.zh: 道光六年，授河南輝縣。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daoguang, he was appointed to Huixian in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Daoguang (1826), he was appointed magistrate of Huixian in Henan.

sentences.zh: 百泉出縣北蘇門山，衛河之源也。

translations.literal: The Hundred Springs issue from Sumen Mountain north of the county and are the source of the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: The Hundred Springs rise from Sumen Mountain north of the county and are the source of the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 其西諸山水經縣南入衛，曰峪河；

translations.literal: The streams and rivers to the west pass south of the county and enter the Wei — this is the Yu River;
translations.idiomatic: The streams and rivers to the west run south of the county into the Wei; this is the Yu River.

sentences.zh: 其北諸澗水歷縣東入新河，曰東石河。

translations.literal: The ravine waters to the north run east of the county into the Xin River — this is the East Stone River.
translations.idiomatic: The ravine waters to the north flow east of the county into the Xin River; this is the East Stone River.

sentences.zh: 新河者，自縣北鑿渠引衛河，至縣南復入衛，又稱玉帶河，皆資疏洩、利灌溉。

translations.literal: The Xin River was a channel cut north of the county to draw water from the Wei, returning to the Wei south of the county; it was also called the Jade Belt River, and all these waterways served both drainage and irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: The Xin River was a canal cut north of the county to draw from the Wei and return to it south of the seat; it was also called the Jade Belt River. All these channels served both drainage and irrigation.

sentences.zh: 時並淤塞，遇水輒苦漂溺。

translations.literal: At the time they were all silted up, and whenever rain came the people suffered flooding.
translations.idiomatic: By then they were all choked with silt, and whenever the rains came the people were drowned in flood.

sentences.zh: 際華履視溝、渠，出俸錢率民醵貲濬峪河，修紅石堰，疏新河。

translations.literal: Jihua walked the ditches and channels himself, contributed his salary and led the people in raising funds to dredge the Yu River, repair the Red Stone Weir, and clear the Xin River.
translations.idiomatic: Jihua inspected the ditches and channels on foot, spent his own salary, and led the people in raising funds to dredge the Yu River, repair the Red Stone Weir, and open the Xin River.

sentences.zh: 鑿東石河六十餘丈，堅築其岸。

translations.literal: He cut more than sixty zhang from the East Stone River and solidly reinforced its banks.
translations.idiomatic: He cut more than sixty zhang from the East Stone River and firmly rebuilt its banks.

sentences.zh: 諸渠綺交脈注，潦患以息。

translations.literal: The channels interlaced like brocade and flowed into one another, and flood disasters ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The channels crisscrossed and fed one another like woven silk, and the flood trouble ended.

sentences.zh: 課民種桑四萬株，教之育蠶，他樹亦十五萬株，於是邑有絲絮、材木之利。

translations.literal: He ordered the people to plant forty thousand mulberry trees and taught them sericulture; other trees numbered a hundred and fifty thousand as well, and the district thereafter enjoyed profit from silk floss and timber.
translations.idiomatic: He set the people to planting forty thousand mulberry trees and taught them to raise silkworms; other trees numbered a hundred and fifty thousand besides. The district thereafter profited from silk and timber.

sentences.zh: 蘇門故多名賢祠宇，咸新之，修明祀事，以勵風教焉。

translations.literal: Sumen had long held shrines to many worthy men; he renewed them all, restored proper sacrifices, and thereby encouraged moral instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Sumen had long held shrines to many worthies; he restored them all, put the sacrifices in good order, and thereby upheld local moral teaching.

sentences.zh: 署陝州直隸州知州。

translations.literal: He served as acting magistrate of Shanzhou Directly Governed Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting magistrate of Shanzhou Directly Governed Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 自澠池入陝，道硤石五十餘裡，險惡為行旅所苦。

translations.literal: From Mianchi into the pass, the road through Xia Gorge ran more than fifty li — treacherous and a torment to travelers.
translations.idiomatic: From Mianchi into the pass, the route through Xia Gorge ran more than fifty li — steep, cruel, and a misery to travelers.

sentences.zh: 際華別開平道，往來者便之。

translations.literal: Jihua opened a level route, to the convenience of all who passed back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: Jihua cut a level road, and those who traveled back and forth found the way easier.

sentences.zh: 迴避，改授江蘇興化縣。

translations.literal: On a conflict-of-interest ruling he was reassigned as magistrate of Xinghua in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Recused on a conflict-of-interest ruling, he was reassigned as magistrate of Xinghua in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 當裡下河之下游，水患尤急。

translations.literal: It lay at the lower reaches of the Lixia River region, where flood peril was especially acute.
translations.idiomatic: The county stood at the lower end of the Lixia River country, where flood danger was especially severe.

sentences.zh: 際華議開攔江壩以洩湖、河之水，鹽官及商皆力爭，以為壩開則水南下溜急，於鹽舟牽挽不便。

translations.literal: Jihua proposed opening a river-blocking dam to release lake and river water; salt officials and merchants all fought the plan, arguing that if the dam opened the water would rush south too swiftly and make towing salt barges difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Jihua proposed opening a river-blocking dam to drain lake and river water. Salt officials and merchants fought the plan, saying that if the dam opened the current would race south and make towing salt boats harder.

sentences.zh: 際華曰：「彼所爭者，十四里牽挽之勞，以較揚州東七縣田廬場灶之漂溺，蠲免賑恤之煩費，輕重何如？

translations.literal: Jihua said: "What they dispute is the labor of towing for fourteen li — compared with the fields, houses, salt pans, and hearths drowned across the seven eastern counties of Yangzhou, and the trouble and expense of tax remissions and famine relief — how do the scales weigh?"
translations.idiomatic: Jihua said: "They are quarreling over fourteen li of towing — set that against the drowned fields, homes, salt pans, and hearths across the seven eastern counties of Yangzhou, and against the cost and trouble of remissions and relief. Which weighs more?"

sentences.zh: 」總督林則徐韙其議。

translations.literal: Governor-General Lin Zexu approved his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Lin Zexu endorsed his plan.

sentences.zh: 調江都，兼署泰州，毀淫祠百餘區，改為義學。

translations.literal: Transferred to Jiangdu, he also served concurrently as acting magistrate of Taizhou; he demolished more than a hundred improper shrines and converted them into charity schools.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Jiangdu, he also served concurrently as acting magistrate of Taizhou. He tore down more than a hundred improper shrines and turned them into charity schools.

sentences.zh: 則徐疏薦之，尋告歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: Lin Zexu memorialized recommending him; soon Jihua requested retirement and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zexu memorialized recommending him. Before long Jihua asked to retire and died at home.

sentences.zh: 先是輝縣及興化民皆不習織，際華輒自出貲置織器教之，轉相授，於是二縣有衣被販貿之利，至今賴之。

translations.literal: Earlier the people of Huixian and Xinghua had not known weaving; Jihua repeatedly spent his own money to provide looms and teach them, and the skill passed from hand to hand until both counties enjoyed profit in cloth and trade — a benefit they rely on to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the people of Huixian and Xinghua did not know how to weave. Jihua again and again paid out of his own purse for looms and taught them the craft; the skill passed from hand to hand until both counties profited in cloth and trade — a benefit they still rely on today.

sentences.zh: 輝縣請祀名宦祠。

translations.literal: Huixian petitioned to enshrine him in the shrine of distinguished officials.
translations.idiomatic: Huixian petitioned to honor him in the shrine of distinguished officials.

sentences.zh: =汪輝祖=汪輝祖，字龍莊，浙江蕭山人。

translations.literal: Wang Huizu. Wang Huizu, courtesy name Longzhuang, was a native of Xiaoshan in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huizu. Wang Huizu, styled Longzhuang, was from Xiaoshan in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 少孤，繼母王、生母徐教之成立。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he was raised to maturity by his stepmother, née Wang, and his birth mother, née Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned while still young, he was brought up by his stepmother, Lady Wang, and his birth mother, Lady Xu.

sentences.zh: 習法家言，佐州縣幕，持正不阿，為時所稱。

translations.literal: He studied legalist doctrine, served as adviser in prefectural and county yamens, stood upright without bending, and was praised by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: He studied legal practice, served as adviser in prefectural and county offices, stood straight and would not bend, and won praise in his day.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十一年成進士，授湖南寧遠知縣。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the twenty-first year of Qianlong, he was appointed magistrate of Ningyuan in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-first year of Qianlong (1756) and was appointed magistrate of Ningyuan in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 縣雜瑤俗，積逋而多訟，前令被訐去，黠桀益肆挾持；

translations.literal: The county was mixed with Yao customs, carried heavy tax arrears, and had much litigation; the previous magistrate had been impeached and driven off, and crafty ruffians grew bolder in holding others hostage;
translations.idiomatic: The county was mixed with Yao custom, burdened with tax arrears, and rife with lawsuits. The previous magistrate had been impeached and driven out, and cunning ruffians grew bolder in bullying others;

sentences.zh: 又流丐多強橫。

translations.literal: Moreover many itinerant beggars were brutish and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: and many wandering beggars were violent and overbearing besides.

sentences.zh: 輝祖下車，即捕其尤，驅餘黨出境。

translations.literal: As soon as Huizu took office he arrested the worst offenders and drove the rest out of the district.
translations.idiomatic: The moment Huizu took office he seized the worst offenders and drove the rest from the district.

sentences.zh: 民納賦不及期，手書諭之曰：「官民一體，聽訟責在官，完賦責在民。

translations.literal: When the people failed to pay taxes on time, he wrote them a personal notice: "Officials and people are one body: hearing cases is the official's responsibility, paying taxes the people's.
translations.idiomatic: When the people fell behind on taxes, he wrote them a personal notice: "Official and subject are one body. Hearing cases is the official's duty; paying taxes is the people's.

sentences.zh: 官不勤職，咎有難辭；

translations.literal: If officials neglect their duties, blame is hard to escape;
translations.idiomatic: If an official neglects his post, he can hardly escape blame;

sentences.zh: 民不奉公，法所不恕。

translations.literal: if the people refuse public obligation, the law will not spare them.
translations.idiomatic: if the people refuse their public duty, the law will not pardon them.

sentences.zh: 今約每旬以七日聽訟，二日較賦，一日手辦詳。

translations.literal: From now on I set each ten-day period thus: seven days for hearing cases, two for comparing tax records, one for drafting memorials by hand.
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter each ten-day period will be divided thus: seven days for hearing cases, two for comparing tax rolls, one for drafting reports by hand.

sentences.zh: 較賦之日亦兼聽訟。

translations.literal: On tax-comparison days I shall also hear cases.
translations.idiomatic: On tax-comparison days I shall hear cases as well.

sentences.zh: 若民皆遵期完課，則少費較賦之精力，即多聽訟之功夫。

translations.literal: If all pay on schedule, I shall spend less strength on tax comparison and devote more effort to hearing cases.
translations.idiomatic: If everyone pays on time, I shall spend less effort on comparison and more on hearing cases.

sentences.zh: 」民感其誠，不踰月而賦額足。

translations.literal: The people were moved by his sincerity, and within a month the tax quota was full.
translations.idiomatic: The people were moved by his sincerity, and within a month the tax quota was met.

sentences.zh: 治事廉平，尤善色聽，援據比附，律窮者，通以經術，證以古事。

translations.literal: He governed with integrity and fairness, and was especially skilled at reading faces; when statutes ran out he cited precedents and analogies, and where the law reached its limit he appealed to the classics and proved his points with historical examples.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with integrity and fairness, and was especially skilled at reading men's faces. When the statutes ran dry he cited precedents and analogies; where the law reached its limit he appealed to the classics and proved his points with ancient examples.

sentences.zh: 據漢書趙廣漢傳鉤距法，斷縣民匡學義獄；

translations.literal: Drawing on the detective method of Zhao Guanghan in the Book of Han, he resolved the case of the county man Kuang Xueyi;
translations.idiomatic: Following the interrogation method of Zhao Guanghan in the Book of Han, he decided the case of the county man Kuang Xueyi;

sentences.zh: 據唐書劉蕡傳斷李、蕭兩氏爭先隴獄；

translations.literal: Drawing on the biography of Liu Zhen in the Book of Tang, he decided the dispute between the Li and Xiao clans over a ancestral tomb;
translations.idiomatic: following the biography of Liu Zhen in the Book of Tang, he decided the dispute between the Li and Xiao clans over precedence at an ancestral tomb;

sentences.zh: 判決皆曲當，而心每欿然。

translations.literal: Every judgment was apt, yet his heart was always heavy with regret.
translations.idiomatic: every judgment was just, yet his heart was always heavy.

sentences.zh: 遇匪人當予杖，輒呼之前曰：「律不可逭，然若父母膚體，奈何行不肖虧辱之？

translations.literal: When a wrongdoer was to be caned, he would call him forward and say: "The law cannot be evaded — yet this is your parents' flesh and blood; how can you bear to act unworthily and bring shame upon it?
translations.idiomatic: When a wrongdoer was to be flogged, he would call him forward and say: "The law cannot be escaped — yet this body is your parents' gift. How can you bear to act unworthily and disgrace it?

sentences.zh: 」再三語。

translations.literal: He would speak thus again and again.
translations.idiomatic: He would say this again and again.

sentences.zh: 罪人泣，亦泣。

translations.literal: The criminal wept, and he wept as well.
translations.idiomatic: The offender wept, and he wept with him.

sentences.zh: 或對簿者，反代請得免，卒改行為善良。

translations.literal: Sometimes litigants themselves pleaded for mercy on another's behalf; in the end the guilty changed their ways and became good citizens.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes those facing judgment pleaded on another's behalf to spare him punishment; in the end the guilty reformed and became decent men.

sentences.zh: 每決獄，縱民觀聽。

translations.literal: Whenever he rendered judgment he allowed the people to watch and listen.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he decided a case he let the people watch and listen.

sentences.zh: 又延紳耆問民疾苦、四鄉廣狹肥瘠、人情良莠，皆籍記之。

translations.literal: He also invited gentry elders to discuss the people's hardships, the breadth, narrowness, fertility, and barrenness of the four townships, and the good and bad in local character — recording all of it in registers.
translations.idiomatic: He also summoned gentry elders to discuss the people's hardships, the breadth, narrowness, fertility, and barrenness of the four townships, and the good and bad in local character, and recorded it all in registers.

sentences.zh: 寧遠例食淮鹽，直數倍於粵鹽，民食粵私，大吏遣營弁偵捕，輝祖白上官，以鹽愈禁則值愈增，私不可縱，而食淡可虞，請改淮引為粵引。

translations.literal: Ningyuan was nominally supplied with Huai salt at several times the price of Guangdong salt; the people ate smuggled Guangdong salt, and high officials sent military officers to spy and seize it. Huizu explained to his superiors that the tighter the salt prohibition the higher the price, that smuggling could not be indulged yet salt shortage was to be feared, and he requested changing Huai permits to Guangdong permits.
translations.idiomatic: Ningyuan was supposed to consume Huai salt at several times the price of Guangdong salt. The people ate smuggled Guangdong salt instead, and high officials sent military officers to spy and seize it. Huizu explained to his superiors that the tighter the prohibition the higher the price, that smuggling could not be winked at yet famine from salt shortage was to be feared, and asked that Huai permits be changed to Guangdong permits.

sentences.zh: 未及報，輝祖即張示：「鹽不及十斤者聽。

translations.literal: Before a reply came, Huizu posted a notice: "Salt in amounts under ten jin shall be permitted."
translations.idiomatic: Before an answer came back, Huizu posted a notice: "Salt in amounts under ten jin shall be allowed."

sentences.zh: 」偵弁謂其縱私，輝祖揭辨，總督畢沅嘉之，立弛零鹽禁，時偉其議。

translations.literal: The spy officers accused him of condoning smuggling; Huizu rebutted them in a public statement, and Governor-General Bi Yuan praised him, immediately relaxing the prohibition on retail salt — his proposal was admired at the time.
translations.idiomatic: The spy officers accused him of condoning smuggling. Huizu answered them in a public statement, and Governor-General Bi Yuan praised him and at once relaxed the ban on retail salt. People admired his proposal at the time.

sentences.zh: 兩署道州，又兼署新田縣，皆有惠政。

translations.literal: He twice served as acting prefect of Daozhou and also concurrently as acting magistrate of Xintian; everywhere he brought benevolent rule.
